commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Pass only the video count to get_num_frames_with_most_features
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`get_num_frames_with_most_features(seq_len, mm_counts)` received every modality's count, and eight models used it to subtract other modalities' tokens from the per-video frame budget. The per-item budget is checked one item at a time, so GLM-4.1V/4.5V, Ovis2.5, InternVL and Intern-S1 reject a video-only prompt that fits `max_model_len` with "exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size". As suggested in review, the method now takes only the video count, `get_num_frames_with_most_features(seq_len, num_videos)`, for all models, so a model can no longer subtract other modalities from it.

## Claims

- Every definition (19) and every caller now passes only the video count, so other modalities can no longer reduce the per-video budget.
- The per-item video budget now equals the profiled video dummy for GLM-4.1V/4.5V, Ovis2.5, InternVL and Intern-S1, and equals the video-only budget for ERNIE-4.5-VL.
- MiniCPM-V, MiniCPM-o (which also subtracted audio) and Nemotron Nano VL lose the same subtraction; their budgets do not change in the tested configurations (frame cap / budget set to `seq_len`).
- Every other model's budget and profiled dummy is identical to main (sweep below).
- Videos that fit the context are served instead of rejected. This is an admission fix; no latency or throughput change is claimed or measured. The whole-prompt check against `max_model_len` is unchanged.

## Validation

**Summary** (every number is in the raw output below):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Video budget, GLM-4.1V at 16384 / Ovis2.5 at 32768 / InternVL3 at 16384 / Intern-S1 at 16384 | 6,084 / 3,138 / 13,056 / 16,128 | 12,168 / 6,274 / 16,384 / 16,384 (= profiled dummy) |
| Video budget, ERNIE-4.5-VL at 16384 / 32768 | 6,084 / 24,336 | 12,168 / 30,420 (= video-only budget) |
| Video budget, MiniCPM-V-4.5 / MiniCPM-o-2.6 / Nemotron Nano 12B v2 VL at 32768 | 1,024 / 1,024 / 32,768 | 1,024 / 1,024 / 32,768 |
| InternVL3-1B, 14,336-token video | rejected: encoder cache 13056 | served |
| GLM-4.1V-9B, 10,240-token video | rejected: encoder cache 8192 | served |
| InternVL3-1B, 12,288-token video (fits both) | served | served, same text |
| KV cache tokens, InternVL3-1B / GLM-4.1V-9B | 2,957,312 / 405,504 | 2,957,312 / 407,552 |

## Details

- **Root cause:** `MultiModalBudget` asks `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item` (or the dummy inputs) for the per-item maximum with one item of every modality, and profiles each modality with a dummy of that modality alone (`get_dummy_encoder_profile_inputs` uses `{modality: 1}`). `get_num_frames_with_most_features` in eight models subtracted the maximum tokens of every image (and, in MiniCPM-o, every audio clip) from `seq_len`, so the admitted video budget was one image smaller than the video that profiling ran. The check in `InputProcessor` compares each item on its own against the encoder cache, so the image does not need to share it.
- **When it shows:** the encoder cache is `max(max_num_batched_tokens, largest per-item budget)`, so the rejection needs chunked prefill (the default) with `max_num_batched_tokens` below the video.
- **Profiling:** the profiled video is the same dummy on both sides. The number of copies is the encoder budget divided by the per-item budget, so with a larger per-item budget it stays the same or drops, depending on `max_num_batched_tokens`. For example, GLM-4.1V at 16384 with `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` profiles 1 copy instead of 2; on main, 2 copies of 12,168 tokens exceed the 16,384-token encoder budget. These counts are derived from `encoder_budget.py`; only the 8192 setting was run on GPU.
- **Validation limits:** serving was run for GLM-4.1V-9B and InternVL3-1B only, on one A100-40GB, at one setting, with synthetic frames. The other models were checked on CPU only.
- **ERNIE-4.5-VL:** its profiled video dummy is already far below its budget on main (5,780 vs. 24,336 at 32768) because its video processor resizes the frames. This PR raises the budget to 30,420. ERNIE already runs out of memory on admitted videos on main in the tested A100-80GB configurations (video-only, 16384 to 32768). The same 32768 request also runs out of memory with this PR. Its undersized profiling dummy is a separate fix.
- **Out-of-tree models:** an override of `get_num_frames_with_most_features` must take `num_videos` instead of `mm_counts` if it is called from in-tree code. The two overrides in vllm-project repos (vllm-omni MiniCPM-o 4.5, vllm-gaudi MiniMax-M3) define their own processing info on `BaseProcessingInfo` and only call their own method, so they are unaffected.
- **Not changed:** GLM-4.6V-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and GLM-OCR take the explicit `get_mm_max_tokens_per_item` path and are unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Exit on permanent engine failure
commits.pr_body:
## Overview


After the engine output dispatcher terminates, the Rust API server becomes
unhealthy but continues listening and returning failed responses indefinitely.

Monitor permanent LLM health failures, stop the HTTP and gRPC servers, complete
resource cleanup, and return an error so process managers can restart the
frontend.

This aligns the Rust frontend with the Python server behavior: exit on engine
failure by default while honoring `VLLM_KEEP_ALIVE_ON_ENGINE_DEATH`.



## Claims

- Exit with a nonzero status when the LLM becomes permanently unhealthy.
- Preserve graceful shutdown for normal termination signals.
- Honor `VLLM_KEEP_ALIVE_ON_ENGINE_DEATH=1`, keeping auxiliary endpoints
  available while reporting an unhealthy status.
- Publish gRPC `NOT_SERVING` before closing health watches and listeners.
- Preserve the engine failure when shutdown and health events arrive together.



## Validation

```bash
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server  -p vllm-cmd  --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked  -- -D warnings
```



## Details


The output dispatcher already publishes a permanent unhealthy state when it
receives an engine-death sentinel or encounters a fatal output error. The Rust
server previously used that state for health reporting only, so no component
initiated server shutdown.

A server-level health monitor now subscribes to the LLM health channel. On a
permanent failure, it waits for gRPC health withdrawal to be published, cancels
the shared server shutdown token, drains the server, and propagates the failure
after LLM cleanup.

The existing keep-alive environment variable bypasses failure-triggered
shutdown. No engine protocol or transport format is changed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Render tool-result media in the Inkling renderer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix `Inkling tool response content must be text, got a part of kind 'image'` when an Inkling tool result carries an image (for example a screenshot). The image stayed in the conversation history, so every later turn in that conversation failed the same way.

The Inkling renderer flattened tool-response content to a single text string. Coalesce adjacent text parts into one tool-response block so text-only results keep their previous framing, and emit one `<|content_image|>` / `<|content_audio_input|>` marker per media item for `InklingMultiModalProcessor`, which expands each marker into the per-patch placeholder run. Empty tool results still emit one empty text block so the answered tool call is not left dangling. A `thinking` part in a tool response raises a clear error instead of being rendered as tool content.

Ported from sgl-project/sglang#33898.

Duplicate-work check: no existing upstream PR covers this. The closest are #58793 (thinking content parts in the Inkling renderer) and #58823 (Anthropic tool-result images); both are different changes. Upstream `main` still has `_flatten_text_content` and the same failure.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_inkling.py -q
```

The new tests cover mixed text + image tool results, one marker per image, coalesced text parts around media, empty content, and audio. They fail before the renderer change with the existing `Inkling tool response content must be text` error and pass after it.

## Test Result

Before the fix, the new media tests fail; after:

```text
53 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files are clean.

## Notes

AI assistance was used in preparing this patch.

The defensive `thinking` guard matches the SGLang fix and becomes reachable once #58793 lands; this PR does not depend on that change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Restore MoE weight padding dropped by #46009
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Re-enables ROCm MoE weight padding (`VLLM_ROCM_MOE_PADDING`, on by default) for unquantized MoE on the TRITON path. It has been silently inactive since #46009. On Radeon Pro W7900 with GLM-4.7-Flash at concurrency 1, this restores 4.5–10.8 % output throughput and 10–13 % TTFT. Related: #46009, #46381 (earlier fix for this padding), #59332 and #62977 (padding tests).

## Test Plan

Commands used for every result below (exact options in the sections that follow):

```bash
# Unit tests (ROCm GPU, any arch; AITER tests need MI300+)
pytest -v tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py tests/rocm/test_moe_weight_replay.py

# End to end: server + concurrency-1 benchmark, once on main and once on this PR
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --port 8100
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --port 8100 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 1 --num-warmups 3 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el

# Controls: same commands on main with VLLM_ROCM_MOE_PADDING=0

# Accuracy (against the same server)
lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 0
# concurrency-1 run: num_concurrent=1 and --limit 250
```

## Claims

- **Bug fix:** expert weights on ROCm get their padded layout again after loading. On current `main` the padding is computed and then discarded.
- **Performance** (GLM-4.7-Flash, 4× W7900, concurrency 1): TP4 output tok/s **+4.5 %**, TTFT **−10.3 %**; TP2 output tok/s **+10.8 %**, TTFT **−12.9 %**.
- **No regression of #46009:** an in-place weight update (`process_weights_after_loading()` called again after CUDA graph capture) still keeps the expert weight storage addresses.
- **Tests:** new regression tests assert that the padded layout persists after loading and after a weight update. Both fail on `main`.
- **No accuracy change:** the MoE output is bitwise identical with and without padding. GSM8K generations at concurrency 1 are identical to `main` (250 / 250).

## Validation

### End-to-end

We observed lower concurrency-1 throughput and TTFT for GLM-4.7-Flash on W7900 with recent `main`, and traced it to #46009. We measured `main` (`e37e51dd2`) against the same build with this patch:
- Setup: bf16, `--max-model-len 4096`, random 1024 input / 256 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 20 prompts, 3 warm-ups, 3 cycles per configuration.
- TTFT is the mean of cycles 2–3 (cycle 1 includes one-off JIT warm-up). TPOT and tok/s are the mean of all 3 cycles.
- Run-to-run spread: TPOT was identical across cycles, and tok/s varied by ≤ 0.03 between cycles 2 and 3. There were no failed requests.

| GPUs | `--gpu-memory-utilization` | Build | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 (4× W7900) | 0.8 | `main` (mean of 2 runs) | 54.27 | 19.56 | 50.57 |
| TP4 (4× W7900) | 0.8 | **this PR** | **48.66** (−10.3 %) | **18.73** (−4.3 %) | **52.85** (+4.5 %) |
| TP2 (2× W7900) | 0.9 | `main` | 68.89 | 23.48 | 42.08 |
| TP2 (2× W7900) | 0.9 | **this PR** | **60.02** (−12.9 %) | **21.20** (−9.7 %) | **46.61** (+10.8 %) |

Controls that isolate the cause:
- `main` with `VLLM_ROCM_MOE_PADDING=0` performs the same as `main` (TP4: 50.52 tok/s, TPOT 19.58 ms), so the padding is already inactive on `main`.
- `main` with only the pre-#46009 line restored performs the same as this PR (TP4: 52.84 tok/s, TPOT 18.74 ms).
- A second `main` run at the end of the series matched the first (50.60 vs 50.54 tok/s).

TP2 uses 0.9 because, with the padding restored, it has no memory left for the KV cache at 0.8 (see *Trade-off*). Concurrency-1 results do not depend on KV cache size.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --port 8100

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --port 8100 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 1 --num-warmups 3 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

To check the layout after loading, look at `w13_weight.stride(-2)` on a MoE layer: on `main` it is `2048`; with this PR it is `2048 + 128` (bf16, 256 B padding).
</details>

### Unit tests (W7900 gfx1100; re-run on R9700 gfx1201 after merging current `main`)

```bash
pytest -v tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py tests/rocm/test_moe_weight_replay.py
```

| Test | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| new `test_triton_moe_padding_persists_after_loading[padding-on]` | **FAIL** (`stride 256 != 256 + 128`) | pass |
| new `test_triton_moe_padding_persists_after_loading[padding-off]` | pass | pass |
| new `test_triton_moe_padding_survives_weight_update` | **FAIL** | pass |
| existing `_maybe_pad_weight` tests (8, incl. #62977's EPLB and non-unit-stride guards) | pass | pass |
| #62977's `test_aiter_moe_padding_rl_reload_address_stable` | needs AITER MoE (MI300+); skipped on RDNA | skipped on RDNA |
| `test_moe_weight_replay.py[triton]` (CUDA graph capture, sleep/wake, weight reload, graph replay) | pass | pass |

On R9700 (gfx1201) with `main` at `87b804f09d`: `main` 3 failed / 10 passed / 2 skipped, this PR 1 failed / 12 passed / 2 skipped. The remaining failure, `test_moe_weight_replay.py[aiter]`, fails identically on `main`: AITER MoE is not available on gfx1201, so the backend is TRITON (`assert 'TRITON' == 'ROCm AITER'`).

The new tests select the TRITON backend explicitly, so they cover the same path in the existing ROCm CI job (`mi300_1` in `test-amd.yaml`). `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Accuracy (lm-eval GSM8K, 5-shot, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`)

Padding changes only the row stride, never the values. With identical inputs, the fused MoE output from padded weights is **bitwise identical** to the output from dense weights. We checked this at GLM-4.7-Flash TP4 shapes (64 experts, H = 2048, I = 384, top-4) for 1, 7, 64, 512 and 2048 tokens.

| Setting | `main` | this PR | Identical generations |
|---|---|---|---|
| Concurrency 1, first 250 questions | 0.844 ± 0.023 | **0.844 ± 0.023** | **250 / 250** |
| Concurrency 64, full set (2 runs each) | 0.8514, 0.8393 | 0.8355, 0.8355 | ~30 % between versions |

Scores are strict-match exact match; flexible-extract is within 0.001 of strict.

With no batching (concurrency 1), the outputs are identical. At concurrency 64, generations depend on batch composition, which depends on timing. The two `main` runs differ from each other by 1.2 points and share only 33 % of generations, partly because the first run was slowed by Triton JIT compilation. The two runs of this PR were identical to each other (100 %). The differences between versions at concurrency 64 therefore reflect scheduling, not numerics.

<details>
<summary>lm-eval command</summary>

```bash
lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8100/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 0
# concurrency-1 run: num_concurrent=1 and --limit 250
```
</details>

## Details

**What the padding does.** For eligible unquantized MoE weights (row size a multiple of 512 B), `_maybe_pad_weight` returns a view with the same shape and values but a 256 B larger row stride, backed by new storage (`F.pad(w, (0, n))[..., :-n]`). The fused MoE Triton kernel reads weights through their strides, so consecutive weight rows land on different DRAM channels instead of the same ones.

**Root cause.** The padding only takes effect if the parameter is pointed at the padded storage. #46009 changed

```python
layer.w13_weight.data = self._maybe_pad_weight(layer.w13_weight.data)
```

to

```python
layer.w13_weight.data.copy_(self._maybe_pad_weight(layer.w13_weight.data))
```

so that storage addresses stay stable for CUDA graphs during weight updates. However, `copy_` writes the values back into the original dense storage and discards the padded layout. `process_weights_after_loading()` also runs on the initial load, so the padding has been disabled for every model on this path. Values are unchanged, so accuracy tests and #46009's address-stability test cannot detect this. Only a stride check or a benchmark can.

**Fix.** `process_weights_after_loading()` points the parameter at the result of `_maybe_pad_weight()` again (`.data = ...` instead of `.data.copy_(...)`). `_maybe_pad_weight()` pads only on the initial load (`self.moe_kernel is None`), the same first-load / weight-update check `_setup_kernel()` already uses for `replace_parameter(..., prefer_copy=...)`; all padding conditions now live in `_maybe_pad_weight()`. Whenever it does not pad, it returns its input, so the rebind is a no-op. On a weight update the padding is skipped:
- The parameters already carry the padded layout.
- The MoE weight loaders write into it in place (`narrow().copy_()`).
- Layerwise reload copies the processed values back into the original tensors.
So storage addresses stay unchanged, which is the guarantee #46009 added. #62977's `test_aiter_moe_padding_rl_reload_address_stable` (AITER path) and this PR's `test_triton_moe_padding_survives_weight_update` (TRITON path) both check it.

**Scope.**
- **ROCm only.** `_maybe_pad_weight` is gated on `current_platform.is_rocm()`, `VLLM_ROCM_MOE_PADDING`, the absence of EPLB and the initial load. On other platforms it returns its input, and the changed lines are a no-op, as they were before.
- **Not architecture-specific.** On ROCm the padding is architecture-independent. This PR restores the behaviour from before #46009 and does not extend padding to anything new.

**Trade-off.** Restoring the padding also restores its memory cost, which disappeared together with the speed-up:

| Config (GLM-4.7-Flash) | Extra memory per GPU |
|---|---|
| TP4 (`w13` padded) | +0.54 GiB |
| TP2 (`w13` and `w2` padded) | +2.52 GiB |

Deployments sized on recent `main` with little memory headroom may need a higher `--gpu-memory-utilization`. Our TP2 run at 0.8 failed with "No available memory for the cache blocks". Alternatively, `VLLM_ROCM_MOE_PADDING=0` trades the speed-up for memory.

**Limitations.**
- End-to-end validation was done on Radeon Pro W7900 (gfx1100) only. Unit tests were also run on Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201).
- The change runs at load time only and adds no CPU/GPU synchronization during inference.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Skip Mooncake saves after failed existence checks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip an optional Mooncake cache save when its SDK existence check fails, instead of interpreting the failed keys as misses and issuing a PUT. Skipped jobs report completion through the existing path so GPU references can be released after all workers finish.

## Claims

- Both regular and boundary-state saves classify negative per-key results and raised SDK exceptions as errors.
- Failed existence checks skip PUT and record accurate failed-key counts and error/partial-failure status.
- Failed or skipped saves still report job completion. Active native transfers retain their buffers until the call returns.

## Validation

With the new tests and the unmodified worker from public main `fe3ed684ce`, the focused regression produced **6 failed, 3 passed**: each failed-existence case incorrectly issued a PUT.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -k 'failed_existence_check_skips_put_and_completes_save or failed_put_still_completes_save' -q
```

With the fix, the full worker and scheduler suites pass: **362 passed**. This includes successful-miss and cached-key filtering, raised SDK errors, boundary saves, failed PUTs making one attempt per job, and GPU references remaining held until all ranks report completion.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
```

Pre-commit checks pass. Tests use a controlled external SDK on a CPU host; no live Mooncake/RDMA, GPU serving, or model evaluation was run. No throughput or output-equivalence claim is made.

## Details

`batch_is_exist` returns 1 for a hit, 0 for a miss, and negative codes for failures. Save deduplication previously recorded a successful check and selected `result != 1` for PUT, including failed keys. Both save paths now share the result classification and skip the optional save if any key check fails.

The existing completion finalizer releases the store job through the scheduler's all-rank accounting. No forced cancellation, queue limit, timeout, or circuit breaker is introduced. The one-attempt test covers vLLM's job, not retries inside the SDK or later jobs.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR covering negative save-existence results. [#66956](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66956) covers transfer-thread shutdown, and [#46906](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46906) covers store retention policy; those are separate paths.

AI assistance was used to prepare this draft.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][P/D] Proxies: return text/event-stream for streaming requests
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The P/D proxies forward the decode instance's SSE stream but always label it `media_type="application/json"`. Clients that pick the parsing mode from the `Content-Type` header (e.g. EvalScope `perf`, NVIDIA AIPerf) then treat the stream as a single JSON body: they wait for the whole response, can't parse any tokens, and report

- TTFT = full end-to-end latency
- TPOT = 0, output tokens = 0, throughput = 0

with no error. `vllm bench serve` and the OpenAI Python client ignore the header, so CI didn't catch it. The NIXL toy proxy is referenced in the P/D docs for single-node testing, so benchmarks run through it can silently produce wrong numbers.

## Change

Use `text/event-stream` when the request has `"stream": true`; non-streaming requests keep `application/json`. Applied to every P/D proxy that forwards the decode stream:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py`
- `examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/disagg_proxy_pushconnector_demo.py`
- `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/p2p_connector_proxy.py` (2 call sites)

```python
return StreamingResponse(
    generate_stream(),
    media_type="text/event-stream" if req_data.get("stream") else "application/json",
)
```

`tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py` also uses `media_type="application/json"`, but it mocks a plain JSON body, so it is left unchanged.

## Test

Single-node 1P1D with the NIXL toy proxy (TP4 prefill + TP4 decode, NixlConnector, GLM-5.3-Flash, 8x MI308X, vLLM v0.33.0):

- Before: `content-type: application/json`. EvalScope perf reported TPOT 0, Gen/s 0, and TTFT ≈ request latency (e.g. 11.9 s for 1k in / 1k out).
- After: `content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`. SSE chunks arrive every ~11 ms (`curl -N`), and EvalScope reports normal TTFT/TPOT/throughput.
- Non-streaming requests (EvalScope GSM8K eval) are unchanged.

The other two proxies get the identical change; only the NIXL toy proxy was exercised end-to-end. `pre-commit run` passes on all three files.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Report the matching request type's error from SageMaker /invocations
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The SageMaker `/invocations` endpoint reports a misleading error for malformed requests (a chat request with a bad field comes back as "Either prompt or prompt_embeds must be provided"), and rejects some valid completion requests that a chat-only validator refuses. This PR makes `/invocations` serve and reject requests the same way as the matching `/v1/...` endpoint. The behaviour was introduced by #36254; #65029 fixes the same pydantic behaviour in `run_batch`.

## Claims

- A malformed chat or completion request sent to `/invocations` gets the same 400 error (message and `param`) as `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/completions`, e.g. `param=body.temperature` instead of `param=prompt` (chat) or `param=None` with "Cannot find suitable handler" (completion).
- A valid completion request that a chat validator rejects, e.g. `{"prompt": "hi", "logprobs": 0, "logprob_token_ids": [1]}`, is served as a completion like on `/v1/completions`, instead of failing with the chat validator's 400.
- On pooling models, a malformed rerank or score request reports its own field error instead of the generic "Cannot find suitable handler" message.
- Requests that `/invocations` already served are routed exactly as before.

## Validation

New test `tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/test_sagemaker_invocation_validation.py`, through `RemoteOpenAIServer` with `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` (already used by the SageMaker tests) and `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L12-v2` (already used by `tests/entrypoints/pooling`).

```
pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/test_sagemaker_invocation_validation.py
```

| | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| chat body, `temperature: "hot"` | FAILED `assert 'prompt' == 'body.temperature'` | PASSED |
| completion body, `temperature: "hot"` | FAILED `assert None == 'body.temperature'` | PASSED |
| valid completion body with `logprobs: 0, logprob_token_ids: [1]` | FAILED `assert 400 == 200` ("when using `logprob_token_ids`, `logprobs` must be set to true") | PASSED |
| rerank body on an embedding model, `top_n: "x"` | FAILED `assert None == 'body.top_n'` | PASSED |
| chat body, `stream_options` without `stream` (guard) | PASSED | PASSED |

The other 22 tests in `tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker` pass on both the base and this PR (`pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker`).

These runs used CPU only: vLLM's Arm CPU nightly wheel for 96710245ec, whose `vllm/entrypoints/`, `vllm/exceptions.py` and `tests/utils.py` are identical to this PR's base, with this PR's `api_router.py` swapped in. The host has no bf16, so the local copies of the tests used `--dtype float32` and `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4`. The committed tests keep their dtypes and run in the "Entrypoints Integration (API Server)" step. `pre-commit run --files` passes on both changed files.

## Details

Root cause: `/invocations` validates the body against each supported request type in priority order (chat, completion, then the pooling types) and treated only `pydantic.ValidationError` as "not this type". #36254 made the protocol validators raise `VLLMValidationError`, which pydantic does not wrap in a `ValidationError` (it wraps only `ValueError` and `AssertionError`). So after a chat body failed chat validation for any reason, `CompletionRequest`'s before-validator raised `VLLMValidationError("Either prompt or prompt_embeds must be provided ...")`, which escaped the loop and became the response. In the other direction, a chat validator that raises `VLLMValidationError` on a valid completion body (e.g. `check_logprobs` on `logprob_token_ids` with `logprobs: 0`) stopped the loop before `CompletionRequest` was tried.

Fix:
- Catch `VLLMValidationError` in the loop too.
- When no type accepts the body, report the error of the first type whose required top-level fields are all in the body, i.e. the type the client meant. A `ValidationError` is re-raised as `RequestValidationError` with a `body` prefix on `loc`, so the existing handler formats it exactly like that type's own endpoint. Required fields are computed once at startup from the request models; a union such as `EmbeddingRequest` contributes one set per member.
- When the body has the required fields of no type, the existing "Cannot find suitable handler" response is unchanged.

The required-field check is used instead of inspecting the errors because the pooling request types report `loc` with pydantic-internal wrapper segments and mix the errors of all union members, so "has a top-level `missing` error" cannot tell a wrong type from a bad field.

Limitation: `CompletionRequest` has no required fields, so on a generate model a body that matches neither type still gets the completion error, as on the base.

Not a duplicate: searched open and merged PRs and all issues for "sagemaker", "invocations", "api_router", "VLLMValidationError", "Either prompt or prompt_embeds", "validate_python" and "Cannot find suitable handler", and scanned the files of the 300 most recently updated open PRs. None touches `vllm/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/`. #64660 changes the Rust frontend's `/invocations`; #65029 fixes `run_batch.py`.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to investigate the bug, write the fix and tests, and run the validation above. I reviewed every changed line and the test results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Multimodal and LoRA in the engine-free renderer
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The engine-free Rust renderer (`vllm-rs render`) now renders multimodal chat requests and accepts LoRA adapter names. HTTP chat render returns Python's `features` object, and the Rust `/inference/v1/generate` accepts `features`, so a multimodal render response can be submitted to generate unchanged.

First of a stack split out of #64685, as requested in review there. The gRPC `vllm.Render.RenderChat` PR builds on this one, and the Derender RPCs follow after that.

## Claims

- **Multimodal render.** `vllm-rs render` loads the multimodal processors and fetches and preprocesses image, video and audio chat parts. New flags:
  - `--dtype`: the dtype media tensors are produced in, which must match the engine's. `auto`, the default, follows the model config and runs float32 checkpoints in bfloat16, like vLLM's `--dtype auto`. Accepts vLLM's `--dtype` choices, including `half` and `float`.
  - `--limit-mm-per-prompt`: the engine's per-modality limits, so render rejects the same requests. Accepts the engine's configurable form too; only `count` applies.
  - `--language-model-only`: skip multimodal processing.
- **HTTP render → generate.**
  - Chat render returns Python's `features` object: `mm_hashes`, `mm_placeholders` and base64 MessagePack `kwargs_data`.
  - It honors `mm_payload: "none"` and the deprecated `return_mm_kwargs: false`.
  - Placeholder ranges carry an `is_embed` mask for models with sparse placeholders, such as Qwen-VL.
  - `/inference/v1/generate` accepts `features`, which is mutually exclusive with `content_parts`.
- **LoRA.** `--lora-modules` names are accepted as the request `model`, are passed through to generate, and are listed in `/v1/models` with `parent` set to the base model. As in Python, no adapter weights are loaded.

## Validation

| Area | Tests |
|---|---|
| HTTP multimodal | `render_chat_multimodal_features_can_be_submitted_to_generate_unchanged`: render a chat request with an image, send the body unchanged to `/inference/v1/generate`, and check the engine request's features (identifier, placeholder range, `is_embed`, `pixel_values`, `image_grid_thw`). `render_chat_mm_payload_none_returns_layout_only`; `features` JSON round trip; hash-only and mismatched `features` rejected. |
| HTTP LoRA | `render_accepts_lora_adapter_model` (render + the `/v1/models` card); `lora_modules_are_checked_like_serve` (served-name and duplicate adapter names rejected at startup, with the same check `serve` runs when loading adapters) |
| Generate | `generate_rejects_content_parts_with_features` (fails without the fix: 200 with `features` dropped) |
| Render server | `--dtype` auto resolution; config `dtype` / `torch_dtype` / `text_config` parsing; CLI flags including `--limit-mm-per-prompt` |

```bash
cd rust
cargo test --no-fail-fast -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-text --lib --bins
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
```

Clippy and fmt are clean. All tests pass except two that are not caused by this branch:
- `routes::tests::chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample` fails in the full `vllm-server` suite on unmodified `main` too, and passes alone.
- `multimodal::audio::tests::audio_pipeline_attributes_stage_timings_to_request` fails intermittently and passes alone.

End to end on one GB200 with Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (bf16): `vllm-rs render` output posted unchanged to `/inference/v1/generate` on `vllm-rs serve --enable-scale-out`, against the same chat request on that server's `/v1/chat/completions` (greedy, 64 tokens, after one warm-up request per prompt):

| Case | Prompt tokens | Prompt token IDs | Output token IDs | `is_embed` true / length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| text | 13 | equal | equal | – |
| image | 159 | equal | equal | 140 / 140 |
| video | 12587 | equal | equal | 12432 / 12566 |
| image + video | 12729 | equal | equal | both of the above |

The video `features` carry about 200 MB of `kwargs_data`, so generate ran with `VLLM_HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` raised. With `mm_payload: "none"`, render omits `kwargs_data` and generate rejects the body with 400. Without the warm-up, the first cold request for the image prompt diverged at the third output token from every later request on either path, including an identical second chat request.

## Details

- **Why render needs `--dtype`.** The render server has no engine handshake to learn the model dtype from, and media tensors must be produced in the engine's dtype. `auto` only reads the dtype when the model has a multimodal processor.
- **Shared codec.** The MessagePack kwargs codec moves from `grpc/media.rs` to a new `mm_wire` module, shared by the HTTP `features` decoder and the existing gRPC `PreprocessedMediaFeatures` decoder. Behavior is unchanged: the depth limit and trailing-data check stay.
- **Limits.** `--dtype auto` reads only the model config (and its `text_config`); unlike vLLM it does not look at the weights or the GPU, so pass the engine's dtype when those decide it; a config dtype it does not recognize runs in bfloat16. Some image processors size images to fit the context, so `--max-model-len` should match the engine's. A large image's or video's `features` can exceed generate's 32 MiB default body limit; `VLLM_HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` raises it.
- **`is_embed`.** #54548 on main added the mask to Python's `PlaceholderRangeInfo`, so both frontends' render responses carry it and both generates read it.
- **Gap vs Python.** The Rust render response does not include `mm_metadata`, and the Rust generate ignores it. A `features` object without `kwargs_data` for every item is rejected.
- **Not a duplicate.** The open PR search found only #64685, which this replaces in part. #36102 and #33693 are Python gRPC render servers, #53418/#53419 are Rust HTTP `/derender`, and #60002 returns token offsets from render. None of them touches multimodal or LoRA in the Rust renderer.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to split this out of #64685 and write the description.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Enable SM90 block-FP8 MegaMoE via FlashInfer MoE-EP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vLLM has no MegaMoE that runs on Hopper today:

- the DeepGEMM MegaMoE (`deep_gemm_mega_moe`) requires SM100;
- the FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernels (`flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl`, `flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm`) require SM100

This PR runs block-FP8 MoE checkpoints on Hopper with FlashInfer's SM90 FP8 MegaMoE, which ships in FlashInfer 0.7.2. The kernel fuses dispatch, both expert GEMMs and combine. It goes through the existing `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` path with no model code, so compatible 128x128 block-FP8 MoE models can use it.

Related:
- #58540: the same kernel, but for DeepSeek-V4 FP4 checkpoints converted to FP8, and on files that #54049 removed.
- #62073: Beam on SM100. It contains the same idle-rank change as this PR.
- #60895: DeepGEMM MegaMoE for GLM-5.3-Flash, SM100 only.
- #53527: DeepSeek-V4 through a DeepGEMM fork.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash decode on 8x H200 (DP8/EP8, 128K/512, MTP3): +11% to +18% output throughput and -6% to -14% TPOT p50, at concurrency 8 to 192.
- GLM-5.3-Flash prefill on 4x H200 (TP2/DP2/EP4, MTP3, ISL 2048 / OSL 1): +23% saturated throughput, and TTFT p50 -14% to -54% at 15 to 21 req/s.
- One MoE layer at EP8: -7% at 8 tokens/rank, up to -48% at 8192 tokens/rank.
- Reported GSM8K scores are comparable in both configurations.
- The backend is opt-in. Default backends do not change.

## Validation

**Main sync (2026-11-09).** Commit `5ba7bd31d3` merges main `199c2e4bff`. All four FP8 loaders retain expert weight processing followed by `keep_constants`; kernel math and backend defaults are unchanged.

- FlashInfer 0.7.3: CPU **32 passed**; H200 **4 passed**, covering synthetic GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next expert geometries at EP2/EP4, exact outputs, storage aliasing/swaps, eager idle-rank participation and nonempty CUDA Graph replay. The same selection also passed with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1.
- Validation uses the current Python sources over the existing native vLLM 0.31 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 build, rather than a full native rebuild of main. Local pre-commit and independent code review passed.
- The serving and GSM8K measurements below are historical and were not rerun for this merge.

**Setup.**
- Source: main fa75d345 with the same KDA RecoverSSM patches (#61566, #56082) in both arms. Only decode enabled `--use-replayssm`.
- Client: `vllm-rs bench serve` (0.32.0rc1.dev284) with token-ID prompts.
- Runs are serial A/B/A on the same GPUs. "Base" is the mean of the two baseline arms.

**Decode.**
- 8x H200, DP8/EP8, DecodeBenchConnector, ISL 128K / OSL 512, MTP3 with synthetic acceptance [0.8, 0.6, 0.5], N = 2C prompts, two passes per arm.
- These runs used the first commit. The later review fixes do not change this path under DP. One extra pass on the second commit gave +8% to +24% throughput over the same base.

| C | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s, base | 911 | 2895 | 5204 | 7977 | 10074 |
| output tok/s, this PR | 1009 (+10.8%) | 3402 (+17.5%) | 5893 (+13.2%) | 9326 (+16.9%) | 11917 (+18.3%) |
| TPOT p50 ms, base → this PR | 7.60 → 6.86 | 9.20 → 7.96 | 9.27 → 8.72 | 10.81 → 9.85 | 11.58 → 10.87 |

**Prefill.**
- 4x H200, TP2 × DP2 + EP4, natural MTP3, ISL 2048 / OSL 1. Both arms run sequence-parallel MoE.
- Saturation: 64 warm-up requests, then 3 × 1000 requests at an unlimited rate. Poisson: 60 s per rate.
- Prefill applied this PR's changes at 7558a8cabb to the same frozen stack.

| | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| saturated req/s, median of 3 | 21.44 | 26.35 (+22.9%) |
| TTFT p50 ms at 11 / 15 / 19 / 21 req/s | 370 / 488 / 787 / 1365 | 409 / 418 / 515 / 630 |
| TTFT p99 ms at 11 / 15 / 19 / 21 req/s | 838 / 939 / 1438 / 2699 | 737 / 808 / 820 / 1059 |

The base saturates at 21.4 req/s. At 23 and 25 req/s its TTFT p50 is 3.8 and 4.5 s, while this PR serves 22.7 and 24.7 req/s at 610 and 831 ms. At 11 req/s the median TTFT is 10% higher (base arms 351 and 389 ms).

**MoE layer, EP8.** GLM-5.3-Flash expert shapes, milliseconds per layer:

| tokens/rank | 8 | 64 | 128 | 512 | 1024 | 8192 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.265 | 0.381 | 0.446 | 0.834 | 1.378 | 9.204 |
| this PR | 0.247 | 0.294 | 0.310 | 0.461 | 0.754 | 4.798 |

**GSM8K.** 1319 questions, 5-shot, natural MTP3:
- DEP8: 0.917 → 0.919.
- TP2/DP2: 0.918 and 0.920 → 0.917 and 0.920. MTP acceptance 0.804 → 0.802.

**Historical tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe_ep.py
# CPU: 29 passed. SM90 GPU: 8 passed (4 expert shapes x EP2/EP4).
```

The SM90 GPU tests need at least two Hopper GPUs and `nvshmem4py`, so CI does not run them.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

`--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` is omitted for the baseline. Both servers run with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.

```bash
# Decode
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-Flash FP8> --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --use-replayssm \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.8,0.6,0.5]}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl

vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 512 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((2 * C)) --seed 0

# Prefill
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-Flash FP8> --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl

# warm-up: --num-prompts 64 --seed 100; saturation: --seed 102, 104, 106
vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --num-prompts 1000 --seed 102
# Poisson
vllm-rs bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --request-rate $R --num-prompts $((60 * R)) --seed $((200 + R))

# GSM8K: the decode server without the KV connector and synthetic acceptance, or the prefill server
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port $PORT
```
</details>

## Details

- **Kernel.**
  - FlashInfer `Sm90PullFp8MegaMoeConfig`, with FP32 128x128 weight scales and a SwiGLU clamp.
  - FlashInfer's push-style SM90 backend has no SwiGLU clamp, so it cannot serve `swiglu_limit` models.
- **Weights.**
  - The kernel wants FC1 rows interleaved as `[pair, {gate, up}, 8]` under one 128x128 scale. Each scale block therefore covers rows from two checkpoint blocks, and both use `max(s_gate, s_up)`.
  - Power-of-two scale ratios preserve values that remain in the E4M3 normal range; smaller rescaled values may round. Other ratios can add an E4M3 rounding step on the rescaled FC1 rows.
- **Workspaces.**
  - The kernel always processes its whole token buffer, with a launch geometry picked for that size. With a single buffer sized at `max_num_batched_tokens`, decode is slower than the baseline.
  - The adapter therefore adds 64-, 256- and 1024-token workspaces. Each call uses the smallest one that fits the largest batch across DP ranks. Without DP-wide token counts it uses the default workspace, because every rank must pick the same buffer.
- **Loaders.**
  - The fp8, compressed-tensors, online FP8 and Quark FP8 MoE methods now call the experts' `process_weights_after_loading`. It is a no-op for other experts.
  - The SM90 path is chosen from the quant config, not the weight dtype. FP8 weights keep their dtype, so a rebuild from preprocessed weights picks the same path.
- **Idle ranks.** With pass-through stages, the experts own the EP collective. A rank without tokens therefore still enters them. The change is identical to the one in #62073.
- **Limitations.**
  - The backend needs expert parallelism and `nvshmem4py`.
  - It rejects DBO, runtime weight transfer and `apply_router_weight_on_input`.
  - Shared experts are not fused.
  - FlashInfer's SM90 input staging is torch-composed, about 1.2 ms per step at C128.
  
## FlashInfer upstream

- [[flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4113](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4113)](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4113): Introduces the SM90 pull-style FP8 MegaMoE kernel (`Sm90PullFp8MegaMoeConfig`) used by this PR through FlashInfer's `MoEEpLayer` API.
- [[flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6999](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6999)](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6999): Ongoing work to add an SM90 NVFP4-weight / FP8-activation (W4A8) MegaMoE backend to the same MoE-EP API. Support for this backend is outside the scope of this PR and can be added as a follow-up.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Muse Spark] Add gfx942 FP8 W8A8 fused-MoE configs for E=32,N=4096
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds tuned Triton fused-MoE configs for gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X) for Muse Spark's per-rank expert shape at TP8 + EP (`E=32, N=4096, fp8_w8a8`, per-token FP8), which today falls back to `get_default_config`. On MI300X: +12–25% serving throughput at 64 concurrent requests, GSM8K unchanged. On MI325X: +20–21% serving throughput at 64–128 concurrent requests, GSM8K unchanged. Config files only; no other PR adds this shape.

## Validation

`amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-PTPC-FP8`, 8× MI300X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-83c078d955`. Both arms run the same image and flags; the candidate mounts this file over `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/`, and the server log confirms it is loaded.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-PTPC-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend triton \
  --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --reasoning-parser muse
```

### Serving

Total throughput, this config vs default, higher is better:

| ISL / OSL | c1 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k / 1k | +1.1% | −0.7% | +3.7% | +2.8% | **+23.6%** |
| 8k / 1k | +1.3% | +0.4% | +4.6% | +4.2% | **+15.5%** |
| 16k / 1k | +1.4% | +1.6% | +4.4% | +4.9% | **+11.6%** |
| 1k / 8k | +1.0% | +2.0% | +4.2% | +3.3% | **+24.8%** |

At 64 concurrent requests, default → this config:

| ISL / OSL | Total tok/s | Median TTFT | Median TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k / 1k | 2,455 → 3,034 | 1.82 → 1.72 s | 50.2 → 40.5 ms |
| 8k / 1k | 6,700 → 7,739 | 2.52 → 2.38 s | 82.5 → 71.3 ms |
| 16k / 1k | 8,768 → 9,781 | 3.19 → 3.02 s | 118.9 → 106.9 ms |
| 1k / 8k | 1,484 → 1,852 | 1.82 → 1.72 s | 48.3 → 38.7 ms |

c1–c8 is flat by design: decode there runs at batch 8 or below, which uses the default tile as on main. One run per point, three waves of requests (four requests at c1), after two warm-up runs.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-PTPC-FP8 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <3*C> \
  --seed 6 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

### Kernel

One MI300X, routing over all 256 experts with one rank's `expert_map`, as in serving: 5–7% faster at batch 16–32 and 23–29% faster at 48–128. Batch 1–8 runs the default tile.

### MI325X

8× MI325X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-3966924d`, the serve command matching with the above MI300X case. 1k / 1k, this config vs default:

| | c1 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 | c128 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total throughput | −0.2% | +0.3% | +1.9% | +5.8% | **+21.4%** | **+20.4%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 13.31 → 13.34 | 19.70 → 19.65 | 24.70 → 23.76 | 31.41 → 29.69 | 44.24 → 36.28 | 55.96 → 46.13 |

GSM8K at 64 concurrent requests (command below), flexible-extract: 0.9500 ± 0.006 default, 0.9515 ± 0.006 this config.

Kernel, one MI325X, the same routing; MoE call time in µs, median of five interleaved runs, vs the default tile and vs the MI300X file under the MI325X name:

| Batch | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 | 8192 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | 234 | 355 | 594 | 631 | 652 | 693 | 844 | 1000 | 1429 | 2557 |
| MI300X file | 222 | 338 | 439 | 452 | 502 | 711 | 814 | 1080 | 1422 | 2352 |
| This config | 216 | 327 | 439 | 441 | 496 | 541 | 617 | 882 | 1329 | 2332 |

The MI300X tiles do not carry over: on MI325X they lose to the default tile at batch 512, 2048 and 3072. Every MI325X entry gives bit-identical outputs to the default tile on the same inputs (FP8 products accumulate exactly in fp32).

### Accuracy

GSM8K 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, at 64 concurrent requests so decode runs at batch 64:

| | flexible-extract |
| --- | --- |
| Default | 0.9507 ± 0.006 |
| This config | 0.9507 ± 0.006 |

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 4321 \
  --model_args model=amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-PTPC-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=<checkpoint dir>
```

## Details

- **Tuning, MI300X.** Batch 512–8192 come from `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --tune --tp-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --dtype fp8_w8a8`. Under EP that script routes every token over the 32 local experts, so each expert sees 8× its serving rows, and its picks for batch 8–32 lost to the default tile. Batch 16–256 were re-tuned with a local patch that routes over all 256 experts and keeps one rank's 32 through an `expert_map`, with `num_stages` in {1, 2}. The patch is not part of this PR; the diff is below. Batch 8 keeps the default tile, and batch 1–7 resolve to it.
- **Tuning, MI325X.** Every batch tuned on MI325X with the patched script's `benchmark_config` (serving routing, per-token activations, `num_stages` in {1, 2}), the top eight of each search re-timed. Batch 8 and 24 keep the MI300X entries, which time level or better on MI325X. Batch 128 is the best of the MI300X tile and the top batch-96 and batch-256 picks, timed at batch 128.
- **Scope.** MI300X and MI325X, TP8 + EP without redundant experts (E=32). The tile is keyed by tokens per step, which chunked prefill caps at 8192, so the 16k rows already exercise every entry. Context beyond 16k was not run.
- The serving table was measured with batch 1, 2 and 4 entries that were later dropped as level with the default tile. They only applied below batch 8, which now runs the default tile.

<details>
<summary>Tuner patch (not in this PR)</summary>

The FP8 quant dtype becomes the platform's: with `float8_e4m3fn`, `FusedMoEQuantConfig.use_fp8_w8a8` is false on gfx942 (e4m3fnuz), and the script does not time the W8A8 kernel serving runs.

```diff
@@ -182 +182,6 @@
-    gating_output = torch.randn(num_iters, num_tokens, num_experts, dtype=torch.float32)
+    global_e = int(os.environ.get("MOE_TUNE_GLOBAL_E", num_experts))
+    expert_map = None
+    if global_e != num_experts:
+        expert_map = torch.full((global_e,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+        expert_map[:num_experts] = torch.arange(num_experts, dtype=torch.int32)
+    gating_output = torch.randn(num_iters, num_tokens, global_e, dtype=torch.float32)
@@ -245 +250 @@
-    input_gating = torch.empty(num_tokens, num_experts, dtype=torch.float32)
+    input_gating = torch.empty(num_tokens, global_e, dtype=torch.float32)
@@ -254 +259 @@
-            quant_dtype = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+            quant_dtype = FP8_DTYPE
@@ -324,0 +330,2 @@
+                global_num_experts=global_e,
+                expert_map=expert_map,
@@ -373 +380,3 @@
-    num_stage_range = [2]
+    num_stage_range = [
+        int(v) for v in os.environ.get("MOE_TUNE_NUM_STAGES", "2").split(",")
+    ]
```

```bash
MOE_TUNE_GLOBAL_E=256 MOE_TUNE_NUM_STAGES=1,2 \
python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model <checkpoint dir> --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --dtype fp8_w8a8 --tune --batch-size <B> --save-dir <dir>
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Offload] Split the shared Tiering region and skip the scheduler pre-fault
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Tiering keeps one shared CPU region per engine so its secondary tiers can address it. At large sizes it is slow to set up:

- The region is one `/dev/shm` file, so every worker pre-faults into the same file and page-cache inserts serialize.
- The scheduler then maps the whole region and pre-faults every page again, on one thread.

This splits the region across `REGION_SEGMENTS` files, as `CPUOffloadingSpec` already does (#59546), and maps the scheduler side without pre-faulting. Secondary tiers still see one contiguous range.

#45693 (hugetlbfs) is a separate, opt-in backend.

## Results

CPU tier setup only (worker pre-fault and pinning, scheduler mapping, P2P registration), timed with a script that runs those steps through vLLM's own classes. One H100 node, 8 worker processes sharing one GPU, P2P tier, GLM-5.3-sized rows (8 x 3.8 MB slots):

| Tier | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 512 GiB | 167-175 s | 59 s |
| 1,250 GiB | 397-460 s | 135-138 s |

At 1,250 GiB, worker pre-fault drops from 255-317 s to 55 s and the 59-140 s scheduler pre-fault is gone. Pinning goes up from 15-35 s to 42 s; P2P registration stays at ~40 s.

commits.pr_title: [Misc] Use the b12x package shipped with flashinfer-python
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

flashinfer-python 0.7.2 and later ship b12x and install it as a top-level `b12x` package, so `import b12x` already resolves to FlashInfer's copy with the `flashinfer-python==0.7.2.post1` that vLLM pins. The `b12x` extra still installs the standalone `b12x==1.5.1` package, which provides a second top-level `b12x` and overrides FlashInfer's copy depending on install order. The standalone repository is archived and development continues in FlashInfer.

This PR:
- turns the `b12x` extra into an empty list kept for backwards compatibility, like the `flashinfer` extra, so `pip install vllm[b12x]` keeps working and no longer installs the standalone package
- changes the unavailable-backend messages in the b12x attention and linear kernels to `The b12x backend requires flashinfer-python>=0.7.2` (0.7.2 is the first release that ships `b12x`), and updates the two tests that assert them
- drops the separate install step from the b12x docs pages and the commented-out Spark b12x lane in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`

No import paths change: `vllm/utils/b12x.py` keeps importing `b12x.*`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the `b12x` extra or the b12x install path (searched open PRs for b12x).

## Test Plan

DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-335dd77b0` with the Python `vllm/` tree and `tests/` from this branch overlaid, flashinfer-python 0.7.2.post1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, no standalone `b12x` installed.

| `model_executor/test_b12x_warmup.py` | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| `kernels/moe/test_b12x.py` | 44 | 0 | 0 |

All 4 `test_w8a8_block_fp8_b12x_matmul` cases pass. The 6 failures in `test_block_fp8.py` are the CUTLASS (`test_w8a8_block_fp8_cutlass_matmul`) and `torch._scaled_mm` paths on SM121, which do not use b12x. They fail identically with standalone `b12x==1.5.1` installed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Use max_split_size_mb:21 so freed 1-10 MiB tensors are reused
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`Worker.load_model` and `profile_run` scope the caching allocator to `max_split_size_mb:20` (#41268, #58430). At exactly 20 MiB, every freed 1–10 MiB device tensor strands a 20 MiB segment, so loaders that upload weights one small tensor at a time fill the device and then load through allocator OOM retries. This raises the limit to 21 MiB.

Fixes #51205. Makes the Inkling-only workaround in #51962 unnecessary.

## Claims

- Freed 1–10 MiB tensors are reused under the load/profile split limit again, instead of each stranding a 20 MiB segment.
- Kimi-K3-REAP (780 GiB), TP8 on 8xB200, RunAI streamer in distributed mode: model loading **690–703 s → 96.8 s**, allocator OOM retries **~964,000 → 0**, same output.
- #51205 (Inkling-Small-NVFP4) is fixed with no Inkling change: the test from #51962, run against the unpatched loader, passes.
- No change for large blocks: blocks of 21 MiB and up are still never split, so freed large blocks stay releasable, which is what #41268 and #58430 rely on.

## Validation

**End to end:** Kimi-K3-REAP-448experts, 8xB200, TP8, `load_format=runai_streamer`, `model_loader_extra_config={"distributed": true}`, `external_launcher`, cold page cache, vLLM nightly `0.33.0rc1.dev1030`, torch 2.14.0.

| `max_split_size_mb` | Model loading | Allocator OOM retries | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 (main) | 689.8 s, 702.6 s | ~964,000 | " Paris.\nThe capital of Germany is Berlin" |
| **21 (this PR)** | **96.8 s** | **0** | same |
| 20 + `expandable_segments:True` | 116.2 s | 0 | same |

With 20, GPU memory sits at 182.6 of 191 GB for the whole load. A mid-load allocator snapshot showed 3,330 cached 20 MiB segments holding 65 GiB with 2.9 GiB in use.

**Unit tests (B200):**
- New `test_scoped_max_split_reuses_freed_small_tensor_segments`: allocates and frees 100 tensors of 1–9 MiB under `load_model`'s limit. Fails with the constant at 20 (reserved grows 2000 MiB), passes at 21 (grows 20 MiB).
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`: 50 passed.
- #51962's `test_moe_w13_upload_reuses_cuda_allocator_segments` body against the unpatched Inkling loader: 320 MiB reserved at 20 (fails its 40 MiB bound), 20 MiB at 21 (passes).

**Allocation sizes at limit 20,** 100 alloc+free each: 6 MiB grows 2000 MiB, 15 MiB grows 16 MiB, 25 MiB grows 26 MiB. Only 1–10 MiB requests are affected.

**Not run:** `tests/kernels/quantization/test_k3_gfx942_int4_requant.py` needs an MI300 (gfx942), which I don't have; it should be covered by the MI300 quantization-kernels job (`/amd-ci run`).

## Details

**Root cause.** PyTorch serves every 1–10 MiB request from a 20 MiB segment (`kLargeBuffer`, a compile-time constant). A free block of size ≥ `max_split_size` is "oversize" and is never split for a request below the limit. With the limit at exactly 20 MiB:
1. A 6 MiB tensor gets a new 20 MiB segment; the other 14 MiB stays cached.
2. The loader copies it into the parameter and frees it. The 6 and 14 MiB coalesce into one free 20 MiB block.
3. 20 ≥ 20, so that block is oversize. The next 1–10 MiB tensor can't use it and gets a new segment.
4. Every such tensor strands 20 MiB. Once the device is full, each allocation frees the cache and retries.

With 21 the 20 MiB block is below the limit, so it is reused. Requests over 10 MiB are not affected at either value: their segment is the request rounded to 2 MiB (below 20, reusable), or oversize but reusable by a request of about the same size.

**Why 20 was there.** #41268 picked 20 as "the minimum PyTorch allows" (torch rejects values below `kLargeBuffer`), to keep large blocks from being split. 21 keeps that for everything above PyTorch's own small-request segment.

**Who hits it.** Any loader that frees a 1–10 MiB device tensor before allocating the next: the RunAI streamer in distributed mode (one owned device tensor per checkpoint tensor), and the Inkling w13 loader (#51205). `expandable_segments:True` also avoids it, but it is incompatible with sleep mode and NIXL, which is why #41268 used `max_split_size_mb`.

**Tests.** The new worker test pins the regression for any loader. The gfx942 requant test hardcoded `max_split_size_mb:20` to mimic `load_model`; it now uses `_MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB` so it tests the real setting. Its working chunks are hundreds of MiB, oversize at either limit, so its reuse should be unchanged.

**Related:** #59893 (open) adds another `max_split_size_mb=20` scope; it should use `_MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB` too if it lands after this.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the root-cause analysis, the change, the tests, and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

cc @MatthewBonanni (author of #41268, which introduced the 20 MiB limit) @tlrmchlsmth

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Disagg][CI] Set token budgets for the MiniMax-M3 wide-EP cells
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 wide-EP cells are very slow. The 2P2D EP16 GSM8K eval takes about 1h37 in CI and the 1P1D EP8 one about an hour. The AITER MXFP8 MoE kernel runs over a padded buffer sized by `--max-num-batched-tokens`, 131072 rows at the default, so every prefill and decode step pays for the whole buffer. Small token budgets shrink it. This sets 2048 for prefill and 64 for decode, and the evals drop to a couple of minutes.

## Changes

`models.yaml`: the MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 `ep:` flags gain `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048` (prefill) and `--max-num-batched-tokens 64` (decode). `--max-num-seqs` clips to the budget on its own. TP cells are untouched.

A launcher dry run over every model, tp/ep, topology and rank (168 cases) differs from main only for the MiniMax wide-EP cells.

## Test plan

Pipeline cells:

```
# 2P2D EP16
MODEL_NAME=MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 xP=2 yD=2 NODES=4 GPUS_PER_NODE=8 WIDE_EP_MODE=1 MORIIO_READ_MODE=0 RUN_AFTER_HEALTH=accuracy ROUTER_TYPE=vllm-router WAIT=1 bash .buildkite/amd-disagg/run-slurm-disagg-test.sh

# 1P1D EP8
MODEL_NAME=MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 NODES=2 GPUS_PER_NODE=8 WIDE_EP_MODE=1 MORIIO_READ_MODE=0 RUN_AFTER_HEALTH=accuracy ROUTER_TYPE=vllm-router WAIT=1 bash .buildkite/amd-disagg/run-slurm-disagg-test.sh
```

Serve commands they launch for EP16 (first node of each role, `--kv-transfer-config` unchanged). EP8 is the same with `--data-parallel-size 8`:

```
# prefill
vllm serve /data/models2/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address <prefill0> --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --port 20005 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --distributed-timeout-seconds 7200 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --block-size 128 --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enforce-eager --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --api-server-count=8 --kv-transfer-config ...

# decode
vllm serve /data/models2/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address <decode0> --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_low_latency --port 20005 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --distributed-timeout-seconds 7200 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --block-size 128 --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 --max-num-batched-tokens 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+quant_fp8"]}' \
  --api-server-count=8 --kv-transfer-config ...
```

GSM8K through `lm_eval` at concurrency 64, gate 0.90, behind `vllm-router`.

## Test results

After numbers are the CI image and CI tree with this diff applied, four nodes for EP16 and two for EP8.

| Cell | Eval time before | Eval time after | GSM8K after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2P2D EP16 | 1h37 to 1h39 | 118 s | 0.9098 |
| 1P1D EP8 | 54 min to 1h01 | 84 s | 0.9030 |

commits.pr_title: [Doc][Tests] Stop setting `gpu_memory_utilization` in most extensible KV cache cases
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With the extensible KV cache (#56492), the default on CUDA and ROCm, `gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0 and the KV cache is sized from the memory measured after warmup. Docs, examples, benchmarks, CI configs, tests and recipes still pass values like 0.9 carried over from estimate-based sizing, which now only shrink the KV cache. This PR documents when to set the option and removes values that no longer have a reason. Companion to #66704, which warns at startup when an explicit value above 0.7 withholds free memory from the KV cache.

## Claims

- **New docs section:** GPU Memory Utilization (`docs/configuration/optimization.md`) says when to leave the option unset, and lists the legitimate reasons to set it:
  - other processes sharing the GPU, including ones that allocate later;
  - unified-memory devices;
  - weight-transfer buffers for weight updates;
  - KV connectors with their own device buffers.

  It also covers where the option still sizes the KV cache: other platforms, and the cases where vLLM falls back to estimate-based sizing. The `CacheConfig`/`LLM` docstrings, the preemption and startup tips, the sharded RDT warning and `recipes/README.md` point to it.
- **Values removed:** explicit values above 0.7 are gone from CUDA/ROCm contexts in docs (7 pages), examples (14), benchmarks (`auto_tune.sh`, 3 scripts), CI benchmark configs (3) and recipes (89 files). Recipe OOM advice that suggested lowering the option is rewritten.
- **Tests and eval configs:** a separate commit drops explicit values that only compensated for estimate-based sizing:
  - raises to fit (0.95–0.98);
  - pins of the old 0.92 default;
  - 0.85–0.96 values whose comments cite CUDA graph memory profiling or FlashInfer autotuning, both of which warmup now measures;
  - unexplained 0.85–0.9 reductions in single-engine tests (spec-decode, batch invariance, multimodal) and gsm8k/gpt-oss eval configs.

  `VllmRunner`'s XPU branch now treats an explicit `None` like an unset value.
- **Values kept** where they're still meaningful:
  - TPU/XPU/CPU;
  - DGX Spark (unified memory);
  - P/D with NIXL, Mooncake or MoRIIO, where the extensible cache is off;
  - shared GPUs;
  - RL weight transfer, with a comment in each example saying why it sets the value.
  - tests with an HF model or a second engine in the same process, a GPU shared with an encoder, or lazy ROCm teardown;
  - tests that deliberately constrain the KV cache, or use `num_gpu_blocks_override` (extensible cache off).
  - Values ≤ 0.7 are left alone.
- **Messages:** the auto-fit `max_model_len` warning suggests raising `gpu_memory_utilization` only when it's below 1.0. The pooler-warmup OOM error no longer suggests lowering it; that warmup runs in the profile run, before any KV cache is allocated.

## Validation

- **pre-commit** passes: ruff, mypy, markdownlint, check-json.
- **Recipes:** each edited recipe still parses. A structural diff against `HEAD` shows the only changes are removed `--gpu-memory-utilization` args (and keys emptied by that) plus prose. No bash block ends in a dangling backslash. I didn't run `validate-source.mjs` from vllm-project/recipes; the `Recipes` PR check will.
- **Not run:** none of the edited examples, benchmarks or recipe commands were executed, and the edited tests haven't been run outside CI.
  - Removing the flag gives them the default, 1.0 with the extensible cache. That's the configuration #56492 validated across eight models.
  - **On vLLM versions before v0.33.0**, a recipe command without the flag gets the old default: 0.92 from v0.20.1, 0.9 before that.
  - **Tests:** the unexplained 0.85–0.9 test values have no recorded reason. If one was working around a transient that warmup doesn't exercise, it will show up as an OOM in CI.

## Details

**Why each kept value stays:** the extensible cache measures free memory once, after warmup, and keeps the measured transient plus a margin of max(1 GiB, 0.75 × peak) free (3 GiB on ROCm). Anything allocated outside that window needs explicit headroom:
- **KV connectors:** they're created after the final extend.
- **Weight transfer engines:** they create their communicators and buffers at `init_weight_transfer_engine`. `_release_for_weight_update` budgets only 3× the largest layer, not the transfer buffers (e.g. 2 × 1 GiB of NCCL packed buffers). This PR doesn't change that logic.
- **Accounted for, no headroom needed:** Mooncake EC's consumer slab is allocated before profiling, so it's counted. EPLB reserves its buffers in the profile run.

<details>
<summary>Recipe values deliberately left in place</summary>

- **Benchmark presets, and sections whose reported results were measured with the value.** These need re-measurement rather than a blind edit.
  - AgentX presets in MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K3, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
  - Measured KV results in GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, Hy4-preview, ERNIE-5.5-Flash, Muse-Glimmer-30B, and the InferenceX command in Kimi-K2.5.
- **diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it (0.85):** headroom for diffusion-denoising activations, which warmup may not exercise.
- **ERNIE-5.5-Flash (0.85):** advice for 1M-token prefills, which the recipe says need tens of GB of temporary memory.
- **Kimi-K3.1-Pro, 810e/m890 strategy overrides (0.9):** it isn't clear whether that platform gets the extensible cache.

</details>

Not in this PR: the vllm-project/recipes command builder offers a global "gpu-memory-utilization = 0.95" toggle (`src/lib/advanced-options.js`), and its `add-recipe` skill recommends copying the flag. Both need a follow-up there.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Bump xgrammar-structural-tag to 0.5 and compose Lark answers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Bump `xgrammar-structural-tag` to [0.5.0](https://crates.io/crates/xgrammar-structural-tag/0.5.0+xgrammar.0.2.9.8f9a127) (synced with XGrammar 0.2.9 in Inferact/xgrammar-structural-tag#1) and compose Lark answer grammars into parser-built output grammars, matching the Python frontend. Stacked on vllm-project/vllm#66691.

## Claims

- `answer_format` maps a `grammar` constraint to `Format::grammar(grammar, syntax)`, with `GrammarSyntax::Lark` for a Lark grammar, instead of returning `None` for Lark. Before, a Lark grammar stayed on its own wire field: under `auto` with no tool grammar it constrained the whole output, so no call could be made, and when the parser built a tool grammar (strict tools) the answer constraint was dropped. The Lark test is still the verbatim port of Python's `grammar_is_likely_lark`. 0.5.0 requires the syntax when building a grammar leaf; only deserialization reads an omitted `syntax` as EBNF.
- DeepSeek V4/V4.1 `auto` grammars now end after one calls block (`stop_after_first = true`), following upstream mlc-ai/xgrammar#936; the two grammar-replay goldens change by that one flag.
- The grammar-replay script pins `xgrammar==0.2.9` (it said "keep in sync with requirements/common.txt" but was still on 0.2.7).

## Validation

```bash
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server   # 1791 passed
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo deny check sources
uv run --script rust/src/chat/tests/grammar_replay.py          # 80 PASS, 0 FAIL on xgrammar 0.2.9
```

- Red-green: with the old `Grammar(_) if lark => None` arm restored, `answer_format_normalizes_composable_constraints` fails on the three Lark cases (moved there from `answer_format_leaves_other_constraints_on_their_wire_field`).
- The outline renderer prints `grammar lark` for Lark leaves so replay snapshots distinguish the two syntaxes.
- GPU (GB200, one GPU per server): this PR and its base (`7c9a2fa2b3` binary, xgrammar 0.2.8 engine) served Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (`hermes`) and Qwen3.5-0.8B (`qwen3_coder` + `qwen3` reasoning, thinking off), 32 cases per model, each sent greedy, streamed, and with 3 sampled seeds at temperature 1.0 (160 requests per server). Differences from base:
  - Lark `yes|no` answer with strict tools under `auto`: base ignores the answer constraint and returns free text ("Yes, the sky is usually blue…") in 5/5 requests per model; with this PR every request is `yes`/`no` or a schema-valid call. Same for a Lark grammar with regex terminals.
  - Lark `yes|no` answer with non-strict tools and a tool prompt: base can only answer (0/5 calls); with this PR both models call `get_weather` in 5/5 requests with schema-valid arguments.
  - Lark `start: "ok" <|im_end|>`, natively and with tools: base returns 500 (the 0.2.8 engine masks every token after `ok`, `grammar rejected tokens [0]`; mlc-ai/xgrammar#710); with this PR every request returns `ok` or a schema-valid call.
  - Everything else matches base on both models: `json_schema`, `json_object`, regex, choice, EBNF, `structural_tag`, `auto` with EBNF, JSON-schema or regex answers, `required`, single-call `required`, named, and `none`.
- Known and pre-existing, not changed here: with `--reasoning-parser qwen3` and thinking off, `DelimitedReasoningParser::wrap_visible_format` still allows an optional new `<think>` block before the answer after the prompt closed one, so a sampled Qwen3.5 request can open it and run to `max_tokens` without reaching the answer. That is 1 of 5 requests (one sampled seed) for EBNF, regex, JSON schema and structural tag on base and on this PR alike. Lark answers now go through the same output grammar, so plain Lark grammars show the same 1/5 on that model, where base passed because the grammar stayed on its wire field. Python enforces the answer from the first token in this case; the fix belongs in the reasoning wrap.

## Details

- The crate comes from crates.io (`0.5.0+xgrammar.0.2.9.8f9a127`); the lockfile change is that one package's version and checksum.
- The composed leaf needs xgrammar 0.2.9 in the engine (0.2.8 ignores `syntax`, parses the Lark text as EBNF, and fails with `EBNF lexer error ... Unexpected character: ':'`), hence the stack on vllm-project/vllm#66691.
- 0.5.0 also adds the `gemma_4` builder, `JsonSchemaStyle::Gemma`, and opt-in `token_markers`; no Rust parser uses them yet.
- Duplicate check: no open PR bumps `xgrammar-structural-tag` (`gh pr list --search "xgrammar-structural-tag"`).
