commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Bump xgrammar to 0.2.9 and compose Lark answers as Lark
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Bump xgrammar to [0.2.9](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/releases/tag/v0.2.9) and use its Lark structural-tag grammars (mlc-ai/xgrammar#1015): when a Lark `grammar` constraint is composed into a parser's structural tag (`response_format`/`structured_outputs` with `tool_choice=auto`), it now stays Lark instead of being converted to EBNF without a tokenizer.

## Claims

- `requirements/common.txt` pins `xgrammar == 0.2.9`; the four test lockfiles change only the xgrammar pin and hashes (0.2.9 has the same dependencies as 0.2.8).
- `structured_outputs_to_format` returns `GrammarFormat(grammar=..., syntax="lark")` for a grammar `grammar_is_likely_lark` classifies as Lark, the same test the xgrammar backend uses for a native grammar. The composed tag is compiled by `full_vocab_compiler`, the same compiler as a native Lark grammar, instead of going through a tokenizer-less `Grammar.from_lark(...)` → EBNF round trip, so the composed leaf matches both the native grammar and the Rust frontend (stacked PR).
- 0.2.9 honors `separators=(",", ":")` for commas (mlc-ai/xgrammar#945, fixed by mlc-ai/xgrammar#948), so the FIXME in `XgrammarBackend.compile_grammar` that asked to be removed on this upgrade is dropped and the two commented-out `disable_any_whitespace=True` comma assertions are re-enabled.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py tests/v1/structured_output/ tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
# 568 passed, 2 xfailed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning
# 9770 passed, 15 failed: all in tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py, and the
# same 15 fail on main with xgrammar 0.2.8 in this environment (unrelated)
```

- Red-green: `test_disable_any_whitespace_is_true` fails with xgrammar 0.2.8 and passes with 0.2.9.
- `test_auto_with_lark_grammar` now asserts the composed leaf is `{"grammar": "start: \"ok\"", "syntax": "lark"}` and still checks matcher acceptance through `Grammar.from_structural_tag`.
- Special tokens, at the matcher level with the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer and the Lark grammar `start: "ok" <|im_end|>`: the old conversion raises `named special token <|im_end|> requires tokenizer_info` in `Grammar.from_lark`; the `syntax="lark"` leaf compiles with the tokenizer and accepts `ok` followed by the `<|im_end|>` token. Over HTTP this frontend still stops such a grammar at request validation, before the parser composes it (see Details).
- GPU (GB200, one GPU per server): this PR and its base (`7c9a2fa2b3`, xgrammar 0.2.8) served, with `--structured-outputs-config '{"backend": "xgrammar"}'`, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (`hermes`) and Qwen3.5-0.8B (`qwen3_coder` + `qwen3` reasoning, thinking off), 32 cases per model, each sent greedy, streamed, and with 3 sampled seeds at temperature 1.0 (160 requests per server). On this frontend every case gives the same result before and after: `json_schema`, `json_object`, regex, choice, EBNF, Lark (literal and regex terminals) and `structural_tag` outputs all conform; `tool_choice=auto` with strict tools and a Lark, EBNF or JSON-schema answer yields a schema-valid call for the tool prompt and a call or a conforming answer for the answer prompt in every request; `required`, single-call `required` and named calls are schema-valid.
- The Rust frontend's grammar-replay goldens (80 cases over real model tokenizers) pass through xgrammar 0.2.9 in the stacked Rust PR.
- No model evaluation was run: the change is a dependency bump plus a grammar-leaf representation change, validated at the matcher level.

## Details

- Request validation (`validate_xgrammar_grammar`, also run by `_xgrammar_supports` before composing) still parses a Lark grammar with `Grammar.from_lark` and no tokenizer, so a Lark grammar naming a special token fails it, before and after this PR. With the `xgrammar` backend the request gets `Invalid grammar specification.` (400), natively and with tools. With the default `auto` it falls back to guidance, which accepts it natively; with tools, `_xgrammar_supports` fails first, so no structural tag is built and the tools cannot be called. The xgrammar engine itself accepts the grammar (the Rust frontend, which has no such check, serves it on the same engine). Tokenizer-aware validation is a separate change.
- 0.2.9 also accepts a stop token that completes the grammar (mlc-ai/xgrammar#710). With 0.2.8, `start: "ok" <|im_end|>` masks every token after `ok` and the engine terminates the request (`grammar rejected tokens [0]`); the Rust frontend, which skips the validation above, returned a 500 for it on the base commit.
- With `tool_choice=auto`, non-strict tools and the default `--tool-strict-level`, there is no structural tag and the answer constraint applies alone, so the composed path needs a strict tool or a higher level; unchanged here.
- Other 0.2.9 features (opt-in JIT grammar compilation, jump-forward tokens, `token_markers`, the re-enabled `gemma_4` builtin) are opt-in and not adopted here. The JSON-schema feature gates in `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` stay: their tracking issues (mlc-ai/xgrammar#937, mlc-ai/xgrammar#958, mlc-ai/xgrammar#959, mlc-ai/xgrammar#960, mlc-ai/xgrammar#961, mlc-ai/xgrammar#964, mlc-ai/xgrammar#965, mlc-ai/xgrammar#966, mlc-ai/xgrammar#967, mlc-ai/xgrammar#968) are still open.
- Duplicate check: no open PR bumps xgrammar to 0.2.9 (`gh pr list --search "xgrammar 0.2.9"`, `"xgrammar in:title"`).
- The Rust frontend counterpart is stacked on this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Pool HF fast tokenizers in BaseRenderer so concurrent truncation stays per request
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Renderers that inherit `BaseRenderer` directly (`CohereRenderer`, `DeepseekV32Renderer`, `DeepseekV4Renderer`/`DeepseekV41Renderer`, `InklingRenderer`, `KimiK3Renderer`) share one HF fast tokenizer across the `--renderer-num-workers` thread pool. Concurrent requests with different `truncate_prompt_tokens` can then be truncated to **another request's** length, silently. This PR moves the per-worker tokenizer pool that only `HfRenderer` had into `BaseRenderer.__init__`.

Related: #64034. This is not a duplicate of the closed #64036 / #64412. Those were closed because `tokenizers >= 0.23.2` no longer raises `RuntimeError: Already borrowed`. This PR shows that the race is still there on the supported dependencies (transformers 5.22.0, tokenizers 0.23.3). It no longer raises; it returns wrong token counts.

## Claims

- With `--renderer-num-workers > 1`, every renderer backed by an HF fast tokenizer now tokenizes each request with its own truncation. Before, 16-17% of concurrent requests got another request's `max_length` (no error), see Validation.
- `HfRenderer` keeps the same behavior: it still pools once, but now in the shared base path.
- No slowdown. Tokenization throughput for the affected renderers goes up about 3.6x because workers no longer share one backend.

## Validation

All on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly `dd4e40142a` (transformers 5.22.0, tokenizers 0.23.3). The touched files are unchanged on `main` @ `cb59326aee`, except for an unrelated chat-template hunk in `hf.py`. The new test was also re-run on the `main`-based files.

**Regression test** `tests/renderers/test_tokenizer_pool.py`. Threading events force one ordering of two concurrent requests: LONG sets its truncation, SHORT sets its own, then LONG encodes. Assertions go through the public `tokenize_prompt_async`.

```text
$ pytest tests/renderers/test_tokenizer_pool.py -q
# main (with cohere-melody installed):
FAILED ...test_concurrent_truncation_is_per_request[CohereRenderer]       - assert 128 == 256
FAILED ...test_concurrent_truncation_is_per_request[DeepseekV32Renderer]  - assert 128 == 256
FAILED ...test_concurrent_truncation_is_per_request[DeepseekV4Renderer]   - assert 128 == 256
FAILED ...test_concurrent_truncation_is_per_request[DeepseekV41Renderer]  - assert 128 == 256
FAILED ...test_concurrent_truncation_is_per_request[InklingRenderer]      - assert 128 == 256
FAILED ...test_concurrent_truncation_is_per_request[KimiK3Renderer]       - assert 128 == 256
6 failed, 8 passed            # HfRenderer already pooled, so it passes on main
# this PR (20 consecutive runs):
14 passed
```

**End-to-end, `vllm serve`.** `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, 1x MI300-series GPU, `--renderer-num-workers 8 --enforce-eager`. 2000 `/v1/completions` requests at concurrency 64, each with a ~3000-word prompt and `truncate_prompt_tokens` drawn from {64, 128, 192, 256}. A request is counted wrong when `usage.prompt_tokens` differs from what the same request gets when sent alone. Two runs, base first and then head first:

| `--tokenizer-mode` (renderer) | `main`: wrong / 2000 | this PR: wrong / 2000 |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v32` (DeepseekV32Renderer) | 3, 11 | 0, 0 |
| `kimi_k3` (KimiK3Renderer) | 5, 0 | 0, 0 |
| `auto` (HfRenderer, control) | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |

**Renderer-level throughput.** Real `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` tokenizer, `renderer_num_workers=8`, 2000 `tokenize_prompt_async` calls at concurrency 64, same prompt and lengths as above, 3 runs each:

| Renderer | `main`: secs / wrong | this PR: secs / wrong |
|---|---|---|
| DeepseekV32Renderer | 9.45-9.69 / 342-357 | 2.59-2.76 / 0 |
| KimiK3Renderer | 9.44-10.17 / 316-350 | 2.56-3.21 / 0 |
| HfRenderer | 2.58-2.61 / 0 | 2.56-2.58 / 0 |

**No regressions.** `pytest tests/renderers tests/tokenizers_` gives the same failure set on `main` and on this PR. The only failures are tests that need gated HF repos, which this environment has no token for. GSM8K with `Qwen3-0.6B-FP8` is 0.3935 on both. `vllm bench latency` changes by 1.003x.

Pre-commit: ruff check/format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and check-test-tethering all pass. The new test runs in the existing `pytest -v -s renderers` CPU step.

## Details

**Root cause.** `TokenizersBackend._batch_encode_plus` calls `set_truncation_and_padding(...)`, which stores `max_length` on the shared Rust `Tokenizer`, and then encodes. These are two separate calls. Since tokenizers 0.23.2 the backend is an `RwLock`, so concurrent calls no longer raise `Already borrowed`. Another worker can still set its own truncation between this worker's set and encode, and the encode then uses the other request's length. `HfRenderer` avoided this with `maybe_make_thread_pool`, which gives each worker its own deep copy. Renderers that inherit `BaseRenderer` directly never got it.

**Change.** At the end of `BaseRenderer.__init__`, after the multimodal processor is created, a shallow copy of any `TokenizersBackend` tokenizer that is not already thread-safe is pooled with `renderer_num_workers + 1` copies. This is the same point and the same pool size that `HfRenderer` used. The copy keeps the cached tokenizer instance that was passed in unchanged. `HfRenderer` drops its own call. Non-HF tokenizers (e.g. `MistralTokenizer`) and `skip_tokenizer_init=True` are not touched. Inkling builds its encoding adapter from `self.get_tokenizer()` after `super().__init__()`, so it gets the pooled tokenizer.

**Tradeoff.** Each affected renderer now keeps `renderer_num_workers + 1` deep copies of the tokenizer, the same memory cost `HfRenderer` already pays. #65674 only changes how pool entries are copied in `vllm/tokenizers/hf.py`, which this PR does not touch. It would reduce this cost, and the two PRs do not conflict.

**Test notes.** The configs are dataclass mocks, following the existing renderer tests. The only patched function is transformers' `set_truncation_and_padding`, wrapped to add events that fix the race order. The test does not sleep. Cohere is `skipif` when `cohere_melody` is not installed; it was run locally with it installed.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Attention] Add an mxfp4_mla KV cache for rope-free sparse MLA (read/write path)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. Each 512-wide latent is stored as 256 bytes of E2M1 codes plus 16 inline E8M0 scales (one per 32 values): 272 bytes per token against 1024 for bf16, or 3.76× more tokens per GiB of KV cache.

This is the first of the smaller PRs split out of #59739, as requested there. It contains the cache format, the write path, and a Triton read path for both the ragged kernel and the split-K decode kernel from #58584. Everything is Triton or Python: no HIP or C++ sources, and no new environment variables.

## Claims

- **KV capacity:** 3.76× more tokens per GiB than bf16 (272 vs 1024 bytes per token).
- **Correctness:** attention over the packed cache is bit-identical to attention over the same dequantized values stored as bf16.
- **No change for other KV dtypes.** The only shared-kernel change is a branch on the cache pointer's element type, which Triton resolves at compile time, so the bf16 and FP8 specializations compile to the same code as before.
- **Same serving speed as bf16, no speedup claimed.** The Triton read path unpacks to bf16 before both dots, so the gain is capacity, not arithmetic. End to end on the current head (GLM-5.3-Flash TP=4, 2048 in / 128 out, 16 prompts, concurrency 8, one run per arm): bf16 322.5 output tok/s (median TTFT 1596 ms, TPOT 9.8 ms) vs `mxfp4_mla` 323.9 tok/s (1608 ms, 9.8 ms). An earlier single run on 2026-10-08, on a development tree before the last rebases, showed 195.9 vs 299.3 tok/s; it did not reproduce on the current head, where both arms take the same split-K decode path, so it is not claimed.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (MI355X / gfx950):

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/mxfp4_mla/ tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py
```

`tests/v1/attention/mxfp4_mla/` (plumbing, read, store; 16 passed on gfx950 at 37b843f, CPU-only rerun after the last main merge) covers:
- the format math, checked bit-for-bit against AITER's `per_1x32_f4_quant`;
- the store kernel, including padding slots and launches past 2^31 source elements;
- the Triton read path, checked against a dequantize-then-attend reference, with both the hardware and software unpack;
- the startup plumbing (KV spec bytes, hybrid block sizing, config validation);
- the routing that sends both prefill and decode through the ragged kernel.

**Accuracy** (GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=4 on MI355X, seed 42; both arms served from the same image of this PR's head b7b9232, 2026-10-28):

| Benchmark | bf16 | `mxfp4_mla`, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy) | 96.97% (1279) | 97.04% (1280) |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 questions, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95) | 91.41% (181) | 89.90% (178) |
| RULER NIAH multikey-2, 32K (50 prompts, greedy, string-match recall) | 100% (50/50) | 100% (50/50) |

Neither gap is significant. On GSM8K the arms disagree on 19 of 1319 questions (10 right only with MXFP4, 9 right only with bf16; exact McNemar p = 1.00). On GPQA-Diamond they disagree on 7 of 198 (2 vs 5; p = 0.45), with 2 generations at the token limit in each arm. Both GPQA scores sit in the 88.9–91.9% range of earlier bf16 and MXFP4 runs. These runs include the indexer page-addressing fix #59412 (#58858), now on main; before it, GPQA-Diamond fell to 80.8–85.4% for bf16 and MXFP4 alike on GLM-5.3-Flash.

## Details

**Format and write path.** The `mxfp4_mla` row is 256 bytes of packed E2M1 (low nibble holds the lower index) followed by 16 E8M0 scales. Scales use the round-up exponent, so no value clamps. `MLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` reports the 272-byte row through `state_content_bytes`, and `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` uses the same size so the mamba state still fits one attention page on hybrid models. `concat_and_cache_mla` can't express per-group scales (its `scale` is a single float), so a Triton store kernel behind `do_kv_cache_update` quantizes and writes the row.

**Read path.** The ragged Triton sparse-attention kernel and the split-K decode kernel (#58584) each gain a branch for a uint8 (packed MXFP4) cache, selected by a compile-time `is_mxfp4` flag. It unpacks each gathered tile to bf16 once and feeds both existing `tl.dot` calls:
- On gfx950 the unpack uses the hardware FP4 converter (`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4`) via inline asm.
- On other GPUs it uses a software unpack. The two are tested bit-identical on gfx950, but I haven't run the software path on gfx942.

The decode-only kernels used by DeepSeek-V4 have no MXFP4 branch, so they refuse a packed cache rather than misread it.

## Follow-ups (stacked on this PR)

- A native FP8 × FP4 MFMA kernel for gfx950 that computes attention directly on the packed cache (opt-in).

Separately, two decode-overhead trims that apply to every KV dtype (host-side `paged_kv_indptr` for pure-decode steps, and skipping the NoPE `q_concat` copy) will go up as their own PR against main.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Trim per-chunk and per-request work in the completions stream
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #52875. Three small CPU trims on the `/v1/completions` streaming and request-validation path, no change to any emitted byte or request object.

## Claims

- Plain stream deltas are encoded with one module-level `json.JSONEncoder(ensure_ascii=False)` instead of `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)`, which constructs an encoder on every call (a non-default kwarg bypasses `json`'s cached encoder): 1.6 → 1.06 µs per chunk for text prompts (−32%), identical bytes.
- The prompt text is resolved only in the echo branch instead of on every chunk, for token-id prompts the per-chunk `_extract_prompt_text` call goes away: 2.2 → 1.07 µs per chunk (−51%).
- `_DEFAULT_SAMPLING_PARAMS` on `CompletionRequest`, `ChatCompletionRequest`, `ResponsesRequest`, `TranscriptionRequest` and `TranslationRequest` is declared `ClassVar`, so pydantic stops deep-copying the dict into every instance (17 `copy.deepcopy` calls per request): request validation 17.6 → 10.7 µs (`CompletionRequest`, −38%), 20.1 → 13.7 µs (`ChatCompletionRequest`, −31%), 15.3 → 10.6 µs (`ResponsesRequest`, −31%). `model_dump`, `repr` and `to_sampling_params` are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: searched 2026-11-07 for `JSONEncoder ensure_ascii`, `_DEFAULT_SAMPLING_PARAMS ClassVar`, `_extract_prompt_text stream`, `completion_stream_generator prompt_text` (open and closed) — none. #52875 (merged) added the delta template this refines; #62788 (open) edits the echo branch's token-id handling on different lines.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_text_offset.py \
    tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_stream_frame_template.py -q
# 15 passed
pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py \
    vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/protocol.py vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/protocol.py
# all hooks passed
```

Byte identity: a harness drives the real `OpenAIServingCompletion.completion_stream_generator` with 2000 synthetic `RequestOutput`s and hashes every frame; SHA identical before/after for text prompts and token-id prompts (2002 frames). `model_dump()` and `to_sampling_params()` identical before/after for completion and chat requests with and without explicit sampling fields.

Performance (CPU, macOS arm64 / Python 3.12, 3 alternated runs, 2000 chunks × 7 reps per run; median per run):

| path | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain delta, text prompt | 1.52 / 1.69 / 1.60 µs per chunk | 1.06 / 1.06 / 1.05 | −32% |
| plain delta, token-id prompt | 2.18 / 2.12 / 2.20 | 1.08 / 1.05 / 1.07 | −51% |
| `CompletionRequest(...)` | 18.7 / 17.0 / 17.0 µs | 10.8 / 10.6 / 10.7 | −38% |
| `ChatCompletionRequest(...)` | 20.9 / 19.5 / 19.8 µs | 14.0 / 13.6 / 13.6 | −31% |
| `ResponsesRequest(...)` (1 run) | 15.3 µs | 10.6 | −31% |

Context: on an H100 serving run (Qwen3-0.6B, Python frontend) the API server ran at 126–128% of a core at 4k–14k tok/s. These are per-token and per-request CPU savings on that process; no end-to-end latency change is claimed (the API server was not the bottleneck in that run).

## Details

- `json.dumps(obj, **kw)` uses the module's cached encoder only when every kwarg is default; `ensure_ascii=False` makes it build a `JSONEncoder` per call. For a `str`, both paths reduce to `encode_basestring`, so the output is identical.
- `prompt_text` was computed for every `RequestOutput` but is read only in the `request.echo and not has_echoed[i]` branch, which runs once per choice; it now resolves there from the same inputs (`res.prompt`, else `engine_inputs[prompt_idx]`). The `return_token_ids` case still yields `""`.
- Underscore-prefixed class attributes on pydantic v2 models become private attributes whose default is deep-copied per instance. The dict is read-only (`self._DEFAULT_SAMPLING_PARAMS[...]`, `.items()`), never serialized, so `ClassVar` is the intended declaration.
- No user-visible change; no docs updated.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for profiling, drafting and benchmarking; I reviewed every line and ran every command above and can explain where perf benefit comes from.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Remove compiled models' bytecode hooks at in-process shutdown
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

After an in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) shuts down, its compiled model can stay alive, holding its weights and CUDA graphs. Dynamo's global bytecode-hook registry keeps a bound method of each `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper`, and two bugs leave hooks behind. This PR fixes both: it registers each instance's hook once, and removes the hooks in `GPUModelRunner.shutdown()`.

Refs #21073. #45195 added the hook cleanup and #54162 made its model reference weak; this fixes the two cases they leave uncovered. It is complementary to #60089, which makes `LLMEngine.__del__` call `engine_core.shutdown()`: that shutdown path still drops the model before the finalizer runs.

## Claims

- After an in-process engine shuts down, no bytecode hook remains, so the compiled model and its weights are freed.
- Fixes CI failures like the one in #66523's build: there, a second in-process Qwen3-0.6B engine started with 1.2 GiB less free memory and failed its 0.92 utilization check on a 16 GiB H200 MIG slice.

## Validation

GB200. The cluster can't run current main's flash-attn interface, so these runs use a recent main checkout with this diff applied cleanly.

**New test, `test_llm_delete_inprocess_removes_bytecode_hooks`.** It starts an in-process Qwen3-0.6B engine and checks Dynamo's hook registry during and after it.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Hooks while the engine runs | 2 (test fails: `assert 2 == 1`) | 1 |
| Hooks after shutdown | | 0 (passed) |

**Memory.** Two Qwen3-0.6B engines in one process, same setup. The "this PR" column was measured with the same two changes patched in at runtime, rather than with this diff:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Leftover after the first engine's shutdown | 1.54 GiB torch-allocated: the model's weights, its compile backends and 29 CUDA graphs | weights and graphs freed |
| Across 3 engines in a row | grows by about 1.2 GiB each time | flat |

What stays allocated with this PR is a one-time, process-wide cost (e.g. the FlashInfer workspace), not per engine.

The existing `test_llm_delete_inprocess` fails on this cluster both with and without this PR: 2.05 GiB is still used, against a 2.00 GiB threshold. It is unrelated to this change.

## Details

**Root cause.** The reference chain is `torch._dynamo.convert_frame._bytecode_hooks` → `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper.bytecode_hook` (a bound method) → the compiled module, e.g. `Qwen3Model`. That module holds the weights, and `VllmBackend` → `PiecewiseBackend` → the CUDA graphs. Two bugs keep the chain alive:

1. **Double registration.** When a model class and its base are both `@support_torch_compile`, as `Qwen3Model` and `Qwen2Model` are, `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper.__init__` runs twice on the instance. It registered two hooks but kept only the last handle, so `cleanup()` left one behind. Now the hook is registered only once per instance, and `cleanup()` clears its handle. One hook is enough: it is a bound method of the same instance, so both registrations behaved the same.
2. **The finalizer runs too late.** `LLMEngine`'s finalizer reaches the model through a weak reference (#54162). By then `GPUModelRunner.shutdown()` has already deleted the top-level model. Nothing else references it, so the weak reference is dead and no hook is removed, while the inner compiled module stays pinned by its hook. `shutdown()` now removes the hooks of the target and draft models before dropping them. The finalizer stays as a fallback and uses the same new helper, `remove_bytecode_hooks()`.

With multiprocessing on, the worker process exits and frees everything anyway, so this only matters in-process.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xgy3B5rJEBQ7NUrLWNd5JJ

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Route biased softmax/sigmoid top-k to AITER topk_gating
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

AMD will soon switch to running CI with Aiter enabled.

With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `fused_topk_bias` runs an unclamped plain-torch top-k for softmax + `e_score_correction_bias`, so a NaN or +Inf row gets NaN weights. This routes supported launches to AITER's `topk_gating`, which takes the bias and `routed_scaling_factor` and gives NaN rows finite weights.

## Claims

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py::test_fused_topk_bias_nan_inf_clamp`: the 36 softmax cases that fail under `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` on the base now pass (72 of 72).
- Behavior with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` is unchanged (72 of 72).

## Validation

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py -k bias_nan_inf_clamp
```
results in all test cases passing.

## Details

- `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`: the `rocm_aiter_topk_gating` op, its fake and `rocm_aiter_ops.topk_gating` take trailing `correction_bias: Tensor | None = None` and `routed_scaling_factor: float = 1.0`; existing callers are unchanged.
- The test's own shapes (E <= 16, T = 4) do not hit AITER's duplicate-expert-id bug on rows with fewer than `topk` valid experts. At other shapes, an AITER without the ROCm/aiter#7838 fix can still return repeated ids on NaN rows. This branch does not guard against that.
- No tests are added; the change is covered by the existing test above.
- Overlap, not a duplicate: draft #57246 also edits `fused_topk_bias` and routes the AITER softmax case to the native `vllm_topk_softmax` kernel instead of `topk_gating`. The two touch the same function, so whichever lands second will need a rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cache multi-page Unlimited-OCR-2 requests in the processor cache
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Unlimited-OCR-2 multi-page requests never use the multimodal processor cache. `_cached_apply_hf_processor` still bypasses the cache whenever a prompt has more than one image, a rule that only holds for Unlimited-OCR v1, which turns cropping off for multi-image prompts. #64016 made v2 crop every page independently in `_get_prompt_updates` and `_get_mm_hashes`, but left the bypass unchanged. As a result, pages are reprocessed on every request, and a request that resends cached pages by `multi_modal_uuids` without the image data fails. This applies the bypass to v1 only.

## Claims

- Multi-page Unlimited-OCR-2 requests are cached per page, like single-page ones.
- Resending cached pages by UUID only is served instead of failing.
- Each page's processed tensors are identical whether it is processed alone or with other pages, so caching does not change outputs.
- Unlimited-OCR v1 is unchanged.

## Validation

**Summary** (every number is in the raw output below):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Pages in the processor cache after a 4-page request (CPU) | 0 | 4 |
| Second identical 4-page request, processing time (CPU) | 240.2 ms | 0.3 ms |
| Pages resent by UUID only (CPU and A10) | `ValueError` | served, same tokens and text |
| Unlimited-OCR v1 (CPU) | not cached | not cached (unchanged) |

**New test** (CPU; on main the PR's test file was copied onto `fea3c5ecc7` as `test_uocr_pr.py`):

```text
$ pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/{test_uocr_pr.py on main, test_unlimited_ocr.py on this PR} -k test_v2_multi_page_request_uses_processor_cache -v
# main (fea3c5ecc7)
E           AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'
E           ValueError: Failed to apply UnlimitedOCR2Processor on data={'images': [None, None], 'prompt': '<image><image>'} with kwargs={'truncation': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'}
FAILED tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_uocr_pr.py::test_v2_multi_page_request_uses_processor_cache
================ 1 failed, 21 deselected, 14 warnings in 9.36s =================
```

commits.pr_title: [Perf][mHC] use FlashInfer mega mHC for MHCFusedPostPreOp (GLM-5.3-Fl…
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash's fused mHC step (mHC post + next sublayer's pre + RMSNorm; hidden 4096, four residual streams) now runs as one launch of FlashInfer's fused kernel, `flashinfer.mega_mhc`, wherever a kernel microbenchmark shows it is faster than the TileLang path. There is no new option or env var: a per-architecture token threshold in the op decides.

- Requires FlashInfer with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7024 (hidden-4096 programs) and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7885 (PDL launch), installed with its experimental kernel sources. Both PRs are in 0.7.3, vLLM's current pin, but FlashInfer's PyPI release wheels leave out experimental kernel sources (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7977). So with the PyPI 0.7.3 wheel the kernel can't be built, and the model keeps TileLang. A FlashInfer nightly (https://flashinfer.ai/whl) or source install enables it.
- With such a FlashInfer, on other GPUs or for other shapes, the model keeps TileLang.

## Heuristic

The GLM-5.3 decoder layer compares a step's per-GPU token count T with `min_tokens` (`_MEGA_MHC_MIN_TOKENS` in `models/glm5next/common/model.py`, keyed by compute capability). If T ≥ `min_tokens` it calls the fused FlashInfer op; otherwise it calls the existing TileLang `MHCFusedPostPreOp`.

| GPU | `min_tokens` |
|:--|--:|
| R200 (sm_107a) | 5 |
| GB300 (sm_103a) | 512 |
| others | none (TileLang only, not measured) |

- T is the batch under TP, about batch/DP under DP/DEP, and the chunk in prefill, so one threshold per GPU covers every parallelism.
- The model runs eagerly under CUDA graphs, so T is a concrete int and each captured size records its own branch.

**R200: 5.**
- The fused kernel is one cooperative launch over all SMs with grid-wide barriers, so it costs a flat ~7.7 µs up to ~32 tokens.
- For ≤4 tokens TileLang has a dedicated small-batch kernel (6.3–7.0 µs) and wins.
- From 5 tokens TileLang runs post + TF32 projection GEMM + pre (8.3 µs and up). The fused kernel then wins at every T measured: by 8–25% up to 512 tokens and 32–46% from 1024 (prefill chunks).

**GB300: 512.**
- Both paths cost about 9.7 µs at small T, so the fused kernel has no fixed-cost advantage.
- Below 512 it ties within ±2% at most T, wins clearly only at T=12 and 24–64, and loses 3–4% at T=1, 96 and 256.
- From 512 it wins at every T, by 22–34% from 1024.
- So GB300 uses it for prefill and large decode batches only. A threshold inside the 12–64 band would chase a few percent next to sizes where it ties or loses.

On both GPUs the TP-like and DP/DEP-like runs give the same threshold.

## Kernel microbenchmark

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mhc_flashinfer_mega.py` (added here) times production `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang` (TileLang + DeepGEMM TF32 GEMM) against the fused op at each per-GPU token count from 1 to 8192.
- Each op runs as 100 [predecessor → mHC] pairs in one CUDA graph, timed beyond the predecessor alone.
- Each pair uses its own weight copy, so weights come from HBM as across the 45 layers.
- `--predecessor plain` puts a kernel without PDL in front, which the mHC launch can't overlap. This models TP, after the all-reduce.
- `--predecessor pdl` puts a PDL kernel in front, which it can overlap. This models DP/DEP.
- `--pad-nan K` fills the last K rows with NaN, like CUDA-graph padding.

Each mode ran twice per GPU; the runs agree within 1%. Summary, per-GPU tables and all raw runs: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65521#issuecomment-6774372363

    python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mhc_flashinfer_mega.py --predecessor plain
    python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_mhc_flashinfer_mega.py --predecessor pdl

## End-to-end validation

GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 serving sweeps over 7 configs (agg DEP2/TP4/TP1, disagg 1P TP4 + 1D TP4, and 3P/4P/6P TP1 + 1D DEP4/DEP8), fused vs production. They used same-day pairs and sa-bench 8192/1024. They ran before the thresholds were set from the microbenchmark: TP used the fused kernel from 5 tokens, TP1/DP/DEP from 1 token. Each comment starts with a note on which points the final heuristic changes.

- **R200** (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65521#issuecomment-6748608494).
  - Mean tok/s/user: DEP2 +2.8%, disagg TP4 +2.6%, TP4 +1.2%, TP1 +0.9%. The large-batch DEP4/DEP8 disagg configs were within noise (−0.2% to +0.7%).
  - The final rule changes only DEP2 C1–C8 and TP1 C2–C4, which now run TileLang. Every other point ran the final kernel choice.
- **GB300** (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65521#issuecomment-6749635099).
  - With the old rule, small decode batches lost (DEP2 C1–C32, TP4 C8/C16, TP1). Under the 512 threshold those now run TileLang.
  - Points that still use the fused kernel gained: disagg TP4 decode at C512–C1024, +2.6% to +2.8%. Prefill also still uses it.
- gsm8k was unchanged on both GPUs.
- No FlashInfer JIT build happened after "JIT kernel warmup finished" in any of the 27 R200 runs, each with an empty JIT cache.

**Known limitation.** NaN in CUDA-graph padding rows slows FlashInfer's coefficient math. On R200 the fused kernel goes to ~12.7 µs and loses up to 512 tokens. On GB300 it loses 2–8% at T=3–24. This only affects batches that aren't a capture size, and the op only sees the padded size, so it can't route around it. The R200 TP tables leave out the padded sizes C3/C6/C12.

## Test plan

`pytest -v tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_flashinfer_mega.py`. On R200 with FlashInfer main (f13c875eb): **13 passed**. The tests cover:
- outputs vs a float64 reference, with TileLang's error as the yardstick, T = 1–4096;
- a batch above 64 tokens/SM (several launches, 3-token remainder);
- an in-place weight update reaches the BF16 split;
- CUDA-graph replay after `lock_workspace()` equals eager;
- the JIT warmup covers every program FlashInfer selects;
- other shapes keep TileLang.

CI: the B200 "mHC Kernels" job collects the test. CI installs FlashInfer 0.7.3 from PyPI, which has no experimental kernel sources, so the GPU tests skip there and only the shape test runs. On R200 the same file gives 13 passed with FlashInfer main (f13c875eb), and 1 passed + 12 skipped with the kernel sources removed, matching the PyPI wheel.

## Implementation

- **`kernels/mhc/flashinfer_mega.py`.**
  - The custom op `mhc_fused_post_pre_flashinfer_mega` only runs FlashInfer; it does not call TileLang.
  - `mega_mhc_supported()` says whether FlashInfer has the program for this shape and device, with its kernel sources installed.
- **`models/glm5next/common/model.py`.** The heuristic: `_MEGA_MHC_MIN_TOKENS` per compute capability, `use_mega_mhc` set at construction when the GPU has a threshold and FlashInfer supports it, and the per-step branch in `hc_fused_post_pre`.
- **BF16 split.** The kernel reads the FP32 projection `hc_*_fn` [24, 16384] as three BF16 pieces [3, 32, 16384]. The decoder layer owns them, makes them in `process_weights_after_loading`, and re-splits in place from the params' weight loaders. That keeps captured graphs and weight updates (reload, RL weight sync) correct.
- **Workspace.** Cross-CTA counters, one pair per launch grid, are a `WorkspaceManager` persistent resource. Scratch comes from `get_simultaneous`. Everything is allocated on the first eager call, before `lock_workspace()`.
- **JIT warmup.** `MegaMHCKernel` (`VllmJitKernel`) builds every program FlashInfer can select for T ≤ min(max_num_batched_tokens, 64 × SMs).
- **Chunking.** FlashInfer before flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8199 (0.7.3 included) refuses more than 64 tokens per SM in one launch, so larger batches run as several launches. mHC is per token, so this is exact.

Follow-up: pass the fused kernel's NVFP4 output straight to the NVFP4 MoE (needs a pre-quantized input path in fused MoE).

commits.pr_title: [KVConnector] Allocate the extensible KV cache exportable for EXPORTS_FD (LMCache MP)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Implements `KVCacheAccess.EXPORTS_FD` from #66605: when a KV connector reports it, the extensible KV cache is allocated exportable as POSIX file descriptors. This lets `LMCacheMPConnector` with `"lmcache.mp.use_vmm_api": true` (LMCache/LMCache#6487) run with the extensible KV cache, with the LMCache MP server importing each layer through a file descriptor (LMCache/LMCache#6266).

It replaces #65507, which predates #66605 and carried its own LMCache config parsing; with #66605, vLLM no longer reads any LMCache key, since LMCache's connector declares its own access mode.

## Claims

- A connector reporting `EXPORTS_FD`, directly or as a `MultiConnector` child, gets an extensible KV cache whose physical allocations request the POSIX fd handle type. Every other configuration keeps the current allocation.
- `EXPORTS_FD` requires the extensible KV cache, since LMCache cannot import the torch allocator's cache: vLLM refuses to start when it would be off (`kv_cache_memory_bytes`, `num_gpu_blocks_override`, `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`, ...) or when the VMM probe fails, instead of failing later in LMCache. The probe allocates with the KV cache's handle types.
- POSIX fds and FABRIC are not requested on one allocation, as that pair is unverified (no GB200 with an IMEX channel was available). An fd importer alone gets POSIX on any host. Next to a FABRIC importer (NIXL) on an IMEX host (GB200/GB300), the KV cache gets FABRIC only and LMCache imports it through FABRIC instead, which is unverified too and logged. A rejected FABRIC request falls back to POSIX.
- With LMCache/LMCache#6487, `LMCacheMPConnector` runs with the extensible KV cache when `use_vmm_api` is set, and keeps it off (legacy CUDA IPC) otherwise.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU, GPUs hidden):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest tests/utils_/test_vmm_driver.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py
```

99 passed, 21 skipped, 10 failed. None of the failures involve this change: MoRIIO ×2 (`msgpack` not installed), `test_data_parallel_start_rank_zero_infers_hybrid_lb`, and 7 `test_gpu_worker.py` tests that need a visible GPU (they pass on the H200 below).

GPU unit tests (one H200):

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py \
  tests/utils_/test_vmm_driver.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py
```

166 passed, 1 skipped (`xxhash` not installed), 2 failed: MoRIIO ×2 (`msgpack` not installed). The new `test_only_posix_fd_importers_get_a_posix_fd[False|True]` passes: the driver exports a POSIX fd only from memory created for an fd importer.

The new config tests fail without the fix (code reverted, tests kept, same H200): `test_posix_fd_importer_needs_the_extensible_kv_cache[kv_cache_memory_bytes|disabled]` (DID NOT RAISE `ValueError`), `test_posix_fd_importer_keeps_the_extensible_kv_cache_next_to_nixl` (cache turned off), and `test_extensible_kv_cache_does_not_fall_back_under_a_posix_fd_importer` (DID NOT RAISE `RuntimeError`).

`KVTransferConfig.kv_cache_access()` with LMCache/LMCache#6487 installed (12/12 as expected):

| `kv_connector_extra_config` | direct | MultiConnector child | with / without `kv_connector_module_path` |
|---|---|---|---|
| (default) | `LEGACY_IPC` | `LEGACY_IPC` | same |
| `use_vmm_api: true` | `EXPORTS_FD` | `EXPORTS_FD` | same |
| `use_vmm_api` + `isolated_ipc` | `EXPORTS_FABRIC` | `EXPORTS_FABRIC` | same |

End to end, one H200 per case: an LMCache MP server (LMCache/LMCache#6487, on the same GPU) and `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host":"tcp://127.0.0.1","lmcache.mp.port":16555,"lmcache.mp.use_vmm_api":true}}'`, varied per case as below. Three identical greedy completions of a 4260-token prompt (48 tokens each); vLLM prefix caching is off, so repeats can only hit LMCache.

| Case | Extensible KV cache | fds delivered / layers registered | KV cache | Outputs | External hits / queries |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `use_vmm_api`, direct | on | 28 / 28 | 1,256,960 tokens (19,640 blocks) | 3 identical | 8192 / 12780 |
| `use_vmm_api`, MultiConnector child | on | 28 / 28 | 1,256,960 tokens | 3 identical | 8192 / 12780 |
| `use_vmm_api`, no `kv_connector_module_path` (in-tree resolver) | on | 28 / 28 | 1,256,960 tokens | 3 identical | 8192 / 12780 |
| no `use_vmm_api` | off (legacy CUDA IPC) | — / 28 | 1,172,096 tokens | 3 identical | 8192 / 12780 |
| no `use_vmm_api` + `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` | startup refused: "a KV connector (e.g. LMCacheMPConnector) shares the KV cache through legacy CUDA IPC, which cannot export driver-mapped memory" | | | | |
| `use_vmm_api` + `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 8589934592` | startup refused: "a KV connector (e.g. LMCacheMPConnector with lmcache.mp.use_vmm_api) imports the KV cache through POSIX file descriptors, which needs it, but it sizes the KV cache from measured memory, which kv_cache_memory_bytes overrides" | | | | |

All runs produced the same text. The extensible cases end up with a 7% larger KV cache than the legacy case, because they size the cache from the memory actually free after warmup.

On a GB200 (driver 595.91, CUDA 13.2), in containers without access to an IMEX channel:

- vLLM's `CudaVmmDriver` (this PR) per set of importers, with the real IMEX detection, and with vLLM made to see a channel, which the container then rejects with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`:

  | `export_handle_types` | No IMEX channel | IMEX channel reported |
  |---|---|---|
  | `0` (no importer) | none | FABRIC requested, rejected, none (as on main) |
  | `POSIX` (LMCache) | POSIX, exports an fd | POSIX, exports an fd |
  | `POSIX \| FABRIC` (LMCache + NIXL) | POSIX, exports an fd | FABRIC requested, rejected, POSIX, exports an fd |

  `vmm_unavailable_reason` passes for all three.
- End to end with LMCache `use_vmm_api` alone (on the previous revision, whose allocation here, POSIX without an IMEX channel, is unchanged): 28 fds delivered and 28 layers registered, 1,647,616 tokens, 3 identical outputs, 8192 / 12780 external hits. Legacy mode: extensible KV cache off, same outputs and hits.
- Not verified: anything with a usable IMEX channel (FABRIC-only allocation for LMCache + NIXL, LMCache importing it through FABRIC), and NIXL + LMCache end to end.

## Details

- `VmmDriver.create` / `_make_alloc_prop` take `export_handle_types`, the handle types other processes import the memory through: POSIX from `EXPORTS_FD`, FABRIC from `EXPORTS_FABRIC` (`kv_cache_export_handle_types`), passed through `ExtensibleTensor` and `ExtensibleKVCache`. One bool could not tell LMCache alone from LMCache next to NIXL, and FABRIC availability, and the retry when it is rejected, live in the driver.
- Only NIXL declares `EXPORTS_FABRIC` in tree; Mooncake, Mooncake store, UMBP and MoRIIO declare `REGISTERS`. LMCache next to them gets POSIX only, without the FABRIC handle main would add and they do not use.
- NIXL alone keeps the extensible KV cache off by default without an IMEX channel; next to LMCache it stays on, and NIXL's transfers within a host fall back to TCP (logged).
- `EXPORTS_FD` already needs one physical allocation per segment (`needs_single_chunk`, #66605), so the importer maps each segment from one handle.
- ROCm is unaffected: #66605 turns the extensible KV cache off there for any single-chunk access, which `EXPORTS_FD` now refuses.
- Requirements for users (documented in `examples/disaggregated/lmcache/README.md`): an LMCache release with LMCache/LMCache#6266 and LMCache/LMCache#6487, vLLM and the LMCache server on the same host as the same user with a shared `/dev/shm`, and a TCP server URL (the fd socket path is derived from the port).
- No CI job runs an LMCache server; the new unit tests run in the existing `utils_` and v1 engine/worker steps.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change, its tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Stream MiniMax M3 tool-call arguments
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust MiniMax M3 parser emits each invoke whole when it closes. This PR streams M3 arguments as they are generated, using the shared writer and call state from vllm-project/vllm#66528. It is stacked on vllm-project/vllm#66767, which matches M3's markers by token identity.

## Claims

- The invoke name goes out when the invoke opens.
- A top-level parameter whose schema type is exactly `string` streams as escaped JSON string fragments as its text arrives.
- Any other parameter, nested elements included, is converted through the schema once its element closes: a depth count over element tags finds that close tag in one pass, and the existing element grammar then builds the value once.
- Behavior changes beyond chunking: a genuine child element inside a string parameter is malformed instead of turning the value into an object (a streamed string cannot become an object, and structural tags already exclude it), and a repeated top-level parameter keeps its first value.

## Validation

- New behavioral tests fail on the base and pass here: `minimax_m3_streams_string_parameters_before_the_invoke_closes` (per-chunk progress), `minimax_m3_child_element_in_string_parameter_is_malformed`, and `minimax_m3_ordinary_partial_marker_in_string_parameter_streams_immediately` (an ordinary partial spelling inside a streamed string is not held back). They replace `minimax_m3_streaming_does_not_emit_incomplete_tool_call`, which pinned the old behavior.
- `minimax_m3_streaming_matches_parse_complete_at_every_chunk_size` passes on the base too, by design: it guards the new event loop's chunk invariance rather than marking a behavior change.
- The token-identity tests from vllm-project/vllm#66767 pass unchanged on the streaming parser, including ordinary markup inside a streamed string and inside a buffered nested element, each split at every char boundary.
- The MiniMax M3 roundtrip case, which uses the real tokenizer's namespace token, passes unchanged.
- `cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server`, clippy with `-D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass, apart from `vllm-server`'s `chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample`, which fails the same way in a full-suite run on main and passes when run alone on both.
- Not covered: a run against a real model or engine.

## Details

- M3 takes the same shape as DSML: one `Invoke { call, body }` mode whose position (between parameters, streamed parameter, buffered parameter) changes in place, `match event`, and one delta per event through the shared `OpenToolCall` (`JsonStyle::Spaced`, since the template renders no JSON).
- The existing tolerance for ordinary text at a parameter boundary (drop the rest of the invoke) and the recursion guard are kept. The streamed parameter's close tag is derived from its name; the buffered element scan resumes from an offset plus depth.
- The element scan runs on the shared `scan_markers` over the guarded element start and end markers, so it counts only genuine tags. `scan_markers` now reports which marker it matched (`Scan::Found { at, index }`) and is crate-visible; its existing callers ignore the index.
- A buffered element is parsed from the attributed buffer once the scan has found its close tag (checkpoint, scan, reset), as the base parses a whole invoke.
- Streaming nested string leaves is out of scope: M3 builds nested values retroactively (duplicate child names become arrays), so they are converted whole.
- Complexity: about 269 non-test lines added and 84 removed, 12/8 of them in `utils.rs` and the rest in `minimax_m3.rs`.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Match MiniMax M3 markers by token identity
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust MiniMax M3 tool parser matches its tags by spelling, although the namespace marker `]<]minimax[>[` that begins every M3 tag is an added token. This PR matches M3's markers by token identity, as the DeepSeek DSML (vllm-project/vllm#62875) and Kimi K3 (vllm-project/vllm#58358) parsers do. It was split out of vllm-project/vllm#66531 (streaming M3 tool-call arguments), which now stacks on it.

## Claims

- A tag counts only where the namespace token produced its namespace marker, so the format spelled with ordinary tokens (the model quoting it) stays text: in content, and inside parameter values, nested elements included. Before, such a quote ended the value or the invoke early, made the call malformed, or opened a tool block from content.
- An ordinary partial spelling at the end of content streams at once instead of being held back.
- A tokenizer without the token keeps matching by spelling.
- Otherwise unchanged: each invoke is still buffered to its end and emitted whole.

## Validation

- New tests fail with the markers' token guards removed (spelling-only matching, as on main) and pass with them: `minimax_m3_ordinary_marker_spelling_inside_string_parameter_stays_value` and `minimax_m3_ordinary_marker_spelling_inside_buffered_parameter_stays_value` (each streamed with a split at every char boundary), `minimax_m3_ordinary_partial_marker_streams_immediately`, and `minimax_m3_ordinary_tool_call_markup_stays_text`. `minimax_m3_without_namespace_token_matches_markers_by_spelling` covers the fallback.
- Existing tests now feed token-attributed input through the real incremental decoder. `minimax_m3_finish_fails_partial_outer_end_marker` now cuts the namespace token itself, since a partial ordinary spelling is plain text under token identity, and the recursion-limit test goes through the parser instead of calling `parse_invoke_params` on a string.
- The MiniMax M3 roundtrip case in `vllm-chat`, which encodes with the real tokenizer's namespace token, passes unchanged.
- `cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server`, clippy with `-D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass, apart from `vllm-server`'s `chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample`, which fails the same way in a full-suite run on main and passes when run alone on both.
- Not covered: a run against a real model or engine.

## Details

- Markers follow the DSML parser: `MinimaxM3Markers` resolves the namespace token at creation, guards every marker on it, and builds each element's close tag from the same token.
- The parser buffers `DecodedText` and parses with `parse_buffered_event_attributed`. An invoke is still scanned to its end, now the first genuine invoke-end marker, and its body is then parsed from the attributed buffer rather than from a text slice, so the element grammar also sees token identity.
- Complexity: about 140 non-test lines added and 54 removed, in `minimax_m3.rs` only.
- No other open PR changes the Rust M3 parser's marker matching.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Replace routed-scale bool flags with a RoutedScaleMode enum
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #65842, as suggested by @bnellnm in review.

`FusedMoEFactory` and `MoERunner` took two related booleans: `apply_routed_scale_to_output` and `divide_shared_output_in_fp16`. The second only meant something when the first was set. This PR replaces both with one enum, `RoutedScaleMode`, that says where `routed_scaling_factor` is applied:

| Mode | Old flags | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ROUTER` (default) | `apply_routed_scale_to_output=False` | The scale goes to the router and experts kernel. Grouped top-k folds it into the top-k weights, and some kernels (e.g. ROCm AITER) apply it themselves. |
| `OUTPUT` | `apply_routed_scale_to_output=True` | The runner scales the routed output. |
| `OUTPUT_FP16_GUARD` | both `True` | Like `OUTPUT`, but in FP16 with shared experts the runner divides the shared output instead, and the decoder layer must compensate. Used by DeepSeek-V2/AXK1 non-MHA layers and openPangu. |

All in-tree callers are migrated. The first commit doesn't change behavior.

The second commit fixes a stale check in the Transformers backend. It still assumed any output scaling divides the shared output in FP16, which hasn't been true since #65842. As a result, FP16 MoE blocks with shared experts fell back to routing in Transformers for no reason. It now checks for `OUTPUT_FP16_GUARD`, so those blocks can be fused in FP16 again.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_scale_shared_experts.py`: the runner test covers `OUTPUT` and `OUTPUT_FP16_GUARD` in fp16 and bf16. The DeepSeek-V2/AXK1 MHA decoder-layer test now asserts `RoutedScaleMode.OUTPUT`. There's a new check of `RoutedScaleMode.scales_output`.
- `pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_moe.py`
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py`: same result before and after on CPU (the CUDA-only cases fail on Mac either way).
- Every changed module imports on CPU, except the two that need CUDA to import at all (`dots3_note/nvidia`, `minimax_m3/amd`). Those compile, and they fail the same way on unmodified `main`.

## Test Result

- `test_routed_scale_shared_experts.py` + `transformers/fusers/test_moe.py`: 41 passed (Mac, CPU).
- `test_moe_layer.py` + fuser tests: 228 failed / 38 passed / 265 skipped both before and after the change (CPU; failures are the existing CUDA-only cases).
- GPU: not run locally; relies on CI (`kernels/moe`, L4 + MI300).

## Notes for reviewers

- `apply_routed_scale_to_output` and `divide_shared_output_in_fp16` are removed rather than deprecated. They're internal kwargs of `FusedMoEFactory`/`MoERunner`, and every in-tree caller is migrated. Out-of-tree models that pass them would break; happy to add a deprecation shim if preferred.
- The second commit (Transformers backend) is a small behavior change. It can be split into its own PR if preferred.
- The Transformers backend only ever uses `ROUTER` or `OUTPUT`, so after the second commit its `divides_shared_output` guard is always `False`. I kept it on purpose as a fail-closed check: Transformers decoder layers don't compensate, so if the backend ever picks `OUTPUT_FP16_GUARD`, fusion falls back instead of silently mis-scaling the output.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Pad the AITER MLA decode head count to a native tile
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Pads the AITER MLA decode head count up to one that AITER runs natively. DCP-gathered counts such as 48, 80 and 112 otherwise fold into 16-head pseudo-batches, and each pseudo-batch reads the KV cache again. The pad target comes from `aiter.get_mla_decode_shape_support` (ROCm/aiter#6107), which is in AITER v0.1.27. vLLM pins v0.1.27 since #63774. Padding is always on; there is no new env var.

Based on main `c1d8fade8d`. 3 files, +357/-15: `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py`.

## Claims

- **Faster decode for folded DCP head counts.** MLA decode kernel time on MI355X (gfx950), AITER v0.1.27, fp8 Q and KV, qlen 1, LSE on:

  | Pad | Batch 52, 16K KV per request | Batch 8, 8K KV |
  |---|---|---|
  | 48→64 | 274.3 → 112.9 us (**2.43x**) | 107.6 → 54.9 us (1.96x) |
  | 80→96 | 360.7 → 180.4 us (**2.00x**) | 105.5 → 57.6 us (1.83x) |
  | 112→128 | 586.6 → 185.7 us (**3.16x**) | 106.6 → 58.1 us (1.84x) |

- **No head-count table in vLLM.** The target comes from the installed AITER. For example, 96 heads is native on gfx950 fp8 at qlen ≤ 6, so 96 stays at 96 for K ≤ 6 and pads to 128 only when the group also has non-causal blocks at qlen 7 or 8.
- **Only folded counts change.** bf16 is never padded, and neither are 16 or fewer heads or counts AITER already runs natively, so for example DeepSeek-style 128 heads at TP1/2/4/8 (16/32/64/128 per GPU) is unchanged. On gfx950 fp8 the query gives 40/48→64, 80→96 and 112→128.
- **Older or failing AITER keeps working.** If the query is missing (AITER < v0.1.27) or raises, the builder logs once and keeps main's head count.

## Validation

All runs on MI355X (gfx950).

**End-to-end.** The model is `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite` with dummy weights, overridden to 48 heads and 4 layers, run at TP2 with DCP2 (48 gathered heads), fp8 KV and CUDA graphs on. 8 prompts of 1500 tokens each generate 48 greedy tokens. Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-40941f2c4ba96fba0a7e282a5355e89cd74d9ac5`, with its own AITER v0.1.27 and this branch's Python on top.

| Run | Head count launched | Result |
|---|---|---|
| This PR | 64 (logs "padding 48 decode heads to 64") | 5/5 completed |
| main `c1d8fade8d` | 48 (folded) | 1 completed, 1 died with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` |

An earlier round on 10-23 used AITER at the #6107 merge commit, whose MLA code is identical to v0.1.27. The padded decode completed 8/8. The unpadded 48-head decode faulted in 5 of 8 runs (main, and this branch with padding disabled). The fault is in main's folded 48-head DCP decode; padding avoids it. That config has no speculative decoding, so cprr is not involved.

**Unit tests.** Run on GPU in the same image, with its AITER v0.1.27, PR vs main:

| Test file | This PR | main `c1d8fade8d` |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` | 85 passed | 73 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` | 30 passed | 30 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` | 63 passed, 597 skipped | same |
| 18 other ROCm AITER MLA files (head_padding, dcp_cprr_numerics, decode, decode_metadata, fp8_support, fp8_prefill, op_registration, causal_verify_mask, sink, sparse_metadata_sync, candidate_mask, fp8_decode_routing, uniform_mtp_qo_len, dcp_context, backends_selection, expand_page_indices, triton_sparse_mla, `tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py`) | same counts as main | 816 passed, 4 skipped |

- The 12 extra passes in `mtp_split` are the new tests.
- The 597 skips in `test_mla_backends` are cases whose `ROCM_AITER_FA` prefill backend is unavailable in the image. The 4 skips in `dcp_context` need 2 GPUs (each run had 1).

**Kernel numerics.** These runs go through `AiterMLAHelper` pad/unpad (fp8 Q and KV, LSE on, qlen 1), with the target chosen by the real query. Each padded run is compared with the unpadded run, and both are compared with an fp32 reference. "Native" is a real 64/96/128-head problem with no padding, a control for the kernel's own error. The table shows mean relative error.

| Case | Padded vs unpadded | LSE max abs diff | Unpadded vs ref | Padded vs ref | Native vs ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 48→64, B=1, ctx 8K | 1.03e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 9.69e-3 | 9.06e-3 | 9.01e-3 |
| 48→64, B=8, ctx 1K | 2.05e-2 | 4.8e-7 | 1.86e-2 | 1.71e-2 | 1.71e-2 |
| 48→64, B=52, ctx 4K | 1.56e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 1.36e-2 | 1.49e-2 | 1.39e-2 |
| 48→64, B=16, ctx 16K | 8.46e-3 | 9.5e-7 | 7.84e-3 | 8.63e-3 | 8.80e-3 |
| 80→96, B=1, ctx 8K | 1.08e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 9.76e-3 | 8.94e-3 | 8.96e-3 |
| 80→96, B=8, ctx 1K | 2.11e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 1.88e-2 | 1.71e-2 | 1.71e-2 |
| 80→96, B=52, ctx 4K | 1.45e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 1.37e-2 | 1.32e-2 | 1.32e-2 |
| 80→96, B=16, ctx 16K | 8.40e-3 | 9.5e-7 | 7.92e-3 | 7.67e-3 | 7.66e-3 |
| 112→128, B=1, ctx 8K | 1.09e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 9.80e-3 | 8.96e-3 | 8.94e-3 |
| 112→128, B=8, ctx 1K | 2.15e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 1.89e-2 | 1.70e-2 | 1.70e-2 |
| 112→128, B=52, ctx 4K | 1.48e-2 | 9.5e-7 | 1.37e-2 | 1.32e-2 | 1.32e-2 |
| 112→128, B=16, ctx 16K | 8.86e-3 | 9.5e-7 | 7.95e-3 | 7.64e-3 | 7.65e-3 |

- **Not bit-identical.** The padded run uses a different kernel. LSE agrees to within 1e-6.
- **80→96 and 112→128.** Padded error vs the reference is at or below unpadded at every shape.
- **48→64 at long KV.** At B=52/ctx 4K and B=16/ctx 16K, padded error is slightly above unpadded. It matches the native 64-head control, so the extra error is the 64-head kernel's, not the padding's. See Limitations.

**Lint.** `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes all hooks, including ruff, ruff-format, typos, mypy and the Buildkite test-wiring check.

## Details

**Why the fold is slow.** When AITER's persistent MLA decode gets a head count it does not run natively, the metadata planner folds the heads into `num_heads / 16` pseudo-batches of 16. Each pseudo-batch reads its request's KV range again. Decode is KV-bandwidth bound, so 48, 80 and 112 heads read the cache 3, 5 and 7 times. Padding Q with replicated heads, and slicing the extra heads off afterwards, reads it once.

**Why the AITER query.** Whether a head count is native depends on the arch, the Q and KV dtypes, the head count and `max_seqlen_qo`. Whether a kernel exists also depends on LSE and causality, and the answer has changed between AITER releases. A wrong guess aborts the process on the first decode. The padded count also sizes the persistent buffers and is captured in CUDA graphs, so vLLM must know it at init. `get_mla_decode_shape_support` answers from the same C++ rules the planner uses. Its defaults (`persistent`, `fast_mode`, `page_size=1`, no `cp_world_size`) match the launch it is asked about.

**Target selection.** The padded count is the smallest multiple of 16 that the query reports `native` and `supported is True` at every shape the plain decode launches. The search runs from the aligned count up to 2x it, capped at 128. If no count fits, if the aligned count is ≤ 16, or if the query is missing or raises, the aligned count is kept, which is main's behavior.

**Design**

- **One count per run.** `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.__init__` resolves the padded count once, because it sizes the persistent buffers and is captured in CUDA graphs.
  - **Buffer sizing.** The buffers are sized for both the padded count and the existing count (cprr's count when cprr is on) at every decode qlen, using the per-qlen sizing from #63116. AITER's buffer needs are not monotonic in the head count: a folded 48 can need more than a native 64.
  - **Planning and launch.** The plain route plans `get_mla_metadata_v1` at the padded count. `AiterMLADecodeMetadata.padded_num_heads` carries it to `forward_mqa`, which pads q and unpads o and lse with it.
- **Which shapes are queried.** Only the plain persistent asm decode is padded. `resolve_padded_mla_num_heads` queries the `(qlen, return_lse, causal)` shapes that route can launch:
  - **Under DCP:** causal qlen 1 with LSE. Causal qlen > 1 takes cprr, segmented or Triton, including #62990's right-aligned adaptive verification.
  - **Without DCP:** causal qlen 1..K.
  - **Groups with non-causal multi-token blocks:** non-causal qlen 1..K as well.
- **Buffer sizing also fixes a main bug.** With DCP and cprr, main sized the shared buffers for cprr's count only, but also planned the plain decode's count into them. At 112 plain / 128 cprr, a guard region showed writes past `reduce_indptr` and `reduce_final_map`. Sizing for both counts removes that.
- **The fp8 non-causal qlen-2 guard** checks the count the batch launches at. A padded 64/96/128 block is no longer refused because of its unpadded 48/80/112.
- **Unchanged routes.** cprr runs at its own native count. Segmented, Triton, Gluon and non-persistent batches run at the aligned count, as on main.

**Limitations**

- **No opt-out.** There is no env var to turn padding off. If AITER's query reports a shape as native that its kernel then mishandles, the affected configs need an AITER fix or downgrade.
- **AITER's native 64-head fp8 kernel is not deterministic at long KV.** At batch 52/ctx 4K and batch 16/ctx 16K, repeated runs on identical inputs give different outputs. 1–10 of 3,328 rows reach up to ~0.26 max relative error, always in heads 32–63. This happens on AITER 0.1.26 and 0.1.27 alike, and 96 and 128 heads are clean. It already affects every model with 64 decode heads, and it affects 48→64 here: real heads 32–47 land in that range. To be reported to AITER separately.
- **Kimi-K3 fused q-prep (DCP1 only).** The fused decode writes q into a buffer sized at the aligned count. A padded count makes `get_mla_padded_q` copy q once per MLA layer instead of viewing it. Output is unchanged; the copy costs a little of the gain.
- **Conservative shape set.** Groups with non-causal blocks query every qlen 1..K, so padding may be refused because of shapes the scheduler never produces.
- **gfx942 is untested.** No MI300 was available. The target follows whatever the query reports there.
- **Speed-ups are kernel measurements.** The only end-to-end number is the earlier 96→128 Kimi-K3 run on AITER 0.1.19 (DCP8/TP8, conc 52): 459 → 169 us per MLA layer, median ITL 52.7 → 43.3 ms.

**Pre-existing issues on main, not addressed here**

- **Folded 48-head DCP decode crashes.** Main's folded 48-head plain DCP decode intermittently hits `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` (see End-to-end). The root cause is not identified. With AITER ≥ v0.1.27 this config pads to 64 and no longer takes that path; with an older AITER it still does.

**Tests** (12 cases in `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`; no new file, no Buildkite change)

- `test_resolve_padded_mla_num_heads` (4): target selection against a fake query. Covers 48→64, the 2x cap, 96→128 with non-causal blocks, and 16 never padding. Under DCP, causal groups query only qlen 1 with LSE.
- `test_resolve_padded_mla_num_heads_without_a_working_query` (2): a missing query and a query that raises both keep the aligned count.
- `test_padded_plain_decode_plans_at_the_padded_count` (2): plain plans at the padded count and cprr at its own.
- `test_padded_plain_decode_unpads_output_and_lse` (1): a 48-head decode padded to 64 comes back at 48 heads, in order.
- `test_builder_sizes_metadata_for_the_padded_head_count` (2): with 64 native, the builder sizes for 48 and 64 at every qlen; with nothing native, for 48 only.
- `test_a_two_token_fp8_block_is_allowed_when_padded_to_a_fold` (1): a 48-head fp8 non-causal qlen-2 block padded to 64 is planned at 64 instead of being refused.

The builder test stubs that replace `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.__init__` now also set `non_causal_multi_token_decode`, which the real init always sets and the padding search reads. This affects two tests in `mtp_split`, including #63116's, and one in `dcp_cprr`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM-5.3] DeepGEMM BF16 MegaMoE for unquantized checkpoints
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3's MegaMoE path (#60895) only took the block-FP8 checkpoint. An unquantized (BF16) GLM-5.3 checkpoint now runs DeepGEMM's `bf16xbf16` MegaMoE: the `MEGA_MOE_BF16` row of the shared MegaMoE layer from #61538, with the shared expert fused and the weights loaded as they are. The switch is the same: `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` with TP1 x DP + EP.

## Claims

- glm-5.3-bf16 (a BF16 GLM-5.3 checkpoint), DEP8 on 8x B200, `vllm bench serve` at concurrency 128, against the default BF16 MoE path (FlashInfer TRTLLM):
  - prefill 8192/1: **+40%** total tok/s;
  - decode 1024/1024: **+13.6%** output tok/s.
- GSM8K matches the default path.
- No change for the block-FP8 checkpoint or any other `moe_backend`. Other quantized checkpoints still raise.

## Validation

8x B200, DEP8 (TP1, DP8, EP), no MTP, prefix caching off, fp8 KV cache, `max-num-batched-tokens` 8192, `max-num-seqs` 64. Both arms ran on the same node and container, one run each, and differ only in `moe_backend`. The default resolves to FlashInfer TRTLLM unquantized MoE (`TrtLlmBf16ExpertsMonolithic`).

Code: nightly `40941f2c4b` with #60895 and this change applied, plus unrelated patches this configuration does not exercise (no MTP, no KV connector). The GLM MegaMoE code this PR touches is identical to main apart from docstring style.

| workload (in/out) | metric | default (FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16) | MegaMoE BF16 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 8192 / 1, 768 prompts | total tok/s | 134,903 | **189,329** (+40.3%) |
| | TTFT mean / p99 | 7.16 / 7.83 s | 5.06 / 5.70 s |
| 1024 / 1024, 512 prompts | output tok/s | 6,357 | **7,221** (+13.6%) |
| | TPOT mean / p99 | 19.3 / 20.4 ms | 17.1 / 17.5 ms |
| | TTFT mean | 0.86 s | 0.61 s |
| | GPU KV cache per rank | 9.71 M tokens | 10.03 M tokens |

GSM8K, lm-eval 0.4.12, 5-shot, chat template, 1,319 questions, temperature 0:

| | default | MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | 0.9553 ± 0.0057 | 0.9560 ± 0.0056 |
| strict-match | 0.8059 ± 0.0109 | 0.7961 ± 0.0111 |

strict-match is equally low on both arms. The cause is the model's answer format, not the backend.

`pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py`: 6 passed. Without this change, the new BF16 test fails with a `TypeError` from the block-FP8 scale path.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <glm-5.3-bf16> --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode glm5_next --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'
# default arm: --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}'

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 768 \
  --num-warmups 64 --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42
# decode: --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 512

lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048 temperature=0.0 do_sample=False \
  --model_args "base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_gen_toks=2048"
```

</details>

## Details

- **Format selection.** `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` uses `MEGA_MOE_BF16` when the checkpoint has no `weight_block_size`. It registers the block-FP8 scale staging only for FP8.
- **Loading.** BF16 shards go straight into the kernel layout through the shared layer's loader, so there is nothing to requantize after loading. `finalize_mega_moe_weights` only requantizes block FP8.
- **Shared expert.** It is fused exactly as for FP8: `mlp.shared_experts.{gate,up,down}_proj` load into the BF16 `shared_l1`/`shared_l2` and run in the same launch.
- **Precision.** Dispatch stays BF16 with no activation quantization, so the experts run at the checkpoint's precision.
- **MTP.** The MTP layer uses the same class. These runs did not enable MTP.
- **CI coverage.**
  - The new test runs in the `GLM5Next` unit-test job. Like the existing tests there, it uses CPU tensors and bypasses the SM100 check.
  - End-to-end runs need SM100 and a BF16 checkpoint, so they are outside CI.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4/4.1] Enable Tensor scale FP8 KV Cache for Sparse MLA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Adds per-tensor FP8 KV-cache support (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) for DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 on ROCm gfx950, served by AITER's sparse MLA kernel. The cache stores plain 512-element FP8 rows instead of the packed `fp8_ds_mla` record, which remains the default. Requires AITER with ROCm/aiter#7429 (`4e91c7ea6`) or later. ## Claims - **New KV-cache format** for DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 on gfx950. Each token is stored as a plain `[448 NoPE | 64 RoPE]` FP8 row with one per-tensor scale. Both the sliding-window and the compressed caches use it. - **No accuracy regression** on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash or DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 in GPQA Diamond, gsm8k, MMLU or NIAH. - **12.5% more KV-cache capacity** in the same memory: 512 instead of 584 bytes per token. - **Up to 7.6% higher output throughput** (TP2/TP4, spec decode). The gain is largest at 8K/1K with C≥16 - **Top-k change,** which also affects the existing packed path. - The V4 / V4.1 packers counted the valid top-k entries but copied only that many leading columns. - A row like `[a, -1, b]` became `[a, -1]`: a negative slot ended up inside a live `indptr` range, and the valid key `b` was dropped. - The packers now compact valid entries in order. ## Validation **Unit tests (MI355X):** ```bash pytest -v -s tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py ``` - These cover top-k compaction for all three packers, including holes, padded rows and CUDA-graph replay. They also check the fused output epilogue (inverse RoPE, MXFP8) against the standalone passes for packed and plain caches, with bf16 and FP8 queries. - All pass. The compaction test fails on the parent commit. - CI: `tests/v1/attention` runs in the MI355 DPX "V1 Attention" job. **Accuracy** (MI355X, AITER `5361651c0`). The two arms differ only in `--kv-cache-dtype`. packed: --kv-cache-dtype fp8 ``` **Client**, one per point: ```bash vllm bench serve --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((10 * C)) --request-rate inf --seed $SEED ```
Accuracy setup - **V4.1-Flash, TP4:** DSpark 5 drafts with `rejection_sample_method: block`, prefix caching off. - **V4-Pro-0813, TP4:** the perf recipe above with DSpark 6 drafts, `rejection_sample_method: block` and `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. - **GPQA Diamond:** simple-evals prompt, effort max, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, 262,144 max tokens, 4 repeats. - **gsm8k:** 5-shot, effort high. - **MMLU:** generative, 5-shot, thinking off. - **NIAH:** RULER multikey, 100 cases at 8K–256K, thinking off.
## Details - **Format.** With `fp8_e4m3`, the layer registers the same `_flashinfer_fp8_*` scale buffers as FlashInfer, so the shared SWA insert, compressor and DSpark writers work unchanged. The buffers start at 1.0; this PR doesn't add scale calibration. - **Writes.** The V4 head-512 compressor, in both its single-stage and two-stage kernels, gains a plain-FP8 row store that applies GPT-J RoPE to the last 64 dimensions. FP8 saturation comes from `torch.finfo(kv_cache.dtype).max` rather than a hardcoded 448. - **Attention.** `_plain_fp8_sparse_mla` passes the SWA cache as the main segment and the compressed top-k cache as the extra segment. - It runs with `qk_rope_head_dim=0` (RoPE lives inside the 512-wide row), `dot_precision="fp8"` and `has_invalid=False`. - The store epilogue applies inverse RoPE, and on V4.1 it writes MXFP8 output directly. That removes V4.1's BF16 workspace and its separate rotate and quantize passes. - `rocm_aiter_ops.triton_sparse_mla_fwd` gains an optional `dot_precision`; other callers keep the existing default. - **Why the compaction is needed.** `has_invalid=False` lets AITER stage K straight into LDS, but it requires every slot inside a live `indptr` range to be valid. The prefill and SWA builders already compact. The decode top-k packers did not, which caused the bug described under Claims. The cost is +0.4–2.2 µs of metadata build at K=512–2048, with no extra launches or allocations. - **Prefill gate.** A plain FP8 cache always takes the AITER sparse MLA prefill, because gather + OPUS only decodes the packed record. The SWA metadata builder applies the same rule, so DeepSeek-V4-Pro at more than 64 heads per rank (TP1) gets its prefill indices. - **Limitations.** - The format requires gfx950 and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1`. - It is rejected together with KV-transfer connectors, which disable the AITER route. - `--monokernel`'s whole-layer path still reads only `fp8_ds_mla`. With `fp8_e4m3`, those layers use the FFN launch only. - **Duplicate check.** I searched the open vLLM PRs for DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 FP8 KV cache, sparse MLA and top-k compaction work on ROCm, and none adds this format. The related PRs are #60076 and #66283 (KV-only DSpark insert), #64120 (MXFP4 compressed KV) and #60583 (GLM-5.3 FP8 KV on gfx942). - **AI assistance.** AI tools (Codex, Claude Code) helped write parts of the code, the tests and the validation runs. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above. ## Supporting Data ## Top-K compaction Effect on Performance **For _pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel** | Rows (T) | DSv4-Pro C4
topk 1024, bs 64 | DSv4.1-Flash ratio 2
