commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] AITER FA: trim the sliding-window decode table with fewer ops
commits.pr_body: ## Overview Cut the ROCM_AITER_FA sliding-window decode-table trim (`_build_swa_decode_tables`, q == 1 decodes) from 10 GPU ops to 7 per call, with byte-identical results. The trim runs eagerly on every decode step for each sliding-window KV-cache group, and it is launch-bound, so this saves about 16 us of host time per call (about 28%). This PR started as an opt-in trim of the block table for spec-decode verify (q > 1), which only paid off with a window-bounded AITER split. AITER instead merged a window-aware split, ROCm/aiter#6889 (`b6c376cfa6`). Its split covers only each sequence's window tiles, so an untrimmed verify table gets the same split as a trimmed one, and the verify trim would only add ops. That part and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_FA_SWA_VERIFY_TRIM` are dropped. vLLM main already has that split: it pins AITER v0.1.29 (#66596), which includes ROCm/aiter#6889. ## Changes - `_build_swa_decode_tables`: the clamp runs in place; the int64 cast is dropped (`_swa_block_offsets` is int64, so adding it already promotes the gather index); the rebased seq lens are written straight into the persistent buffer with `torch.sub(lens, first_block, alpha=block_size, out=...)` instead of a temporary plus `copy_`. Ops per call: `sub, clamp_, floor_divide, add, clamp_, gather, sub` (was `sub, clamp, floor_divide, _to_copy, add, clamp_, gather, mul, sub, copy_`). - `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa.py`: fix an out-of-bounds read in `test_aiter_paged_decode_over_window_trimmed_block_table_matches_reference`. It passed a `query_start_loc` of `num_seqs` entries, but `paged_attention_v1` reads entry `i + 1` to skip rows whose query length is not 1 (AITER `csrc/cpp_itfs/pa/pa.cuh:88-89`). The last row's check read whatever the allocator left past the tensor, and when that was not `num_seqs` the kernel skipped the row and left its output uninitialized. On main the leftover value happens to be right. With this change's fewer temporaries it is not, and the test failed deterministically on MI355X (last row wrong, 920/6144 elements). The test now passes `num_seqs + 1` entries sliced to `num_seqs`, as the backend does with `query_start_loc[:num_decodes]`. The backend call itself was never affected. ## Performance MI355X, one GPU, block size 16, contexts random in [1, 32768]. Per-call time: 2000 back-to-back calls with one sync at the end, best of 5. Kernels and GPU time: `torch.profiler` over 200 calls. | window | decodes | before (us/call) | after (us/call) | saved | kernels | GPU time (us) | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 128 | 1 | 57.6 | 41.5 | 27.9% | 10 → 7 | 13.8 → 10.1 | | 128 | 32 | 58.4 | 42.1 | 27.9% | 10 → 7 | 14.4 → 11.8 | | 128 | 512 | 58.8 | 42.3 | 28.2% | 10 → 7 | 19.2 → 15.7 | | 2048 | 1 | 58.8 | 42.4 | 28.0% | 10 → 7 | 13.8 → 10.7 | | 2048 | 32 | 58.2 | 41.8 | 28.1% | 10 → 7 | 17.9 → 15.1 | | 2048 | 512 | 59.3 | 42.5 | 28.3% | 10 → 7 | 20.0 → 16.1 | The 6 shapes not shown (decodes 8, 128 and 256) are within the same range: 27.9-29.6% saved. No change when spec decode is on: the trimmed table is built only for q == 1 decode batches. ## Accuracy MI355X, AITER 0.1.29, vLLM nightly `f5d93296`, whose `rocm_aiter_fa.py` is identical to main's. Main is the image as is; the PR side mounts this PR's `rocm_aiter_fa.py` over it. - **Helper:** the trimmed table, seq lens and max seq len are bitwise equal to the previous formula. CPU: 560 random cases, windows 16-4097, contexts up to 3x the window, blocks 16 and 32. GPU: the 12 shapes above. - **Kernel tests:** the three cases that build and use the trimmed table passed 3 of 3 runs on both main and this PR: - `test_aiter_paged_decode_over_window_trimmed_block_table_matches_reference`: window 256, including a window start inside a block. - `test_aiter_fa_shared_kv_matches_reference[mixed-*-False-16]`: metadata builder, `forward()`, then `paged_attention_v1`, with bf16 and fp8 KV. The whole file gives 121 passed on both sides. - **End to end:** Qwen3-0.6B forced to an all-sliding 512-token window (`hf_overrides` `sliding_window: 512`, every `layer_types` entry `sliding_attention`), `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`, CUDA graphs on (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE). Greedy GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 questions, prompts up to 850 tokens. - Main and this PR produced identical output tokens for 1319 of 1319 questions, with both bf16 and fp8 KV, in two runs each. - The trim dropped blocks in 514 decode steps with bf16 KV and 517 with fp8 KV. - The score is the same on both sides (0.6%) but is not meaningful: a full-attention model loses the start of the prompt under a forced window. - **Real sliding-window model:** `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` (window 512, head 256, 5 sliding layers per global layer), `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`. The `unsloth` copy is used because `google/gemma-3-1b-it` is gated. - Greedy GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 questions: main and this PR produced identical output tokens in every configuration. The trim dropped blocks in about 1,980 decode steps per run. - `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_correctness_sliding_window.py` (Gemma cases, ROCM_AITER_FA forced) gave the same answers on main and this PR. `test_sliding_window_retrieval` with the hybrid KV cache manager on, and `test_hybrid_kv_cache_manager_output_equivalence`, pass on both. `test_sliding_window_retrieval[disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager=True]` fails on both with the same wrong answer: 4 of 5 correct, where the test requires 5 of 5. So that failure is on main too. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Remove CUDA-only dependencies from Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH attention
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Make the Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH attention path (#64016) run on non-CUDA Triton backends (validated on Intel XPU). It hard-coded two CUDA-only dependencies. Also skip the FlashInfer test cases where FlashInfer is not installed.

## Claims
- Fix `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_MODULE_UNLINKED` on XPU when the DASH `_rope` Triton kernel loads during warmup.
- Fix `ImportError: vllm.vllm_flash_attn requires the CUDA flash attention extensions` in `flash_dash_attention` on XPU.
- `test_unlimited_ocr.py` skips the `FLASHINFER` cases when FlashInfer is unavailable, instead of failing with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flashinfer'`.
- `test_unlimited_ocr2_excess_markers_survive_preemption` pins `block_size=16` so `num_gpu_blocks_override=80` produces preemption again. On XPU it failed with `assert 0 > 0` on `vllm:num_preemptions`. ( #63231 makes the default block size to 64 and 16 was the original block size; so this change matches the original test case)
- CUDA behavior is unchanged. Both replacements resolve to the same CUDA symbols and functions as before.

## Validation
All runs on Intel Arc Pro B60 passed as shown below:

```bash
pytest -sv models/multimodal/generation/test_unlimited_ocr.py

====================== 8 passed, 8 skipped, 2 warnings in 423.14s (0:07:03) =======================
```

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K2 FFN seam at TP4 / TP8
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**Stacked on #64152, which is stacked on #63893 and #63027. Only the last commit, `3e7bf14c49`, belongs to this PR.**

On gfx950 (MI355X) at TP4 and TP8, K2's FFN seam and the FFN launch's seam now use the tuned seam that #63027 wrote for its TP2 compress-ratio-2 layers. The MoE route also loads its bias before it polls the logits. Outputs stay bit for bit the same as the generic seam's. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with TP4 `--monokernel`, the decode step is 144 us shorter at c1 (-2.8%) and 449 us shorter at c4 (-5.3%).

### Stacking (review only the last commit)

Fork branch `okorzh-amd/vllm:okorzh/dsv41-mono-tuned-k2-seam`, head `3e7bf14c49`, on main `4b47db922b`:

| Commit | From | Must land first |
|---|---|---|
| `96fa04ad7a`, `043dd8da90`, `37372f010c` | #63027 (tuned TP2 ratio-2 builds), rebased onto main | yes |
| `3d923a6848` | #63893 (tuned K1 at TP4) | yes |
| `0cc5f92bd5` | #64152 (tuned K1 at TP8) | yes |
| **`3e7bf14c49`** | **this PR** | |

#63893 has since been force-pushed to `d47af6ce62`. That push rebases its commit, and #63027's three commits under it, onto main `913fccd118` and trims comments. #63027's own PR head is still `d104a70f8d`. #64152 and this branch still sit on `3d923a6848`, and this branch will be rebased when #64152 is.

## Claims

- **Decode step at TP4 (measured):**
  - Setup: 4x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87. 4-round ABBA against the stack without this commit.
  - Results: c1 **-144 us (-2.83%)**, c2 **-80 us (-1.26%)**, c4 **-449 us (-5.35%)**.
  - Every round is faster at every concurrency. Each mean is larger than t x SE and larger than the base A/A spread, the rule #63893 states.
- **Outputs bit for bit unchanged (measured, at the tested shapes):**
  - The numerics test compares the whole layer (K1 + K2) bit for bit against a `generic=True` runner at TP4 and TP8, at 6-48 rows. It now compares the FFN launch the same way.
  - The test passes on MI355X. It is not vacuous: a mutant that scales half of the tuned seam's fp32 TP sums by 1 + 2^-7 (1-2 bf16 ulps) fails it. With the mutant in K2, the whole-layer compare fails; with it in the FFN launch, the new compare fails.
- **Accuracy within noise (measured):** GSM8K with every decode-only step on mono goes from 0.9199 to 0.9165 (McNemar exact p = 0.20, 6 paired passes). AL goes from 3.5785 to 3.5810.
- **Scope:**
  - The gate is fixed at build time, with no env var. `MonoBuild.tuned_seam` equals `tuned_front`: gfx950, not `generic`, TP4 or TP8, plus the TP2 ratio-2 builds, which already had this seam.
  - It selects the tuned seam for the target's K2, the DSpark draft's K2 and the FFN launch, and it turns on the route's early bias load.
  - K2's attention back half, the router and the rest of the MoE stay generic.
  - TP2, gfx942 and `generic=True` builds compile the same code as before. This is inferred from the gate; those builds were not recompiled. The scratch layout does not change.
- **TP8:** checked only by the bit compare and the CI cases. There is no TP8 end-to-end A/B.

## Validation

**Unit tests (measured).**
- Image `kog:seam2`: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-335dd77b09`, with its mono package and `mono_decode.py` replaced by this branch's files (byte-identical).
- The nightly lies between main `4b47db922b` and `67d677bdef`, and that range has no mono changes.

```bash
# 4x MI355X: the commands of the mi355_4 CI step
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py  # [2] [4] PASS; [8] (8 GPUs) and the gfx942 test skip; 230 s
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py    # [2-8] [4-8] PASS; [4-42] (gfx942), [8-8] [8-28] (8 GPUs) skip; 402 s
# 8x MI355X: the ids of the mi355_8 CI step (run here in one session; CI runs them as 2 commands)
pytest -v -s "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py::test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[8]" \
  "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]" \
  "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-28]"   # 3 PASS; 592 s
```

- **Test change:**
  - Since #63893 and #64152, `_check_layers` compares K1 + K2 bit for bit against the `generic=True` runner at TP4 and TP8, so it already covers K2's tuned seam.
  - When `build_key(M, 0).tuned_seam` is set, the test now also runs the FFN launch on both runners. It asserts that the outputs and the normed scratch are `torch.equal`.
  - `ffn_kernel` now passes `generic`, so the reference FFN launch is a generic build.
  - Cases, as (ratio, requests x tokens): (1, 1x6), (0, 1x7), (2, 2x6), (2, 6x6), (2, 8x6). That is 6, 7, 12, 36 and 48 rows.
  - Then come 300 CUDA-graph replays. Each replay is asserted bit-identical to the first run, so run-to-run noise cannot make the bit compare flaky.
- **Mutant controls** (`test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[4]`):
  - The mutant multiplies `acc0` in `reduce_slice_quad` (half of the tuned seam's fp32 TP sums) by 1 + 2^-7 before the bf16 rounding.
  - One build puts the mutant in K2 only, another in the FFN launch only.
  - **K2 mutant:** FAILS the whole-layer compare.
  - **FFN mutant:** passes the whole-layer compare and FAILS the new FFN compare.
  - Both fail at the first case, `ratio 1, 1 x 6`.
- **CI:** any change under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/` triggers these steps:
  - `test_areas/models_basic.yaml` runs exactly the ids above in `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics` (mi355_4) and `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics TP8` (mi355_8).
  - `test-amd.yaml` has only the 4-GPU step, and it is marked optional.
  - The MI300 gfx942 mono steps also run: `models_basic.yaml` on mi300_4 and `kernels.yaml` on mi300_1. They build gfx942 code that this commit leaves unchanged, and they were not run here.

**Decode step A/B (measured)**

| 4x MI355X, TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, AV off, synthetic AL 3.87 | base (stack) | this PR | delta, mean of 4 rounds | per round (E1 / E2 / E3 / E4) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| c1 step, 7 rows (ITL p50) | 5.084 ms | 4.940 ms | **-144 us (-2.83%)** | -135 / -142 / -152 / -147 us |
| c2 step, 14 rows | 6.317 ms | 6.238 ms | **-80 us (-1.26%)** | -67 / -86 / -79 / -86 us |
| c4 step, 28 rows | 8.404 ms | 7.955 ms | **-449 us (-5.35%)** | -466 / -388 / -471 / -472 us |

- **Noise:**
  - t x SE of the mean round delta (t = 3.18, 3 df): 12 / 15 / 65 us at c1 / c2 / c4.
  - Base A/A spread of the round means: 15 / 36 / 66 us.
  - All 2,304 requests completed, with 0 engine faults.
- **Design:**
  - Both arms run at the same time, one TP4 server per GPU half. The halves swap between rounds, 2 rounds each way.
  - Each server runs a warm-up, then 3 runs x {c1, c2, c4} x 32 prompts: random 32k in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`.
- **Images:**
  - Base `kog:stack`: the nightly plus the stack's mono package (`0cc5f92bd5`).
  - This PR, E3/E4: `kog:seam2`.
  - This PR, E1/E2: `kog:seam`, built from the pre-fix tree `9d5ccb4509`. That is a local commit that was not pushed. Its mono package and test equal this branch's earlier push, `7a52eda806`, except for one README paragraph.
  - From the pre-fix tree to this branch, the mono diff changes only comments, an equivalent body of `tuned_seam`, the generic runner's FFN build and the test. 11 sampled production builds have identical `gpu.binary` hashes on both trees (list below).
  - Mean deltas, E1/E2 vs E3/E4: c1 -139 / -149 us, c2 -76 / -83 us, c4 -427 / -472 us.

**Accuracy (measured).**
- Setup: GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy, real (block-rejection) acceptance.
- Each arm ran on 2 servers, with the GPU halves swapped. Each server ran 3 passes: one cold, then two with a per-request `cache_salt`.
- Accuracy is the number correct over 6 x 1319 questions. AL is 1 + accepted / drafts for each pass, averaged over the 6 passes.

| | base | this PR | delta | McNemar exact p (base-only vs PR-only correct, paired by round and pass) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `--parallel 6`, this branch. 6 x 7 = 42 rows <= 48, so every decode-only step runs on mono | 0.9199 / AL 3.5785 | 0.9165 / AL 3.5810 | -0.0034 / +0.0025 | 0.196 (216 vs 189) |
| `--parallel 8`, pre-fix tree. 8 x 7 = 56 rows > 48, so a step with all 8 requests decoding runs off mono (inferred from the cap; not counted) | 0.9158 / AL 3.5824 | 0.9177 / AL 3.5814 | +0.0019 / -0.0010 | 0.488 (196 vs 211) |

Over all 12 paired passes: 412 vs 400, p = 0.70.

**Static checks.**
- CPU compile (FlyDSL `COMPILE_ONLY`, gfx950, pre-fix tree): 140 TP4 and TP8 production builds compile, with LDS at most 142,368 B. The only spill, TP4 K2 at 14 rows, already exists on the unmodified stack. Details below.
- `pre-commit` passes on the 5 changed files.

**Layer microbenchmark (measured; the script is not in this PR).**
- Setup: TP4, 7 rows, 40 K1 + K2 launches per HIP graph.
- Result: -2.40 to -3.00 us per layer over 3 runs in both GPU orientations. The output digests of the two arms are equal.
- The table and the stage timeline are below.

<details>
<summary>CPU compile, build hashes, microbenchmark and stage timeline, A/B noise, GSM8K per pass, reproduction</summary>

**CPU compile.**
- **Builds:** K2 (ratio 0/1/2, the index-source and DSpark-draft variants) and the FFN launch, at TP4 and TP8. Rows: M = 1, 6, 7, 12, 14, 21, 28, 36, 42 and 48.
- **Spills:** no build spills or uses scratch except TP4 K2 at 14 rows. Its 5 target variants use 255-256 VGPRs, with 4 spilled and a 20 B private segment.
  - The unmodified stack has the same 4 spills and 20 B in the 2 variants compiled there (ratio 0, and ratio 2 with the index source), at 255 VGPRs.
  - #63892 reports removing this spill on its own base.
- **Against the unmodified stack:** 4 TP4 K2 builds were compiled on both trees: ratio 2 at 7 and 12 rows, and at 14 rows ratio 0 and the ratio-2 index source.
  - LDS is unchanged in all 4 (96,640 / 109,408 / 121,408 B).
  - VGPRs are unchanged, except the 14-row index source, which goes from 255 to 256.
  - No width above 16 rows, where the seam's `red` grows, was compiled on the base.

| build (gfx950, this PR, M = 1-48) | TP4 VGPR | TP8 VGPR | LDS (B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| K2, target (ratio 0/1/2, index source) | 231-256 | 232-250 | 96,640-142,368 |
| K2, DSpark draft | 171-207 | 163-199 | 96,640-134,480 |
| FFN launch | 232-248 | 232-249 | 43,408-142,368 |

**Build hashes:** 11 of 11 sampled production builds are identical between the pre-fix tree and this branch. The comparison uses the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `gpu.binary`.
- TP4: K1 (7 rows, ratio 2); the FFN launch (7 rows); K2 at 7 rows (ratio 0, 1, 2, the ratio-2 index source, draft), at 14 rows (ratio 1) and at 28 rows (ratio 2).
- TP8: K2 at 7 rows (ratio 2) and at 28 rows (ratio 1).

**Layer microbenchmark.**
- Setup: TP4, 7 rows (1 request x 7 DSpark tokens), pre-fix tree.
- Method: 40 K1 + K2 launches in one HIP graph, cycling 8 random weight sets so that the weights stream from HBM. Each value is the minimum over 5 batches.

| run | ratio | base (us / layer) | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| base on GPUs 0-3, PR on 4-7 | 1 | 93.47 | 90.47 | -3.00 (-3.2%) |
| PR on 0-3, base on 4-7 | 1 | 92.99 | 90.59 | -2.40 (-2.6%) |
| PR on 0-3, base on 4-7 | 2 | 92.37 | 89.79 | -2.58 (-2.8%) |

- Within a run, batches differ by 0.10-0.18 us.
- The 4th run (ratio 2, base on GPUs 0-3) failed in setup with `ValueError: Duplicate layer name`, before any kernel launch. The timeline builds in that orientation show -3.3 us at both ratios.

**Stage timeline** (timeline build of the benchmark above; one sample per arm, base on GPUs 0-3 and PR on 4-7):
- Each value is the time at which the last CTA passed that point, in us after K2's first CTA started.
- The last row is the whole layer, measured from K1's start.

| point | ratio 2 base | ratio 2 PR | ratio 1 base | ratio 1 PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| wo_b done | 18.84 | 18.39 | 18.54 | 18.36 |
| reduce + slice | 25.36 | 25.19 | 26.29 | 24.88 |
| 2nd seam loop (base: gates; PR: norms) | 29.41 | 25.96 | 30.23 | 25.54 |
| seam end, after a barrier (base: after norms; PR: after gates) | 29.57 | 29.58 | 30.39 | 29.11 |
| MoE x quant | 31.62 | 29.74 | 32.42 | 29.27 |
| router | 33.72 | 31.21 | 34.59 | 30.59 |
| route | 36.33 | 34.24 | 37.33 | 33.35 |
| K2 end | 77.28 | 74.86 | 79.85 | 76.32 |
| K1 + gap + K2 | 91.48 | 89.03 | 94.15 | 90.92 |

- From wo_b done to route done: 17.5 -> 15.9 us at ratio 2, and 18.8 -> 15.0 us at ratio 1.
- x quant waits on the norms. It finishes 1.9 us earlier at ratio 2 and 3.2 us earlier at ratio 1.

**A/B noise.**
- Within one server, the run-to-run SD is at most 14 us at c1, 29 us at c2 and 69 us at c4.
- PR A/A spread of the round means: 19 / 56 / 83 us.
- Worst PR run vs best base run:
  - c1: 4.957 vs 5.073 ms;
  - c2: 6.294 vs 6.291 ms (they overlap by 3 us);
  - c4: 8.032 vs 8.324 ms.

**GSM8K per pass** (the binomial SE of one pass is about 0.0075)

| run | arm | accuracy per pass | AL per pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--parallel 6` | base | 0.920 / 0.915 / 0.923 / 0.920 / 0.926 / 0.917 | 3.560 / 3.585 / 3.573 / 3.578 / 3.582 / 3.593 |
| `--parallel 6` | this PR | 0.915 / 0.914 / 0.920 / 0.915 / 0.913 / 0.922 | 3.587 / 3.573 / 3.573 / 3.584 / 3.581 / 3.587 |
| `--parallel 8` | base | 0.926 / 0.904 / 0.920 / 0.920 / 0.915 / 0.911 | 3.584 / 3.574 / 3.592 / 3.572 / 3.590 / 3.583 |
| `--parallel 8` | this PR | 0.918 / 0.916 / 0.920 / 0.912 / 0.921 / 0.919 | 3.600 / 3.577 / 3.576 / 3.565 / 3.586 / 3.584 |

**Reproduction**

```bash
# One server per GPU half (4x MI355X each). For accuracy, use "rejection_sample_method":"block"
# and drop synthetic_acceptance_length.
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \
  --block-size 128 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'

# Warm-up: c2, 4 prompts, 32k in / 256 out, seed 7. Then 3 runs per conc; the step is ITL p50.
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
# c2 / c4: --max-concurrency 2 / 4 with --seed 102 / 104.

# GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt, stops and scoring over /v1/completions; 1319 questions,
# 8-shot, temperature 0, max 512 new tokens, 6 (or 8) in parallel. One cold pass, then two passes
# with a unique "cache_salt" per request.
# AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total), from /metrics.

# CPU compile: COMPILE_ONLY=1, ARCH=gfx950; build_mono_k2 / build_mono_ffn of
# MonoBuild(M, tp, ratio, index=..., fold=True). Draft builds: experts=128, topk=3, ug_groups=1, swa_width=192.
# Read vgpr_count, vgpr_spill_count, group_segment_fixed_size and private_segment_fixed_size from the kernel metadata.
```
</details>

## Details

**What the tuned seam does differently.** All of this is #63027's existing code. `tuned_seam` now selects it in `run_ffn`, `build_mono_k2` and `build_mono_ffn`.
1. **Reduce fused into the slice** (`stage_reduce_slice`, `reduce_slice_quad`, `slice_rest`):
   - Each thread takes 4 columns of a token through the TP sum (in rank order), R_new of the 4 streams and the layer input, all in registers.
   - The residual, the comb/post/pre mixes and the `hc_fn` weights are loaded before the poll on the TP partials.
   - Before, the generic reduce polled, stored to `pend_lds` and hit a barrier, and only then did the slice load its operands.
2. **`slice_mix_all`:** it runs every token tile's mix MFMAs, then one barrier, then every tile's wave sums.
   - That is 2 barriers per slice task instead of 2 per token tile.
   - The seam's LDS `red` is sized for all tiles (`_seam_lds(s, key.tuned_seam)`). Up to 16 rows the size is the same.
3. **Tuned `stage_norm`:**
   - `norm_w` is loaded before the row's wait.
   - The 3 chunks are polled in one batch of 12 pairs instead of 3 serial polls.
   - Each thread writes its 8 normed values with one 16-byte store (`store_normed(wide=True)`) instead of 8 bf16 stores.
   - There is no tail barrier; the publish's drain provides one.
4. **Norms before gates:** the MoE waits on the norms, and nothing in the launch waits on the gates. Past 16 rows (more than one router group), the gates run on the route CTAs after the route (`after_route`).
5. **Early bias** (`stage_route`): the routing bias is loaded before the logits poll. #63027 does this under `MoeBuild.tuned`. Here `cb["early_bias"]`, a build-time bool, turns it on while the MoE stays generic.

The arithmetic and its order do not change. Only loads, polls, stores, barriers and the stage order move, and the bit compares check that.

**Gate.**
- **Separate name:** `tuned_seam` returns `tuned_front`. It has its own name so that K2's seam and K1's front each have their own gate.
- **What stays off:**
  - `BackBuild.tuned` and `MoeBuild.tuned` still come from `MonoBuild.tuned`, which is TP2 ratio 2 only. So at TP4 and TP8, K2's tuned back half and the tuned MoE stay off.
  - In particular, the router's gate weights still load after the wait on x (`router_task_weights` is used only under `MoeBuild.tuned`).
- **CUDA graphs:**
  - #63893 notes that a TP4 tuned K2 hung during FULL capture in an earlier experiment.
  - This commit turns on only the seam and the bias.
  - The 300 graph replays at TP4 and TP8, and all 8 PR servers (CUDA graphs on), finished without a hang.
- **`ffn_kernel` now passes `generic=self.generic`:**
  - Before this commit, the FFN launch never took a tuned path: it builds at ratio 0, where `tuned` is false, so ignoring `generic` did not matter.
  - With `tuned_seam`, ignoring it would have made the generic runner's FFN launch tuned too, and the new compare could not fail.
  - Only test runners set `generic`.
- **TP8 poll:** this commit builds the tuned seam's TP poll at TP8, which #64152 noted was not built. It is 8 specs of 2 pairs, one batch under `POLL_MAX = 12`. So the TP8 poll-batch fix that #64152 left out is not needed.

**Motivation:** keep operands in flight before each wait, as in Kog AI's [MI300X single-kernel engine write-up](https://blog.kog.ai/building-a-single-kernel-latency-optimized-llm-inference-engine-on-amd-mi300x-gpus/). At TP4 / TP8, K2's FFN seam and the route's bias still issued their loads after their polls.

**Limitations and coverage gaps**
- **The FFN launch never ran end to end:**
  - With this config every layer takes the whole-layer path; the server logs list no FFN-launch layers.
  - The FFN launch serves only layers whose attention the kernels do not take: another KV cache dtype or indexer, or a compressor without an indexer.
  - The unit bit compare is its only check.
- **Not bit-compared on GPU:**
  - the DSpark draft's K2: at TP4 its only check is the GSM8K AL at `--parallel 6`, and at TP8 nothing checks it;
  - the index-source K2: only the layers test checks it, within tolerance;
  - 14 and 28 rows, the c2 and c4 widths: layers `[8-28]` checks 28 rows at TP8, within tolerance.

  The >16-row path (gates after the route) is bit-compared at 36 and 48 rows.
- **TP8 performance is not measured.** TP8 takes the same code as TP4. Its builds compile with no spill, and they pass the bit compares and the 300 replays.
- **Per-width gains not explained (not profiled):**
  - c4's -449 us is larger than the 7-row microbenchmark suggests. At 28 rows, `slice_mix_all` saves two barriers and the gates run after the route.
  - c2 gains less than c1 (-80 vs -144 us) with twice the rows. 14 rows is the TP4 K2 width that spills, in both arms.
- **Scaling estimate (inferred):** 18 ratio-2 layers x 2.58 us plus 20 ratio-1 layers x 2.40-3.00 us gives 94-106 us, against the 144 us measured at c1. The 2 ratio-0 layers and the K2 of the 3 draft layers were not benchmarked.
- **Repeated prompts:** each perf run reuses its prompts (seed 100 + c), so runs 2 and 3 hit the prefix cache during prefill. The metric is the decode step, which this does not affect.

**Related PRs**
- **#63027, #63893, #64152:** the stack. Some of their statements become partly stale, because with this PR K2's seam is tuned at TP4 and TP8:
  - "K2 stays generic", in #63893 and #64152;
  - "At TP8 the tuned seam's TP poll is not built", in #64152.
- **#61934** issued the same static loads early on the generic seam. It was closed with "No e2e gain observed". This PR also takes #63027's fused reduce + slice, the one-batch norm poll, norms before gates and `slice_mix_all`, and it has the 4-round end-to-end A/B above.
- **#63892 / #64153** (TP4 / TP8 K2: batched X8 copies, push peer bases loaded late):
  - #63892 edits `run_ffn` at the `cb["x_cm"], cb["x_ready"]` line, where this commit adds `cb["early_bias"]`. #64153 carries the same edit through the #63892 commit it is stacked on.
  - That is the one textual conflict this commit adds; keep both lines.
  - #63892's removal of the 14-row spill was measured on its own base, not with this commit.
  - Their gains were measured separately and may not add up.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Exclude FlashInfer autotune peak from KV cache sizing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Exclude the one-off FlashInfer autotune peak from the extensible KV cache's transient reserve while preserving the peaks before and after tuning. Addresses the startup regression in [#66193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66193), introduced by [#56492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492).

## Claims

- Keep FlashInfer autotuning enabled without reserving its tactic-profiling scratch peak throughout serving.
- Preserve the profiled activation reserve and transients from warmup before and after autotuning.
- Restore startup for the reported Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 MTP3 workload on a 32 GB RTX 5090 at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`.

## Validation

The accounting patch was tested on the two pinned vLLM versions below, as recorded in [#66193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66193). This branch additionally initializes the saved worker field to zero, matching the patch's existing fallback and satisfying type checking. These are existing GPU measurements, not new runs of this branch, which is based on `2aca74f916`.

Single RTX 5090, `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, MTP3, max model length 36,000, concurrency 1, FlashInfer autotune enabled; one run per arm:

| vLLM base | Unpatched reserve / KV cache | Patched reserve / KV cache | Unpatched → patched startup | Patched output tok/s: 2k/128 / 2k/1000 + 32k shared prefix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dd4e40142` | 3.83 / 1.51 GiB | 1.79 / 3.56 GiB | ValueError → passes | 66.1 / 33.7 |
| `4fab5a074` | 3.83 / 1.46 GiB | 1.79 / 3.51 GiB | ValueError → passes | 68.5 / 36.2 |

Startup reproduction, run against each unpatched and patched wheel:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 36000 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --speculative-config.method mtp --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 3 \
  --cudagraph-capture-sizes 4 8 16 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --load-format runai_streamer
```

The patched server completes both benchmark scenarios. The classic-sizing comparison on `dd4e40142` measured 69.0 / 28.8 output tok/s; these single runs do not establish a throughput improvement. Full benchmark details and the environment report are in the issue.

The warmup module is byte-identical between this branch's base and `4fab5a074`; the worker's `_compile_or_warm_up_model` method is also unchanged apart from line offsets. A fresh GPU run of this branch and model accuracy evaluation remain outstanding. Higher concurrency, TP > 1, other GPUs, and other model families have not been validated for this fix.

## Details

The extensible cache sizes its reserve from the allocator peak over warmup. FlashInfer autotuning profiles candidate tactics using temporary scratch buffers, so its peak can exceed the memory needed by the selected tactics during serving. Charging that peak inside an explicit utilization budget leaves too little KV capacity even when the device has free memory.

Before tuning, save `allocated_bytes.all.peak - allocated_bytes.all.current`. After tuning, collect garbage, synchronize, and reset the peak counter. At the existing reserve calculation, take the maximum of the saved transient, the later warmup transient, and the existing profiled reserve. Cleanup and synchronization occur only during startup with the extensible cache enabled. Later warmup still exercises the selected tactics before cache sizing and CUDA graph capture.

This does not remove persistent allocations or change the memory budget. The two 16,384-token configurations discussed in #66193 still fail because retained non-KV allocations consume their budgets. Other autotuning steps are unchanged.

Duplicate checks on 2026-11-07 found no open PR referencing #66193 or implementing this fix. Related [#54209](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54209) and [#54479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54479) address compilation peaks during initial memory profiling; [#55828](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55828) addresses accounting for other processes. This patch targets FlashInfer tuning during the later extensible-cache warmup window.

AI assistance was used: the patch and original GPU investigation were prepared with Opus; Codex prepared this branch, reviewed the integration, and drafted this description. Human line-by-line review and confirmation of validation are pending before submission.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][MiniMax-M3] Add FlashInfer MSA backend for SM90 and SM120/SM121
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a FlashInfer `msa_ops` backend for MiniMax-M3 sparse attention (lightning indexer + block-sparse attend) on Hopper (SM90) and consumer Blackwell (SM120/SM121). Today these GPUs run the Triton fallback; the vendored MSA kernels are SM100-only.

Supersedes #48994 (SM120/SM121 only, by @yichengj0, whose commits are kept here) and adds SM90. Requires FlashInfer 0.7.3 (pin bump in #65930); on older FlashInfer the feature probes keep the Triton path, so merge order does not matter.

## Claims

- **Kernel level (H100, MiniMax-M3 TP8 shapes):** one sparse layer (indexer + attend) is 1.02-2.13× faster on decode under CUDA graphs, 2.6-5.6× on prefill and 3.5-5.0× on mixed decode + prefill steps.
- **End to end (8× H100 and 8× H200, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP8 with MTP, concurrency 1-10):** ITL p50 9-22% lower and TTFT p50 3-19% lower than the Triton path, with GSM8K accuracy unchanged.
- **SM120/SM121:** indexer and attend match the Triton/reference paths (validated on RTX 5080 in #48994).
- Selection is automatic: configurations FlashInfer does not support keep the Triton pair.

## Validation

**Kernel level.** Single H100 80GB, one MiniMax-M3 sparse layer per TP8 rank. Layer = indexer (proxy score + top-k) + attend. Times are medians in µs.

Problem shape:

| parameter | value |
|---|---|
| query / KV / index heads per rank | 8 / 1 / 1 (TP8) |
| head dim (attention and index) | 128 |
| KV cache and index cache | fp8 E4M3, page size 128 |
| top-k blocks / local window | 16 / 1 |
| max model len | 1,048,576 (8192-column page table) |
| KV pool | 32,768 pages |
| decode | 4 query tokens per request (MTP verify), timed as CUDA graph replay |
| prefill and mixed | eager |

Decode (N requests × 4 query tokens, each at the given context length):

| requests | context | Triton | FlashInfer | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8k | 19.4 | 13.6 | 1.42× |
| 8 | 8k | 28.8 | 18.0 | 1.60× |
| 48 | 8k | 113.6 | 61.5 | 1.85× |
| 1 | 32k | 24.2 | 13.9 | 1.74× |
| 8 | 32k | 45.3 | 25.5 | 1.77× |
| 48 | 32k | 172.4 | 113.5 | 1.52× |
| 1 | 128k | 33.4 | 16.2 | 2.06× |
| 8 | 128k | 89.3 | 64.1 | 1.39× |
| 48 | 128k | 391.1 | 312.8 | 1.25× |
| 1 | 512k | 55.6 | 38.1 | 1.46× |
| 8 | 512k | 228.9 | 197.0 | 1.16× |
| 48 | 512k | 1271.0 | 1101.2 | 1.15× |
| 1 | 1M | 79.1 | 62.2 | 1.27× |
| 8 | 1M | 406.6 | 370.9 | 1.10× |
| 48 | 1M | 2308.4 | 2118.0 | 1.09× |

The full grid (1/4/8/16/32/48 requests × 1 or 4 query tokens × 8k-1M context) ranges 1.02-2.13× and is never slower.

Prefill and mixed steps:

| step | Triton | FlashInfer | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 1 × 8192 tokens, no prefix | 1693.7 | 300.3 | 5.64× |
| prefill 1 × 8192 tokens + 32k cached prefix | 2280.3 | 804.9 | 2.83× |
| prefill 1 × 8192 tokens + 128k cached prefix | 3306.1 | 1069.6 | 3.09× |
| prefill 1 × 8192 tokens + 1016k cached prefix | 13050.5 | 3024.0 | 4.32× |
| prefill 8 × 1024 tokens + 32k cached prefix | 2194.5 | 810.5 | 2.71× |
| prefill 32 × 256 tokens + 32k cached prefix | 2190.6 | 856.3 | 2.56× |
| prefill 32 × 256 tokens + 600k cached prefix | 8133.0 | 2615.3 | 3.11× |
| mixed: 8 decode (4 tokens @ 128k) + 1 × 2048 prefill | 1668.0 | 335.4 | 4.97× |
| mixed: 32 decode (4 tokens @ 128k) + 1 × 2048 prefill | 1837.2 | 527.9 | 3.48× |

Numerics vs the Triton pair on identical inputs: attend rel-L2 ≤ 3.4e-3; top-k rows 87.5-100% identical on decode and ≥ 99.4% on prefill, differences being ties between equal-score blocks.

**End to end.** MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on 8× H100 and 8× H200: TP8, fp8 KV and index caches, MTP (3 draft tokens), prefix caching, agentic multi-turn traces at concurrency 1-10, against the same build with the FlashInfer path disabled. ITL p50 is 9-22% lower and TTFT p50 3-19% lower at every concurrency on both GPUs. GSM8K (400 questions) is unchanged within noise: 96.75% vs 96.25% (H100), 96.50% vs 97.25% (H200).

**Tests.** `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py`: on H100 with FlashInfer 0.7.3 from PyPI, `-k flashinfer`: 11 passed, 11 skipped (bf16 caches and the NHD layout, which SM90 does not serve); whole file: 129 passed, 98 skipped (other-arch cases), 0 failed. SM120/SM121 parity: see #48994 (RTX 5080).

The kernel-level and end-to-end runs used a FlashInfer source build whose SM90 `msa_ops` sources are identical to the 0.7.3 release.

**CI.** The new tests run in the existing kernel-attention job but skip on GPUs other than SM90/SM120/SM121 or without FlashInfer ≥ 0.7.3. The selection-predicate test is CPU-only and always runs.

## Details

- **One selection predicate.** `minimax_m3_use_flashinfer_msa()` is computed once per layer and feeds both the indexer and the attend selectors. The two FlashInfer impls share the top-k buffer in a layout the Triton pair does not use, so a mixed pairing must never happen.
- **Indexer.** One `msa_proxy_score` + one `msa_topk_select` call per step for the whole batch (no decode/prefill split). Each token's causal extent and local window go into the top-k kernel as per-token `num_valid_pages` / `force_end_blocks`, so there is no per-token masking in Python.
- **Attend.** The kernels read vLLM's paged KV cache in place (K/V views split from the packed cache); fp8 descales fold into the softmax scale and the output scale. On SM90 the kernels write into `out=`, and the backend requests the head-major `LBHNC` layout they read.
- **SM90 support.** FlashInfer takes fp8 E4M3 main and index caches, bf16 activations, top-k 16, GQA groups 8 or 16 (MiniMax-M3 at TP1-TP8), and 1, 2 or 4 index heads per rank. Everything else stays on Triton.
- **Feature probes** in `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py` (`has_flashinfer_msa*`) detect each required FlashInfer capability. FlashInfer exposes no flags for SM90 support or per-token top-k bounds, so those two are detected from the op signatures.
- **Workaround:** on SM90, FlashInfer 0.7.3's `msa_proxy_score` can read up to 127 rows past the end of `q` on prefill steps, which can fault when `q` ends at the edge of its allocation. On SM90 prefill steps the indexer pads `q` (one small copy per prefill step); this goes away once FlashInfer fixes the read.
- **Not included:** preloading FlashInfer's SM90 top-k JIT kernels at warm-up. Without it, the first prefill/mixed step of a new shape compiles once (1-2 s, then served from FlashInfer's disk cache). The only preload hook is a private FlashInfer API, so this is left for a follow-up.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Fuse native BF16 ReLU2 with NVFP4 quantization
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse native BF16 ReLU2 with NVFP4 quantization for Nemotron shared experts on SM10x. Removes one launch and the BF16 intermediate; reuses the consumer from [#59612](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59612), with no GEMM changes.

## Claims

- **24–31% lower activation/quantization latency at 2K–4K tokens; 13–20% lower including the down-projection GEMM.**
- Bit-exact packed values and live scales, with existing activation/LoRA fallbacks preserved.

## Validation

**Revision `462744b0`, GB200, Nemotron shared-expert dimensions** (K=5376, N=4096). Ordinary native compiler settings, warm CUDA graphs; eight paired samples per shape:

| Tokens | ReLU2 + quantization (µs) | Including down GEMM (µs) | Component speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2.56 → 1.54 | 6.53 → 6.28 | 1.04× |
| 128 | 3.33 → 2.31 | 8.16 → 7.77 | 1.05× |
| 2,048 | 17.17 → 12.98 | 35.94 → 31.24 | **1.15×** |
| 4,096 | 35.60 → 24.46 | 74.63 → 59.85 | **1.25×** |

All pairs improve; paired component speedups are 1.147–1.151× at 2K and 1.246–1.258× at 4K. Nsight confirms **3 → 2 kernels** with identical GEMM kernel and grid.

**Correctness:** 325 GPU checks and pre-commit/mypy pass. Full-model oracle: 707,680 fused calls, zero value/scale/padding errors, no post-startup compilation. GSM8K: 90.75% in the current instrumented run; prior controlled A/B: 91.66% in all four runs, identical tokens (not a new-stack paired comparison).

**Revision `60a2df16` (warmup removed), B300:** bitwise identical to `462744b0`, 0–13% lower kernel latency. GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, TP1, CUDA graphs) on Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4: 93.6% vs 93.7% on main.

**Serving:** prior-stack C50, 2K-input/1K-output median throughput is 2,359 → 2,375 output tokens/s (+0.66%, six trials/arm), with overlapping ranges—not a robust serving-speedup claim.

**Prefill-heavy serving (same revision):** AGG TP1, C50, 8K-input/128-output; fresh-cache B–C–C–B, six 100-request trials per implementation/budget. Both full retries completed: 24/24 trials, 2,400/2,400 requests passed.

| Token budget | Baseline output tokens/s, median [range] | Fused output tokens/s, median [range] | Median change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 202.87 [198.90–204.09] | 204.56 [201.90–208.36] | +0.83% |
| 4,096 | 386.05 [379.85–394.53] | 392.02 [389.71–397.70] | +1.55% |

## Details

Reuses QuantizedActivation; opaque dispatch preserves dynamic rows under guard-free Dynamo. The kernel has a single Triton specialization per K (no M-dependent constexprs), so the profile run compiles it and no startup warmup registration is needed. Output is bitwise identical to `scaled_fp4_quant`, so it feeds any `kNvfp4Dynamic` consumer (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS verified bit-exact). No scheduler, runner, communication or dependency changes.

Distinct from routed-MoE [#56740](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56740), GELU [#59467](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59467) and normalization [#61073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61073). No DISAGG, TP>1 or default-stack serving claim.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Move the AMD monokernel steps into a Monokernels test area
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Every AMD monokernel step is named after what it tests rather than what it needs, so the seven of them sit in three different files. A monokernel is a fused persistent kernel that runs most of a decoder layer, or a whole decode step, in one launch; the steps that exercise them are all gfx950/gfx942, all multi-GPU, and all blocking. Scattered like this, nobody can see what the group costs.

This moves them into one `Monokernels` test area. **It is a pure relocation** - no step definition changes, no command changes, no test file touched. Follow-up to #67038, which pinned the same steps to explicit test files.

Keys are preserved, so Buildkite history and flake tracking survive the move.

## Changes

| file | |
|---|---|
| `.buildkite/test_areas/monokernels.yaml` | new, 178 lines, 7 steps |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` | -131, six steps removed |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml` | -35, one step removed |

Group header follows the convention every other area uses - `group:` plus `depends_on:`. All seven steps are AMD, so the group depends on `image-build-amd`, the same way the CPU-only areas (`crcr_report.yaml`, `docker.yaml`) depend on `image-build-cpu`.

| key | agent | | timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` | mi355_4 | 4 | 40 min |
| `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-tp8-amd` | mi355_8 | 8 | 60 min |
| `dsv41-mono-decode-layers-gfx942-amd` | mi300_4 | 4 | 40 min |
| `dsv41-mono-decode-gfx942-amd` | mi300_1 | 1 | 30 min |
| `dsv4-mono-decode-numerics-amd` | mi355_8 | 8 | 60 min |
| `minimax-m3-monokernel-mi355` | mi355_4 | 4 | 45 min |
| `kimi-k3-specialized-decode-amd` | mi355_8 | 8 | 60 min |

All seven were top-level steps, not `mirror.amd` blocks, so nothing needed mirror surgery. All seven are blocking, and stay blocking.

No pipeline-side change is needed: `ci_config.yaml` lists `.buildkite/test_areas` as a *directory* in `job_dirs`, so a new yaml there is picked up automatically.

## This is a pure relocation

Parsed every `test_areas/*.yaml` at `main` and at this branch, expanded each `mirror.amd` into its own synthetic entry, and compared `label`, `device`, `num_devices`, `timeout_in_minutes`, `optional`, `working_dir`, `automatic_shard`, `dind`, `depends_on`, `source_file_dependencies`, `commands` and `command` per step:

```
steps before: 519   after: 519
keys only in BEFORE: (none)
keys only in AFTER : (none)
steps whose definition CHANGED: 0

total commands before: 1252  after: 1252
commands removed: (none)
commands added  : (none)
```

Zero changed definitions is the whole claim. The seven steps are the same objects, read from a different file.

Also checked: none of the seven keys is referenced from any other `.buildkite/` file, so nothing is left dangling; `group: Monokernels` is not already in use; `yaml.safe_load` is clean over all 38 pipeline yamls; `check_test_tethering.py --all` is byte-identical to its output on `main` (it reports the same two stale allowlist entries, `tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py` and `tests/distributed/test_pipeline_partition.py`, which predate this series and are left alone to keep the diff to one concern).

## Deliberately not in scope

The new file is not yet exhaustive, and the header says so rather than claiming otherwise. Four things belong in this neighbourhood but are behaviour changes, not moves, and including any of them would break the proof above. Each is worth its own PR with before/after measurement:

- Merging `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` (mi355_4) and `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-tp8-amd` (mi355_8) into one mi355_8 step, which would free a 4-GPU reservation.
- Pulling `models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` and `models/test_dsv4_mono_decode.py` off the generic AMD models step so they run only here.
- Muse Spark is a fifth monokernel model. `models/test_muse_spark_rocm_mono.py` rides the same generic step and has no dedicated step at all.
- `test-amd.yaml` carries its own `:amd: (MI355) MiniMax M3 Specialized Decode` (L1434) and `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics` (L4706). Both are `optional: true`, so no blocking cost is duplicated, but the legacy pipeline is a different schema (`mirror_hardwares`/`agent_pool`/`num_gpus`) and folding it needs an AMD-infra owner.

## Test plan

yaml only, no test file changed. `pre-commit run` clean on all three files, including `check-test-tethering` and the explicit-key check.

All seven steps rendered under the new group and passed on [build 101955](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101955). Times against [build 101867](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101867) on #67038, the same step set before the move:

| check name | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `amd-mi355-deepseek-v4-dot-1-mono-decode-numerics` | 12:59 | 13:07 |
| `amd-mi355-deepseek-v4-dot-1-mono-decode-numerics-tp8` | 12:09 | 12:12 |
| `amd-mi355-deepseek-v4-pro-mono-decode-numerics` | 7:44 | 7:47 |
| `amd-mi355-minimax-m3-monokernel` | 8:36 | 8:30 |
| `amd-mi355-kimi-k3-specialized-decode-shard-1-slash-2` | 17:36 | 17:38 |
| `amd-mi355-kimi-k3-specialized-decode-shard-2-slash-2` | 9:17 | 9:19 |
| `amd-mi300-deepseek-v4-dot-1-gfx942-mono-decode-layer` | 15:49 | 16:50 |
| `amd-mi300-deepseek-v4-dot-1-gfx942-mono-decode-kerne` | not selected | 10:56 |

Check names are identical, which is the point of preserving the keys. The last row did not run on #67038 because it lived in `kernels.yaml` and that PR did not touch `kernels.yaml`; a step is selected when the file declaring it is in the diff. Collecting the seven means one edit to `monokernels.yaml` now exercises all of them together.

None of the seven is `optional:`, so none of this needed a manual unblock.

Groundwork for the AMD monokernel test work in #63486, which adds two steps per model to exactly this file.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][Multimodal] Accept features together with content_parts in /generate
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Multi-turn multimodal RL on `/inference/v1/generate`: by turn N the prompt holds earlier images already expanded (from the previous response's `prompt_token_ids` / `mm_placeholders`) plus a new image with a compact placeholder. Today the request has to pick one of two mutually exclusive inputs, and neither fits:

- `content_parts` only: the processor matches the first placeholder tokens it finds, which sit inside the earlier expanded runs, so the prompt is silently corrupted unless the caller collapses every earlier run first.
- `features` only: the new image has no processed data.

As discussed below with @DarkLight1337 and @hickeyma, this PR lets the two be used together instead of detecting expansion in the processor (the earlier version of this PR):

- `features` carries the earlier items, already expanded, at explicit ranges.
- `content_parts` carries the new media. Only the prompt after the last `features` range is rendered, so the matcher never sees the expanded runs; its placeholders are shifted past that prefix and appended to the `features` items.

A new placeholder placed before the last `features` range is not in the rendered part, so it cannot be matched and the request gets a 400. The only processor change turns that unmatched-item `assert` (a 500) into a `VLLMValidationError`. Requests that use only one of the two fields behave as before.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `content_parts features`, `generate multimodal features`, `mm_placeholders generate`. #53169 reprocesses raw images to shrink payloads and does not combine the two inputs. #54548 (keep `is_embed` across the round trip) is orthogonal; until it lands, `features` items lose `is_embed` as they already do today.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py -v
```

`test_features_with_content_parts` renders a two-image prompt, then sends the first image as `features` and the second as `content_parts` with its placeholder collapsed, and checks that `/generate` returns the same `prompt_token_ids` and `mm_placeholders` as `/render`. On main this request is rejected (`content_parts and features are mutually exclusive`).

## Test Result

Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct on 1x GB200 in the `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image (`18f8f96`, with this diff applied to its copies of the changed files): `6 passed`. Without the change, `test_features_with_content_parts` fails (400 Bad Request).

AI assistance (Claude) was used; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Extensible KV cache: release warmup's blocks before CUDA graph capture
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65868. With the extensible KV cache (the MRV2 default), large CUDA graphs such as encoder graphs could crash startup with CUDA OOM, because warmup's KV blocks still took the memory capture needed. Release those blocks before capture. `extend_kv_cache` then commits the size measured after capture, as it does today.

## Claims

- `google/gemma-4-31B-it` with `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on 1× H100, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`: main crashes at startup with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` at both `max_model_len=4096` and 8192. With this PR both start and serve.
- Graphs captured while only the null block is committed stay valid after the cache regrows. With Qwen3-0.6B and CUDA graphs, greedy outputs match the run with the extensible cache off.
- Only startup changes: one remap before capture. Nothing changes in steady state.

## Validation

1× H100 80GB (SM90), main `821851eab0`, MRV2. The 31B runs use the same model, ViT on `FLASH_ATTN`, `compilation_config={"cudagraph_mm_encoder": True}`, `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2}` and greedy decoding over 6 image prompts:

| `max_model_len` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 | `OutOfMemoryError` in `_dummy_sampler_run`, right after capture (3.89 GiB of graphs) | starts: 772 blocks (7.54 GiB) of KV, 6/6 prompts generate |
| 8192 | `OutOfMemoryError`, same place (4.47 GiB of graphs) | starts: 714 blocks (6.97 GiB) of KV, 6/6 prompts generate |

The OOM site depends on how much is left. When I filed #65868 on `871147447b`, capture itself failed; at 4096 it started, because the graphs were smaller.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py
# 114 passed
```

The new `test_capture_gets_the_memory_warmup_committed` starts Qwen3-0.6B with CUDA graphs and records how many KV blocks are committed when `capture_model()` runs. It then checks that greedy outputs match the run with the extensible cache off. Without the fix it fails with `assert [1025] == [1]`.

<details><summary>31B repro</summary>

```python
from vllm import LLM

llm = LLM(
    "google/gemma-4-31B-it",
    max_model_len=8192,  # or 4096
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.95,
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2},
    mm_encoder_attn_backend="FLASH_ATTN",
    compilation_config={"cudagraph_mm_encoder": True},
)
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** With the extensible cache, `profile_cudagraph_memory()` returns 0, so no memory is set aside for CUDA graphs before KV sizing. The comment there says the cache "measures the capture footprint after warmup". Meanwhile, warmup commits blocks up to `warmup_committable_blocks`, which only keeps the profiled activation peak plus a margin free (about 2.8 GiB on 31B). So capture runs in whatever is left. Decoder graphs fit in that. Encoder graphs (3.9–5.8 GiB here) do not.

**Fix.** In `Worker.compile_or_warm_up_model`, right after the sizing warmup measures its transient peak, call `kv_cache.commit(1, shrink=True)`. This is safe because:
- The warmup blocks hold only dummy data.
- Capture addresses only the null block: `BlockTables.get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes the block tables, and `get_dummy_slot_mappings` pads with `PAD_SLOT_ID`.
- The views stay valid across commits, because the virtual reservation does not move. `test_views_stay_valid_across_commits` and `test_shrinking_commit_remaps_to_the_smaller_prefix` already cover this.
- `measure_kv_cache_blocks` sizes the cache from free memory plus committed bytes, so it gives the same answer whatever is committed at that point.

As a result, the final size now accounts for all graph memory, and a config that cannot fit fails with the usual "not enough KV cache" error instead of OOM.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *Reserving an encoder-graph estimate in `reserved_headroom_bytes`.* This needs a pre-capture estimate, which is what the extensible cache avoids.
- *Capturing encoder graphs before warmup.* This splits `capture_model()` and reorders startup.

Releasing the blocks is 4 lines and keeps the existing order.

**Cost.** The cache is remapped and zeroed again after capture. The 31B log shows 2 s from "Graph capturing finished" to "Extended KV cache", out of a ~200 s startup. That 2 s also includes the sampler warmup and the final measurement.

**Not a duplicate:**
- `gh pr list --search "65868 in:body"` finds no open PR.
- #51590 fixes CUDA graph memory profiling for the non-extensible path, which this PR does not touch.
- #47363 is the original extensible-cache demo.

**AI assistance:** prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Broadcast scalar block scales in Triton fused MoE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the block-FP8 Triton fused MoE compilation failure with Triton 3.9 by broadcasting scalar weight scales directly. Fixes #66195.

## Claims

- Avoid rank-0 tensor slicing when a weight-scale group contains the entire N tile, for both `SWAP_AB` orientations.
- Preserve the scalar-load optimization from #64760 and the existing vector-scale path.

## Validation

Prior validation reported in #66195 used vLLM `a2bcb5657` with this same kernel change, torch 2.15.0 and Triton 3.9.0 on 4x GB200. The unpatched image failed during startup; the patched image started and completed an 8k-input/1k-output benchmark at concurrency 1, 64 and 256. This is prior validation, not a run of this branch based on `5a763c3649`.

Reproducer:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 9216 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
```

The original runs additionally used `--load-format runai_streamer`.

Current-branch test attempted:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k refined_block_scales -v
```

Blocked during conftest import by missing NumPy; the local environment also lacks PyTorch and CUDA hardware. Existing `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe_refined_block_scales` exercises the reported `[32, 32]` configuration against a native reference. No new tests were added.

## Details

#64760 makes `offs_bsn` scalar when `group_n >= BLOCK_SIZE_N` and `group_n % BLOCK_SIZE_N == 0`. Loading through that pointer yields a rank-0 `b_scale`, but the accumulation still slices it with two indices. Triton 3.9 rejects this. Use the same compile-time condition at accumulation to broadcast the scalar directly; keep vector slicing otherwise. The change adds no runtime branch or host/device synchronization.

Duplicate checks on 2026-11-07 found no open PR referencing #66195 and no overlapping fix in searches for scalar MoE scales and `b_scale`/Triton. Nearby #52577 addresses K-tile bounds and scale indexing in other paths, not this scalar broadcast failure.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to inspect the reports, prepare the patch, and draft this description. Before submission, the human submitter must review every changed line, run the relevant GPU tests and confirm current-branch serving validation.

commits.pr_title: [Misc] Warn when gpu_memory_utilization withholds memory from the extensible KV cache
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With the extensible KV cache, an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization` is a hard cap on everything the engine uses, and the KV cache gets what is left inside it. Values just under 1.0, such as a 0.9 carried over from estimate-based sizing, therefore leave free device memory unused, and nothing says so. This PR adds a startup warning for that case and fixes the out-of-memory error, which blamed the device when the cap was the limit (#66192, #66193).

## Claims

- A startup warning, logged once per node, fires when an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization` above 0.8 and below 1.0 keeps at least 1 GiB of measured free memory out of the extensible KV cache. It states the amount and suggests leaving the setting unset unless other processes share the GPU.
- No warning when the setting is left unset, set to 1.0 or set to 0.8 or below, or when another process already holds the memory above the cap.
- When `gpu_memory_utilization` is below 1.0, the KV cache memory error names it and its 1.0 default, instead of claiming the cache "already takes all device memory". After warmup, it also names CUDA graphs and points at the capture sizes.

## Validation

GB200, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `max_model_len=4096`, one run each:

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | Warning | KV cache |
|---|---|---|
| 0.9 | "caps this instance at 165.88 GiB, keeping 15.03 GiB of free device memory out of the KV cache" | 23920 blocks (157.68 GiB) |
| unset (1.0) | none | 26200 blocks (172.71 GiB) |

The 15.03 GiB in the warning is exactly the difference between the two KV caches.

The new error text, from `max_model_len=262144`:
- At `gpu_memory_utilization=0.05`: "... 3.07 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (2.97 GiB) ... The KV cache gets what is left after the model and its activations within `gpu_memory_utilization`=0.05; increase it (with the extensible KV cache it defaults to 1.0) or decrease `max_model_len` or `max_num_seqs`."
- At 0.03: "No available memory for the cache blocks", with the same hint.

Both come from the sizing estimate made before warmup. The variant raised after warmup, which also mentions CUDA graphs, did not trigger in these runs.

**Unit test.** `test_measured_sizing_warns_when_utilization_withholds_memory` covers four cases:
- 0.9 warns;
- unset doesn't;
- 0.5 doesn't;
- 0.9 doesn't when another process already holds the memory above the cap.

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py -k "measure or measured"`: 7 passed.

The cluster runs used a recent main checkout plus this diff. Its vendored flash-attn interface works with the prebuilt binaries there; today's main does not. The two `vllm/` files this PR changes are identical between the two.

## Details

**How the warning measures what is held back.** `measure_kv_cache_blocks` sizes the cache from memory measured after warmup. The warning repeats that sizing with a budget of all memory free at startup, which leaves only the device as the limit. The difference is what the cap keeps from the KV cache. A cap that only stops the engine from growing into memory another process holds therefore does not warn.

**Why above 0.8.**
- Explicit values just under 1.0 look like habits carried over from older defaults: the long-standing 0.9, or 0.92 without the extensible cache.
- Estimate-based sizing needed that headroom. The extensible cache measures warmup and CUDA graph memory instead, and its 1.0 default already keeps a safety margin.
- Lower values usually mean the GPU is deliberately shared.
- A value of exactly 1.0 is the default.

**Where it applies.** `measure_kv_cache_blocks` runs only when the extensible KV cache is active. Configs that fall back to estimate-based sizing never reach it: no VMM support, `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, or NIXL without IMEX.

**Not in this PR.** Several in-repo examples and recipes still pass `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`. They will now log this warning, which is accurate for them.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MLA] Fuse the decode W_UK absorb, q concat + fp8 quant and head pad via AITER
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm with AITER MLA and an fp8 KV cache, each MLA decode layer builds the asm decode query in three launches: the bf16 W_UK absorb `torch.bmm`, the q concat + static fp8 quant, and the `repeat_interleave` head pad to the asm kernel's 16 heads. This PR replaces them with one AITER Triton kernel, `fused_bf16_bmm_cat_quant_pad_mla` (ROCm/aiter#7171), when AITER ships a tuned config for the layer's shape.

Depends on ROCm/aiter#7171. Without it, the tuned-config check returns false and the existing path runs unchanged.

## Claims

- Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X: output throughput **+3.2% to +7.1%**, mean TPOT **−2.8% to −6.2%** across 1k/1k (concurrency 16/64/128) and 1k/8k (concurrency 64).
- Decode query prep: 61 × (5.66 + 4.55 + 5.32) µs → 61 × 4.58 µs per decode step, **947 µs → 279 µs**, two fewer launches per layer.
- Accuracy unchanged within stderr (GSM8K 5-shot, GPQA diamond CoT 0-shot).

## Validation

Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, 8× MI355X, fp8 KV cache, AITER at ROCm/aiter#7171. Both builds ran on the same node and container; one run per configuration.

**Serving benchmark** (`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`, `--temperature 0`, `--seed 0`, num prompts = 10 × concurrency):

| ISL/OSL | Concurrency | Output tok/s (base → PR) | Mean TPOT ms (base → PR) | Mean TTFT ms (base → PR) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1k/1k | 16 | 1,580 → 1,693 (+7.1%) | 9.80 → 9.19 (−6.2%) | 348 → 278 |
| 1k/1k | 64 | 4,151 → 4,335 (+4.4%) | 14.78 → 14.13 (−4.4%) | 666 → 657 |
| 1k/1k | 128 | 6,343 → 6,549 (+3.2%) | 19.34 → 18.80 (−2.8%) | 871 → 773 |
| 1k/8k | 64 | 3,964 → 4,115 (+3.8%) | 16.07 → 15.48 (−3.7%) | 637 → 600 |

The TPOT gain matches a fixed saving of about 0.6 ms per decode step: about 6% of a 9.8 ms step, 4.4% of 14.8 ms, 2.8% of 19.3 ms.

**Profile** (rank 0, 1,020 full-batch decode steps at concurrency 64; the kernel count confirms the fused path runs in all 61 layers):

| Per decode step | Base | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| W_UK `torch.bmm` (hipBLASLt `MT64x16x64`) | 345 µs | — |
| q concat + fp8 quant (inductor) | 278 µs | — |
| Head pad (`float8_copy`) | 324 µs | — |
| `_fused_bf16_bmm_cat_quant_pad_mla_kernel` | — | 279 µs |
| Kernels per step | 1,309 | 1,187 (−122 = 61 × 2) |

The profiled steps' totals also differ by run-to-run collective time (`cross_device_reduce_2stage`, reduce-scatter), which is unrelated to this change. The 668 µs above is the part this PR changes.

**Accuracy** (lm_eval):

| Task | Metric | Base | PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| gsm8k (5-shot) | flexible-extract | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 |
| gsm8k (5-shot) | strict-match | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9325 ± 0.0069 |
| gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot | flexible-extract | 0.6768 ± 0.0333 | 0.6667 ± 0.0336 |
| gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot | strict-match | 0.0707 ± 0.0183 | 0.0707 ± 0.0183 |

**Tests**

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k aiter_fused_decode_query -v -rs
```

All 6 cases pass on MI355X (gfx950) with AITER at ROCm/aiter#7171.

`test_aiter_fused_decode_query_matches_unfused_ops` compares the fused output with exactly what `MLAAttention` builds otherwise: `torch.bmm` into the token-major buffer, `_DecodeConcatQuantFP8.forward_native`, then `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q`. It covers 1, 64 and 300 tokens, with `q_scale` 1.0 and 0.37. The only expected difference is the BMM's accumulation order, which can move a value by one fp8 step, so the test allows one step and requires under 1% of bytes to differ.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# server (same for both builds)
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
vllm serve /data/models/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --dtype auto --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 512 \
  -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True \
  -cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla=True \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code --port 8002

# benchmark, one per row above
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://localhost:8002 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model /data/models/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --max-concurrency 64 --num-prompts 640 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0

# accuracy
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=/data/models/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8002/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=/data/models/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8002/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True \
  --tasks gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=16384
```

</details>

## Details

**Where it plugs in.** The fused call sits in the decode branch of `MLAAttention.forward_impl`. That branch runs inside the opaque attention custom op, so deciding per step from the attention metadata is safe under `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs. It runs only when every one of these holds:

- AITER MLA is enabled.
- W_UK takes the bf16 `torch.bmm` path: not the AITER fp4/fp8 BMMs, not AMX, and `q_pad_num_heads` unset.
- The KV cache is fp8 and the impl takes a quantized query.
- There is no DCP.
- AITER has a tuned config for (heads, `kv_lora_rank`, `qk_nope_head_dim`). This is checked per shape at M=128, like `_triton_gemm_config_is_tuned`'s other callers, so the shape's tuned large-M (`any`) config is used above the largest bucket.

**Head padding comes from the backend.** The asm decode's head count depends on the step: Gluon decode/verify and the DCP routes read the unpadded query. A new `MLAAttentionImpl.decode_query_padded_num_heads()` returns `None` by default. `AiterMLAImpl` returns the asm head count only when that step pads by repeating heads (`get_mla_padded_q`'s divisor case). `_forward_mqa` now also accepts a query that arrives at that count; `get_mla_padded_q` returns it unchanged, and `get_mla_unpadded_o` (`[:, ::2]`) unpads it as before.

**Numerics.** The kernel computes what the unfused path does: the fp32 accumulator is rounded to bf16, multiplied by `1 / q_scale`, clamped to vLLM's `get_fp8_min_max()` bound and cast to vLLM's fp8 dtype. Each head is then written twice, matching `repeat_interleave`.

**Limitations.**
- Tuned configs exist only for gfx950. On other archs the check returns false.
- CI: the MI355 "V1 Attention" step runs `test_mla_backends.py` with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. The new test skips there until vLLM's ROCm image pins an AITER that includes the kernel.

**Related work.**
- #55230 fuses decode RoPE + MLA KV-cache write + fp8 query assembly through AITER's HIP `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`, also in this decode branch. Both PRs replace the q concat + fp8 quant, so they can't both run that op as written. This PR instead removes the W_UK BMM and the head pad with it (−668 µs per decode step here; #55230 reports −0.29 ms for its two launches). Folding RoPE and the KV write into this kernel would combine the two as a follow-up.
- #36573 (draft) fuses the AITER fp4/fp8 BMM variants with RoPE behind an env flag. This PR covers the default bf16 W_UK path and the head padding.
- Duplicate check: searched open PRs for fused BMM / W_UK / decode query / head pad / concat+quant on MLA and ROCm. Only the two above overlap, and neither covers the bf16 W_UK BMM or the head pad.
