commits.pr_title: [Kernel][Perf] Run DeepGEMM Mega MoE on SM90 with MXFP4 experts
commits.pr_body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"simon-veitner-redhat"} -->
_Requested by **Simon**_

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR enables the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` MoE backend on SM90 (H200) for MXFP4 routed experts. It uses DeepGEMM's new SM90 FP8 x FP4 Mega MoE kernel, which fuses dispatch, L1 GEMM, SwiGLU with FP8 quant, L2 GEMM and combine into one persistent kernel over NVLink symmetric memory.

Depends on vllm-project/DeepGEMM#44. The DeepGEMM pin in `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` must be bumped once that PR lands. Until then the SM90 test cases skip.

## Claims

- `moe_backend=deep_gemm_mega_moe` works on SM90 with MXFP4 experts, with the same functionality as SM100 within one NVLink domain.
- On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, single node DP8+EP8, output throughput is 17-26% higher than main's default MoE path and 12-19% higher than main with deepep_v2, at concurrency 1 to 1024.
- On two nodes, as two DP8+EP8 replicas, output throughput is 16-27% higher than main's default and 10-16% higher than main with deepep_v2.
- In a 2-node P/D AgentX setup, ITL p50 drops by 10-11% and TTFT p50 by 12-17%.
- Greedy generations are coherent and agree in content with main's default backend.
- SM90 activations are staged with one FP32 scale per 128 channels, the format DeepGEMM#44's SM90 kernel now takes. Against the earlier revision of both PRs this is 1-2% faster under load, and GSM8K is unchanged.

## Validation

All runs on 8x H200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MXFP4 experts.

**Tests**

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`, `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` on the final revision: 120 passed, 12 skipped (the skips are SM100-only NVFP4 cases). They include the FP32 staging cases, bit-exact against DeepGEMM's `per_token_cast_to_fp8`.
- `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` and the FlashInfer EP tests: 29 passed.
- CI: these files run only in the B200 "DeepSeek V4 Kernels" step, so CI covers SM100 only. The SM90 cases skip unless DeepGEMM has the SM90 kernel, so they need the pin bump and an H200 step; the results above are from local H200 runs.

**Final revision vs the measured one**

The final revision (FP32 activation scales and the review fixes) was compared end to end with the revision measured below, on one node with three fresh servers each: +1.2% output tok/s at c=1024, +1.9% total tok/s and −2.2% mean TTFT on a prefill-heavy load (4096 in / 16 out, c=256), and +0.5% TPOT at c=1 (8.55 vs 8.51 ms). GSM8K (lm_eval, 5-shot, 1319 questions) is 92.93 vs 92.72, equal within the ±0.5 pt resolution. The throughput tables below were measured on the earlier revision (see Reproduction).

**Throughput, single node DP8+EP8** (random 1024 input / 256 output, prompts = max(32, 4 x concurrency))

Cells are output tok/s / mean TPOT (ms). main default is HUMMING with block-FP8 activations (#61875). Mega MoE and main default use allgather_reducescatter. main deepep_v2 is main's fastest all2all backend here. Each cell is the mean of two runs, one on each of two nodes at the same time; the two runs agree within 7%, and most within 2%. The exception is deepep_v2 at c=16, which is one run because the other run had a one-off 1.4 s TTFT stall.

| Concurrency | Mega MoE | main default | main deepep_v2 | Δ tok/s vs default | Δ tok/s vs deepep_v2 | Δ TPOT vs default | Δ TPOT vs deepep_v2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 115 / 8.4 | 92 / 10.4 | 97 / 10.0 | +26% | +19% | -19% | -16% |
| 16 | 1359 / 10.8 | 1102 / 13.1 | 1156 / 12.5 | +23% | +18% | -18% | -14% |
| 64 | 4029 / 13.9 | 3402 / 16.3 | 3513 / 15.8 | +18% | +15% | -15% | -12% |
| 256 | 9424 / 22.7 | 7640 / 28.1 | 7988 / 26.7 | +23% | +18% | -19% | -15% |
| 512 | 13380 / 32.0 | 11478 / 37.6 | 11953 / 35.9 | +17% | +12% | -15% | -11% |
| 1024 | 18566 / 45.9 | 14733 / 59.9 | 16013 / 53.4 | +26% | +16% | -23% | -14% |

**Throughput, two nodes** (2x8 H200, same workload, concurrency is the total)

Mega MoE needs EP within one NVLink domain, so every arm runs as two DP8+EP8 replicas with half the requests each. Cells are the summed output tok/s / mean TPOT (ms), one run per row. Main as one DP16+EP16 server with deepep_v2 internode was not measured.

| Concurrency | Mega MoE | main default | main deepep_v2 | Δ tok/s vs default | Δ tok/s vs deepep_v2 | Δ TPOT vs default | Δ TPOT vs deepep_v2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 13191 / 16.9 | 10938 / 20.2 | 11439 / 19.3 | +21% | +15% | -16% | -12% |
| 512 | 20238 / 21.5 | 16565 / 26.5 | 17503 / 24.8 | +22% | +16% | -19% | -13% |
| 1024 | 28716 / 30.0 | 24847 / 34.9 | 26004 / 32.9 | +16% | +10% | -14% | -9% |
| 2048 | 39740 / 42.9 | 31253 / 56.0 | 34297 / 49.7 | +27% | +16% | -23% | -14% |

**AgentX P/D, 2 nodes**

With the prefill and decode roles on separate nodes, Mega MoE beats main HUMMING + deepep_v2 by +1.5% / +4.3% / +4.0% tok/s/GPU at c=128 / 256 / 512. It also cuts ITL p50 by 10-11% and TTFT p50 by 12-17%. The agentic trace has idle gaps, and they cap throughput. Harness: [agentx-harness](https://github.com/project-cb-lab/agentx-harness) at 89b2186 (a public fork of [SemiAnalysisAI/agentx-harness](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/agentx-harness)), scenario `agentx`, dataset `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`.

| c | Mega MoE tok/s/GPU | main tok/s/GPU | ITL p50 ms (mega / main) | TTFT p50 s (mega / main) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 248.9 | 245.2 | 6.06 / 6.76 | 0.68 / 0.77 |
| 256 | 485.3 | 465.4 | 7.56 / 8.51 | 0.90 / 1.08 |
| 512 | 894.0 | 859.6 | 9.54 / 10.69 | 1.31 / 1.51 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

Mega MoE is vLLM main 9633997299 with this PR applied and DeepGEMM at the SM90 PR head (f4685f2), the revision before the FP32 activation scales. main is vLLM main 9633997299.

```bash
# Mega MoE
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 8 --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter
# main default: the same command without --moe-backend
# main deepep_v2:
EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE=0 VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=indexed \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 8 --all2all-backend deepep_v2

# Client, after a 256-prompt warm-up (two nodes: one client per replica at concurrency C/2)
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --num-prompts $((C < 8 ? 32 : 4 * C)) --max-concurrency $C --seed 0
```

</details>

**Correctness**

Greedy samples on five prompts (temperature 0, max 4096 tokens) from Mega MoE and main default, single node DP8+EP8. All outputs are coherent and finish normally. Each pair reaches the same answer and differs only in wording and small details; for example, main's code returns tuples. On the multi-turn prompt, Mega MoE recommends Day 3 and main recommends Day 2, and each calls the other day a close second. On the final revision, 10 further prompts (each sent greedy twice and sampled twice, on three fresh servers) all finish with correct answers, the same as on the earlier revision.

<details>
<summary>Generation samples (final answers; reasoning omitted, long answers cut after the first paragraph)</summary>

**Math.** Solve step by step: A train leaves at 3:15 pm traveling 84 km/h. Another leaves the same station at 4:00 pm traveling 105 km/h on the same track in the same direction. At what time does the second train catch the first? Give the final answer on its own line.

Mega MoE:

> The first train has a 45-minute head start.
>
> - 45 minutes = 0.75 hours
> - Distance first train travels before 4:00 pm:  
>   \(84 \times 0.75 = 63\) km
> - Relative speed of second train:  
>   \(105 - 84 = 21\) km/h
> - Time for second train to catch up:  
>   \(63 \div 21 = 3\) hours
>
> So, 3 hours after 4:00 pm is 7:00 pm.
>
> 7:00 pm

main default:

> The first train has a 45-minute head start.
>
> - 45 minutes = 0.75 hours
> - Distance first train travels before second starts:  
>   \(84 \times 0.75 = 63\) km
> - Relative speed of second train compared to first:  
>   \(105 - 84 = 21\) km/h
> - Time for second train to catch up:  
>   \(63 \div 21 = 3\) hours
>
> The second train leaves at 4:00 pm, so it catches the first at:
>
> 7:00 PM

**Code.** Write a Python function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that merges overlapping closed intervals and returns them sorted. Include a short docstring.

Mega MoE:

> ```python
> def merge_intervals(intervals):
>     """Merge overlapping closed intervals and return them sorted by start."""
>     if not intervals:
>         return []
>
>     intervals = sorted(intervals, key=lambda x: x[0])
>     merged = [list(intervals[0])]
>
>     for start, end in intervals[1:]:
>         if start <= merged[-1][1]:  # closed intervals overlap at endpoints
>             merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
>         else:
>             merged.append([start, end])
>
>     return merged
> ```

main default:

> ```python
> def merge_intervals(intervals):
>     """Merge overlapping closed intervals and return them sorted by start."""
>     if not intervals:
>         return []
>
>     intervals = sorted(intervals, key=lambda x: x[0])
>     merged = [list(intervals[0])]
>
>     for start, end in intervals[1:]:
>         last_start, last_end = merged[-1]
>
>         # Closed intervals overlap if start <= last_end
>         if start <= last_end:
>             merged[-1][1] = max(last_end, end)
>         else:
>             merged.append([start, end])
>
>     return [tuple(interval) for interval in merged]
> ```

**Factual.** Why is the sky blue but sunsets red? Explain in four sentences.

Mega MoE:

> Sunlight contains all colors, and air molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths much more strongly than longer red ones. During the day, this scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all parts of the sky, making it look blue. At sunset, sunlight passes through more atmosphere, so most blue light is scattered away and the remaining light appears red or orange. The same Rayleigh scattering process therefore creates a blue daytime sky and red sunsets.

main default:

> Sunlight contains all colors, but air molecules scatter short wavelengths like blue much more strongly than long wavelengths like red. During the day, this scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all parts of the sky, making the sky appear blue. At sunset, sunlight passes through a much longer path of atmosphere, so most blue light is scattered away before it reaches us. The remaining light that travels more directly to our eyes is dominated by longer wavelengths—reds and oranges—so the Sun and sky near the horizon look red.

**Multi-turn chat.** Three turns. User: "I am planning a 3-day trip to Kyoto in November. Suggest one main sight per day." Assistant: "Day 1: Fushimi Inari Taisha. Day 2: Arashiyama bamboo grove and Tenryu-ji. Day 3: Kiyomizu-dera and the Higashiyama streets." User: "Which of those days is best for autumn leaves, and what time of day should I go to avoid crowds?"

Mega MoE:

> **Best day for autumn leaves:** **Day 3 — Kiyomizu-dera + Higashiyama** is the strongest overall for classic Kyoto autumn foliage. **Day 2 — Arashiyama/Tenryu-ji** is a very close second and arguably better if you want river, bamboo, and garden scenery. **Day 1 — Fushimi Inari** is not primarily a autumn-leaves destination.
>
> [...]

main default:

> **Best day for autumn leaves: Day 2 — Arashiyama + Tenryu-ji.**  
> Tenryu-ji’s garden and the Arashiyama area are classic Kyoto momiji spots. **Day 3 — Kiyomizu-dera + Higashiyama** is a very close second and can be spectacular in late November. **Day 1 — Fushimi Inari** is mainly about the torii gates, not autumn leaves.
>
> [...]

**Long-form (about 300 words).** Write about 300 words, for a first-year computer science student, on how a hash table works: hashing, collisions (chaining and open addressing), load factor and resizing.

Mega MoE:

> A hash table stores key-value pairs and aims for average O(1) lookup, insert, and delete. It uses a hash function to turn a key—such as a student ID or string—into an integer, then maps that integer to an array index: `index = hash(key) % table_size`. A good hash function spreads keys evenly and is fast to compute.
>
> [...]

main default:

> A hash table stores key-value pairs so you can find, insert, and delete items quickly—usually O(1) on average. It uses a hash function to turn a key (like a student ID or string) into an integer, then maps that integer to an index in an array of buckets: `index = hash(key) % table_size`. A good hash function is fast and spreads keys uniformly. Ideally, different keys get different indices, so lookup is just one array access.
>
> [...]

</details>

**Kernel time (8 ranks)**

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash shape, slowest rank, median of 3 runs. T=8192 reaches about 675 TFLOPS per rank. The kernel's decode tuning cuts kernel time by 2.0-2.7% at T=1-128 and by 8.5% at T=512 against the untuned kernel; prefill sizes are unchanged. With FP32 activation scales, the final revision is a further 0.5-0.8% faster at T=1-512 and 4.1% faster at T=8192 than the revision in this table (mean over ranks, 3 interleaved reps).

| Tokens per rank | BLOCK_M | Mega MoE (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16 | 85.2 |
| 8 | 16 | 212.7 |
| 32 | 16 | 282.4 |
| 128 | 32 | 321.2 |
| 512 | 64 | 570.6 |
| 2048 | 128 | 1693 |
| 8192 | 128 | 6015 |

## Details

- `deep_gemm_mega_moe.py`: on SM90, activations are dispatched as FP8 with one FP32 scale per 128 channels (`MEGA_MOE_MXFP4_SM90`). `prepare_megamoe_inputs` computes it as `amax * (1 / 448)` with a correctly rounded inverse, so scales and values match DeepGEMM's `per_token_cast_to_fp8` bit for bit, and stores its bits in the int32 `x_sf` buffer and in the shared-expert scale layout. SM100 keeps UE8M0. The weight loader relayouts routed FP4 shards and repacks their scales with DeepGEMM's SM90 transforms. Fused FP8 shared experts are requantized once all their shards are loaded.
- BLOCK_M hint: every rank of a launch passes `num_tokens_for_block_m`, the mean tokens per EP rank of the step. All ranks then pick the same BLOCK_M, so idle DP ranks do not run small blocks next to busy ones. Without the hint, ragged steps are 1.5-1.9x slower on the slowest rank.
- DeepSeek V4 routes with `GateLinear` and `fused_topk_bias` off SM100, because `bf16_mega_gate` does not exist there. Warmup skips those configs on SM90.
- SM100 behaviour is unchanged.

**Follow-ups**

- Bump the DeepGEMM pin after the DeepGEMM PR merges.
- A visual walkthrough of the kernel is available on request.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Make MEAN pooling batch invariant when the flag asks for it
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, MEAN-pooled embeddings are not reproducible: the same request can get
different bits between identical runs and alone versus inside a batch. `MeanPool` sums each sequence
with `index_add_`, which is nondeterministic on GPUs. Under the flag, this PR sums each sequence over
its own rows instead; the default path is unchanged. Related: #38559.

## Claims

- **Bug:** `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` says "Batch invariance ensures that the output of a model
  is deterministic and independent of the batch size or the order of requests in a batch." With MEAN
  pooling on `main` (A40, `intfloat/e5-small`), embedding the same 64 texts five times changed the bits
  of 44 of 64 embeddings (46 of 64 in a second run).
- **Root cause:** `MeanPool.forward` accumulates with `segment_sums.index_add_(0, segment_ids,
  hidden_states)`. On CUDA this is an atomic add, so the order of the additions changes between
  launches, and float addition is not associative. The batch-invariant overrides cover matmul,
  softmax and mean, not this reduction.
- **Fix:** under the flag, `MeanPool` splits `hidden_states` by prompt length and sums each sequence on
  its own (`sum(dim=0, dtype=torch.float32)`), so each sum depends only on that sequence's rows.
- **Cost:** only under the flag. The pooling call launches one reduction per sequence: on the A40 it took
  1.5× the default path for a step of 64 × 512 tokens and up to 7× with 128 short sequences. With
  #38559's `vllm bench serve` command line (multilingual-e5-base, flag on, five runs per side) the two
  sides overlapped: 167.06–179.59 req/s on `main`, 170.41–188.42 req/s with this PR.

## Validation

Commands, output excerpts and the full logs: [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60035#issuecomment-6012056147). NVIDIA A40 (SM86), vLLM nightly wheel for
`main` `30ab428235` (`0.30.1rc1.dev708+g30ab42823`), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

- `pytest "tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py::TestMeanPool::test_batch_invariant_under_the_flag"`
  (fp32 and bf16): both cases fail on `main` and pass with this PR. The test pools 64 random sequences
  in one batch and checks that three of them pool to the same bits alone.
- End to end, `repro_60035.py` (e5-small): on `main`, 44 of 64 embeddings change across five identical
  runs, and texts 31 and 63 differ from their in-batch embedding. On `main` that second check cannot
  separate position from run-to-run noise. With this PR, all 64 embeddings are identical across the
  five runs, and all three texts match their in-batch embedding.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no sync error on `main` or with this PR; a positive control that adds an
  `.item()` to `MeanPool.forward` raises, so the check covers this code.

The new test is in `TestMeanPool`, which runs in CI's Model Executor job (H200 MIG 35GB, and MI300 for
the AMD mirror), so no new CI wiring is needed.

## Details

- **Why not the earlier `cumsum`:** going back to the pre-#38559 `cumsum` over the batch would be
  reproducible but still position dependent, since each segment's sum is a difference of prefix sums
  over every preceding sequence.
- **A vectorized alternative:** `torch.segment_reduce(hidden_states.float(), "sum", lengths=...)` (three
  launches instead of one per sequence) gave
  identical bits across calls and for three sequences pooled alone versus in a batch, and was 2.0–6.4×
  faster than this PR's loop, but it needs an fp32 copy of the whole step's hidden states. I kept the
  loop; I can switch if that trade is preferred.
- **Not a duplicate:** in late August I searched PRs for `MeanPool`, `mean pooling`,
  `pooler determinism` and `index_add`, and issues for `embedding deterministic`, and repeated it
  on 2026-10-05. On 2026-10-06 I searched issues and PRs created since 2026-10-05 for `MeanPool`,
  `index_add`, `mean pooling`, `embedding deterministic`, `pooling batch invariant` and
  `embedding batch invariance`; the only match is this PR. #59181 (open issue) reports a 1-ulp
  cross-encoder difference on sm_120 that it attributes to the matmul overrides, not pooling.
- **Limitations:** measured on one GPU (A40, SM86): reproducibility with e5-small, serving cost with
  multilingual-e5-base.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and to run the measurements. I reviewed every changed line and the logs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Size extensible KV cache reserve on the full token budget
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make the extensible KV cache's sizing warmup measure the largest step the scheduler can actually run. It currently misses multi-request full-budget steps when `max_model_len < max_num_batched_tokens`, and is skipped entirely with `max_num_seqs=1`. This is a prerequisite for #66197, whose CI run exposed the first gap.

## Claims

- The transient reserve covers a full `max_num_batched_tokens` step even when one request can't hold it, by splitting the prefill across requests.
- With `max_num_seqs=1` the sizing step runs as a prefill-only step instead of being skipped.
- Prompt logprobs are still measured on a single-prompt step, so `max_logprobs=-1` doesn't reserve full-vocab logprobs for the whole token budget.
- Together with #66197, `test_flashinfer_replayssm_prefix_cache_mtp` keeps the full-budget peak in the reserve while dropping the FlashInfer autotune scratch peak.

## Validation

#66197 fails `test_flashinfer_replayssm_prefix_cache_mtp` deterministically on H100 (OOM allocating 322 MiB for a 16384-token step; reserve 0.83 GiB vs 1.04 GiB on main). That test uses `max_model_len=12288` with the default 16384-token budget.

Runs on GB200 (SM100), one GPU per arm, all on the same `main` base. Reserve is "kept for transient activations"; engine 1 runs a cold FlashInfer autotune and engine 2 hits its cache:

| Arm | `test_flashinfer_replayssm_prefix_cache_mtp` | Reserve (engine 1 / engine 2) |
|---|---|---|
| main | pass | 16.24 / 1.60 GiB |
| #66197 | pass | 1.51 / 1.51 GiB |
| this PR | pass | 16.24 / 1.61 GiB |
| this PR + #66197 | pass | **1.61 / 1.61 GiB** |

Same model and engine config, single engine:

| Arm | Reserve |
|---|---|
| main, autotune off | 1.51 GiB |
| this PR, autotune off | 1.54 GiB |
| #66197, `max_num_seqs=1` | 1.15 GiB |
| this PR + #66197, `max_num_seqs=1` | 1.24 GiB |

On main, the FlashInfer autotune dummy run at 16384 tokens is the only thing measuring the full-budget step; without it (autotune off, or #66197) the reserve stays at the single-prefill 1.51 GiB. With this PR the sizing step reaches the same peak itself. GB200 has enough headroom that none of these arms OOM, so the H100 failure was not reproduced here; SM90 validation is outstanding.

`tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_all_logprobs` (`max_logprobs=-1`, `max_model_len=256`), GB200 reserve: main 0.70 GiB; this PR with prompt logprobs on the full-budget step 8.08 GiB (CI: 5.0 GiB on an 18 GB MIG slice, no room for KV cache); this PR 0.70 GiB.

Unit tests: `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_attention_warmup.py`, `tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py` (127 passed).

## Details

`run_kv_cache_sizing_warmup` measured one prefill of `min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_model_len)` tokens next to a decode request. The scheduler can pack several prompts into a full-budget step, so the reserve could fall short of it. On SM90+ the FlashInfer autotune dummy run at `max_num_batched_tokens` happened to cover this; #66197 excludes that window and so exposed it.

- `run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup` now splits prefill tokens beyond `max_model_len - 1` across extra prefill requests (full-length prompts first), bounded by `max_num_reqs` and draft slots. If committable KV blocks can't hold them all, it drops extra prefill requests rather than skipping the step. Existing callers pass at most `max_model_len` tokens and get the same single-prefill batch as before.
- The mixed step needs two requests, so with `max_num_seqs=1` the sizing step never ran and the reserve never covered a full-length prefill's attention (profiling skips attention). A `prefill_only_fallback` option runs the prefill alone in that case; only the sizing warmup enables it.
- The model runner computes prompt logprobs for every token of a step that requests them, so requesting them on the full-budget step reserved full-vocab logprobs over the whole budget with `max_logprobs=-1`. When the budget exceeds `max_model_len` and prompt logprobs are enabled, they are measured on a separate single-prompt step as before, and the full-budget step runs without them. A mixed full-budget batch containing a full-vocab prompt-logprobs request remains under-measured, as on main; computing prompt logprobs only for the requesting requests' rows would fix that and is left for a follow-up.
- The sizing step is larger when `max_model_len < max_num_batched_tokens`, and adds a second step there when prompt logprobs are enabled (the default `max_logprobs=20`). Startup time comparisons from the runs above were too noisy to quantify this.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix FlashInfer plan buffer race causing illegal memory access with PP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63505. `FlashInferMetadataBuilder` could call FlashInfer `plan()` again before the GPU had copied the previous plan out of the wrapper's page-locked buffer. The earlier step's attention kernel then ran with the later step's plan and read out of bounds. This PR makes the builder wait for that copy before it plans again. The race became reachable with #57214.

## Claims

- Fixes the `illegal memory access` that kills the engine on the first long cold prefill with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, `--pipeline-parallel-size=3`, chunked prefill and prefix caching.
- The wait covers every `plan()` call in `FlashInferMetadataBuilder.build()`: prefill, DCP prefill and decode (`fast_plan_decode`, which also plans the CUDA-graph decode wrappers). The TRTLLM/XQA paths do not call `plan()`, so they neither wait nor record.
- The host waits only when it is more than one plan ahead of the GPU. On one GPU with async scheduling it never blocked (0 of 2000 builds).
- New test `test_flashinfer_plan_waits_for_previous_plan_copy` (prefill and decode cases) fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Validation

**Setup:** 3 x NVIDIA A10 (23 GB, sm_86). vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev505+g00b6c4c56`, built from source at `00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b`, with and without this commit. The issue was reported on 3 x RTX A4500 (also sm_86).

**End-to-end reproducer.** Server, as in the issue:

```bash
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PHB \
  VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK=1 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=23,23,18 \
  VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --pipeline-parallel-size=3 -cc.max_cudagraph_capture_size=4 \
  --max-model-len=262144 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens=6144 --max-num-seqs=4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization=0.95 --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype=fp8 \
  --reasoning-parser=qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser=qwen3_coder
```

After `Application startup complete`, run `BASE=http://localhost:8000 python3 client.py 1 <outdir>`. The client is the reporter's script, plus a fixed seed, a 240 s timeout and a `CHECK` line. It sends three short `2+2=?` requests, then one cold prompt of about 27k tokens that asks for Record 500. It saves the request bodies to `<outdir>`.

<details>
<summary>client.py</summary>

```python
import json, os, random, sys, time, urllib.request, uuid, hashlib
base, key = os.environ["BASE"], os.environ.get("VLLM_API_KEY", "")
run = int(sys.argv[1]); outdir = sys.argv[2]
random.seed(run)
def chat(content, max_tokens, tag):
    body = {"model": "Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
            "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}
    raw = json.dumps(body)
    open(f"{outdir}/attempt-2-run{run}-{tag}-request.json", "w").write(raw)
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/chat/completions", raw.encode(),
                                 {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": "Bearer " + key})
    t = time.time()
    r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=240))
    m = {k: v for k, v in r["choices"][0]["message"].items() if v}
    return m, r["usage"]["prompt_tokens"], round(time.time() - t, 1)
print(f"=== run {run} ===", flush=True)
for i in range(3):
    print("short", i, chat("2+2=?", 32, f"short{i}"), flush=True)
words = "alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel india juliet kilo lima mike november oscar papa".split()
recs = [" ".join(random.choice(words) for _ in range(12)) for _ in range(1200)]
sid = uuid.UUID(int=random.getrandbits(128))
doc = f"Session {sid}\n" + "\n".join(f"Record {i}: {r}" for i, r in enumerate(recs))
print("expected:", recs[500], flush=True)
try:
    m, n, dt = chat(doc + "\n\nRepeat the words of Record 500 exactly.", 64, "cold")
    print("cold", m, n, dt, flush=True)
    print("CHECK cold-prefill:", "ok" if recs[500] in (m.get("content") or "") else "WRONG ANSWER", flush=True)
except Exception as e:
    print("CHECK cold-prefill: FAILED", type(e).__name__, e, flush=True)
```

</details>

 | Tree | Runs | Client | Server log |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Base `00b6c4c56` | 5, failed in all 5 (1 from source, 2 in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c5…` image, 2 diagnostic runs) | `CHECK cold-prefill: FAILED HTTPError HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error` | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, then `EngineDeadError` |
 | This PR | 2, passed in both | `CHECK cold-prefill: ok` (27,423 prompt tokens, correct Record 500) | four `200 OK`, no `illegal memory`, `Traceback` or `EngineDeadError` line |

Before (from source; in the nightly image the same error surfaced in the GDN kernel `chunk_delta_h.py`, as in the issue):

```
[rank0]:[E1027 04:00:40.284348528 ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:2192] [PG ID 5 PG GUID 21 Rank 0] Process group watchdog thread terminated with exception: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
(EngineCore ...) ERROR ... [multiproc_executor.py:380] Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
(APIServer ...) ERROR ... [async_llm.py:943] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
```

After:

```
short 0 ({'role': 'assistant', 'content': '2 + 2 = 4'}, 16, 0.5)
short 1 ({'role': 'assistant', 'content': '2 + 2 = 4'}, 16, 0.6)
short 2 ({'role': 'assistant', 'content': '2 + 2 = 4'}, 16, 0.5)
expected: delta charlie november november charlie november lima foxtrot papa papa november juliet
cold {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'delta charlie november november charlie november lima foxtrot papa papa november juliet'} 27423 14.2
CHECK cold-prefill: ok
```

Also with the fix: 2 more recipe runs on an earlier revision of this PR (non-blocking event, otherwise the same) passed. On the same servers, 7 more cold prompts with other seeds (27,344 to 27,429 tokens) all printed `CHECK cold-prefill: ok`. 3 of them ran at the same time, so prefill chunks and decodes shared batches and the decode-plan path ran too. Control: on the base commit, the same command with `--enforce-eager` prints `CHECK cold-prefill: ok`.

**Unit test** (one A10):

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k test_flashinfer_plan_waits_for_previous_plan_copy
```

- With this PR: `[prefill] PASSED`, `[decode] PASSED`.
- With `flashinfer.py` from `00b6c4c56`: both fail with `AssertionError: assert [False, False, True] == [False, False, False]`. The third `plan()` runs while the second plan's copy is still queued.
- I ran it with `--noconftest` because the local env had no `tblib`. The test uses no conftest fixture. It lives in `tests/v1/attention/`, which Buildkite runs (`.buildkite/test_areas/attention.yaml`).

Other FlashInfer tests in the same file (`-k 'flashinfer or FLASHINFER'`, full conftest with a `tblib` stub): 34 passed, 5 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are `test_flashinfer_fa2_spec_decode_correctness`, with `GatedRepoError: 403` on `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` (no access to the gated model). `test_flashinfer_avoids_seq_lens_copy_without_spec_tokens` passes, so the fix does not bring back the `seq_lens` copy that #57214 removed.

`pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py`: all hooks pass.

No accuracy eval and no throughput benchmark were run. The cost numbers below come from counting blocked waits.

## Details

**Root cause.** FlashInfer's `plan()` writes its plan (request, tile and merge indices) into a page-locked host buffer owned by the wrapper. Then it copies that buffer to the GPU with `cudaMemcpyAsync` and does not wait. `FlashInferMetadataBuilder` reuses the same wrappers every step. If the host calls `plan()` again before the GPU has run the previous copy, the previous step's kernel reads the next step's plan. It reads page indices out of range and faults. This matches the Xid 31 `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ` in the issue thread.

**How it was found.**

- A CUDA core dump (`CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION=1`) names the faulting kernel: `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `flashinfer::BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel` (bf16 query, fp8 KV) on PP rank 0. The GDN frames in the issue are only where the asynchronous error was reported.
- A debug print before each prefill `plan()` checked, without blocking, whether an event recorded after the previous `plan()` had completed. The 27,423-token prompt is cut into chunks of 4704 (five times), 3136 and 767 tokens. The plan for the last 767-token chunk was written while the copy of the 3136-token plan was still pending. That was the only such case in the log, and the illegal memory access came right after it.
- With PP=3 the scheduler keeps up to three steps in flight, so a stage gets the next chunk before its GPU has finished the earlier ones. That is why PP with chunked prefill hits this. The race needs the host to be at least two plans ahead, so changes in timing (eager mode, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`) hide it.

**Why it is a regression.** Before #57214 (in v0.31.0, not in v0.30.0), `build()` called `common_attn_metadata.seq_lens.cpu()` on every step of the native FlashInfer paths. That blocking copy drained the stream, so the previous plan's copy had always run before the next `plan()`. #57214 replaced it with the CPU upper bound when there is no speculative decoding. This matches the report: v0.28.0 good, v0.31.0 bad.

**The fix** (6 lines in `flashinfer.py`). The builder records a CUDA event after its `plan()` calls and synchronizes on it before the next ones. Both happen only when `needs_paged_kv_indices` is true, which is exactly when `build()` calls a wrapper's `plan()`. This follows `synchronize_input_prep` in `gpu_model_runner.py`, which does the same for vLLM's own reused CPU buffers. The event is created with `blocking=True`, so the host sleeps during the wait instead of spinning. Each builder has its own wrappers and its own event. `synchronize()` on an event that was never recorded returns at once.

**Cost.** The host blocks only when it is more than one plan ahead of the GPU, which is exactly when the race can happen. One GPU with async scheduling: 0 of 2000 builds blocked. PP=2 with Qwen2.5-0.5B: 69 of 1000 builds blocked, up to 8.5 ms each. A wait never lasts more than one plan step, which is less than the full stream drain of `seq_lens.cpu()` before #57214. In that PP=2 setup the base commit also crashed in 1 of 3 runs, and this PR in 0 of 3.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

- Bring back `seq_lens.cpu()` in `build()` (revert #57214 for this path). It fixes the race only as a side effect, and it drains the stream on every step for every FlashInfer user.
- Use two or more wrappers in turn. This only lowers the chance: with PP the host can be `pp_size` or more steps ahead, so it still needs events, and each wrapper costs its own buffers.
- Give the wrapper a fresh pinned buffer before each `plan()`. PyTorch's caching host allocator does not see FlashInfer's `cudaMemcpyAsync`, so it can hand the freed buffer out again while the copy is pending.
- Fix it in FlashInfer, so that `plan()` guards its own buffer. Worth raising upstream, but vLLM has to work with the FlashInfer version it uses.

</details>

**Limitations.**

- Not changed: the MLA FlashInfer prefill wrappers (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flashinfer.py`), the sparse SM90 MLA backend and the step5 sparse ops. They also call `plan()` on reused objects, but they have their own builders and were not tested here. The MLA prefill path is safe today only because it passes GPU indptrs to `plan()`, and FlashInfer copies them to the CPU with a blocking copy. #52657 plans to remove that copy, which would expose this path to the same race.
- The issue also reports gibberish output with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. On 3 x A10 that config runs out of GPU memory on the cold prompt, with and without this PR, so I could not check it. This PR makes no claim about it.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Avoid DSpark placeholder shared vocab allocations
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4 DSpark on ROCm was allocating draft-side placeholder `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` modules even though the AMD DSpark draft model does not own those weights in steady state.

For this model family, `load_dspark_model()` aliases the target model's shared vocab modules into the draft model. That means the placeholder allocations were only transient startup overhead. On the Strix Halo TP=2 bring-up that overhead was large enough to matter: about `0.863 GiB` per placeholder per rank, or about `1.73 GiB` per rank combined.

This also matches an existing DSpark pattern already in tree: `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py` <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py> sets `has_own_embed_tokens = False` and `has_own_lm_head = False`, keeps `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` as `None`, and relies on target-model aliasing after draft loading.

This PR narrows the fix to the ROCm implementation only:

- change `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py`
- keep `embed_tokens` as `None` until `load_dspark_model()` aliases the target module
- keep `lm_head` as `None` until `load_dspark_model()` aliases the target module
- add defensive assertions before those modules are used
- remove now-unused placeholder allocation imports

## Test Plan

Validate this change on a 2-node Strix Halo TP=2 ROCm setup by applying the no-placeholder DSpark behavior and checking the following runtime outcomes:

- repeated DSpark server startup tests after removing the placeholder shared-vocab allocations, using `gpu_memory_utilization` values of `0.30`, `0.34`, `0.38`, `0.42`, `0.46`, `0.50`, `0.60`, `0.70`, `0.80`, `0.90`, `0.93`, `0.95`, `0.97`, and `0.99`
- offline DSpark-vs-baseline TP=2 comparison

## Test Result

On a 2-node Strix Halo TP=2 ROCm setup, applying the no-placeholder DSpark change removed the transient draft-side shared-vocab allocations and improved DSpark startup behavior.

Startup-memory impact:

- removed about `1.73 GiB` transient draft-side startup allocation per rank for the shared vocab placeholders combined; this savings comes from eliminating two fixed-size placeholder modules, so it is the same regardless of which `gpu_memory_utilization` setting was used in the startup tests
- after the no-placeholder patch, the old immediate DSpark startup-memory failure mode no longer reproduced in the startup sweep

Offline TP=2 DSpark benchmark summary (E2E latency per request):

| Input -> Output | Baseline E2E latency | DSpark E2E latency | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `1024 -> 128` | `178.63s` | `44.39s` | `~4.0x` |
| `4096 -> 256` | `608.98s` | `85.91s` | `~7.1x` |
| `8192 -> 256` | `375.22s` | `86.00s` | `~4.4x` |

commits.pr_title: [Core][Kimi K3.1] Write draft KV at block-stride slots instead of translating slot mappings
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #66037. DFlash now computes draft KV slots that already include the packed block stride, so a packed draft cache keeps the normal kernel-page binding and the slot-mapping translation layer can go.

## Claims

- Removes `AttentionGroup.map_to_kernel_slot_mapping` and its Triton kernel and buffers, `maps_slot_mapping` / `slot_mapped_layers`, the attention group key change, the DFlash context slot plumbing, and `AttentionBackend.writes_kv_cache_from_block_table`.
- Adds no property or flag to `AttentionBackend` or `AttentionLayerBase`. `vllm/` is +65/−156.
- Kimi K3.1 with the DSpark draft serves as it does on main, with the same sanity outputs and matching GSM8K within run-to-run spread.

## Validation

Pruned Kimi K3.1 at TP4 on B300 with `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview`, `num_speculative_tokens=5`, `--seed 7`, on 9c868d4069. The one later commit moves the stride calculation into `propose` and renames it, and does not change K3.1's slots.

| Check | #66037 head | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 10 sanity prompts, chat and completion text | baseline | 10/10 byte-identical |
| GSM8K, 100 samples, `num_concurrent=16` | 0.41, 0.45, 0.45 (3 runs) | 0.44 (1 run) |
| Draft acceptance during GSM8K | 57.4–58.3% | 59.0% |

Concurrent GSM8K text varies with batching. On #66037's base, the same slot logic matched #66037 on 100/100 GSM8K answers at `num_concurrent=1`, with identical draft counts (2,553 drafts, 7,453 accepted). That serial comparison was not repeated on this PR.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_dense_draft.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py \
  tests/models/minimax_m3/test_dspark_drafter.py
# 242 passed, 1 skipped (GPU)

vllm serve vllm-project/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-pruned75 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --seed 7 --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview","num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

Not run: DCP with a draft, TP8 or multi-node, and the unpruned checkpoint. Tests and serving used a compiled extension from an earlier commit because the local build could not fetch a dependency. The compiled changes since then are limited to top-k.

No open PR removes this machinery (searched `map_to_kernel_slot_mapping` and block-stride DFlash terms). AI assistance was used.

## Details

Manager slots step by `block_size`, but a packed row places other layers' pages between a layer's blocks, so memory steps by the block stride. A kernel-page view can't express both spacings in one dimension. Compressed caches already handle this by writing from the kernel block table. DFlash now does the same for draft KV: `cp_local_slot` takes `block_stride`, and both context and query slots use it.

The guard in `map_kv_cache_to_kernel_blocks` now reads the existing `uses_slot_mapping`. The K3.1 indexer and DSpark draft layers use a K3-only `SelfAddressedMLASpec`, which reports `False`. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs.uses_slot_mapping` becomes `any(...)`, so a group that mixes these with ordinary MLA layers keeps its slot row.

Limitations:
- Only layers using this spec can split a packed token cache. On main, any DFlash draft could. Others now refuse at startup with the existing error, which suggests a smaller block size or a layer-compact layout.
- The subclass opts K3.1 out of parallelism-agnostic canonical offload (`type(spec) is MLAAttentionSpec`). That path fails closed.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Load ModelOpt NVFP4 W4A16 token embeddings in mixed-precision checkpoints
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoints can mark the token embedding `W4A16_NVFP4` in `quantized_layers`, but today only Q8_0 embeddings load (through b12x). On main, `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB` with its BF16 embedding re-quantized to NVFP4 fails to load:

```
The size of tensor a (4096) must match the size of tensor b (2048) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

This PR adds `ModelOptNvFp4EmbeddingMethod`, which keeps the packed table and dequantizes only the looked-up rows, in one Triton kernel on GPU (adapted from the INT embedding kernel in `compressed_tensors_embedding.py`) and in torch on CPU.

## Claims

- **NVFP4 embeddings load and serve:** weights drop from 23.05 to 22.33 GiB and the KV cache grows 1.9%.
- **No accuracy or speed change:** MMLU-Pro 57.90 vs 57.19 (2,100 questions, within noise), same TTFT and ITL.
- **The Triton lookup is bitwise equal to the torch path and faster:** on RTX 6000D with a 131,072 × 4,096 table, 23 vs 81 µs at 1–256 tokens and 277 vs 5,434 µs at 32K tokens (peak scratch 256 vs 2,272 MiB). It compiles with a dynamic token dimension.
- **Tying the embedding to an LM head is refused**, since the LM head would read packed bytes.
- **Weight reloads keep the lookup table in place**, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid, and pre-processed weights load.

## Validation

**Unit test:** `pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4_embedding.py` gives 6 passed on an RTX 6000D (main `75be5c3919` + this PR); the CPU quantization CI job runs the 2 CPU tests. The 4 GPU tests compare the Triton path with the torch path at zero tolerance (bf16/fp16, hidden 64 and 2,080, every finite e4m3 scale code). It builds a real `VocabParallelEmbedding` through `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig`, loads it through `weight_loader`, and compares with `break_fp4_bytes` dequantization at zero tolerance. It also checks both tie errors, and that rerunning post-processing (as a weight reload or a pre-processed load does) keeps the lookup table's address. On main: `ImportError: cannot import name 'ModelOptNvFp4EmbeddingMethod'`.

**End to end** (before the Triton kernel)**:** one RTX 6000D (SM120), main `46f36fa294` with this PR and #64766 (without #64766, main's b12x linears kill the engine on the first long prompt, whatever the embedding). TTFT and ITL are medians in ms at C=1.

| | BF16 embedding | NVFP4 embedding |
|---|---|---|
| weights | 23.05 GiB | 22.33 GiB |
| KV cache | 5,701,632 tokens | 5,812,539 tokens |
| MMLU-Pro (2,100 q) | 57.19 | 57.90 |
| TTFT 768 / 2K / 8K, ITL | 136.2 / 314.4 / 1231.7, 6.69 | 136.3 / 314.4 / 1232.4, 6.68 |

<details>
<summary>Serve command</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve <checkpoint> --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --linear-backend b12x --moe-backend b12x --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --mamba-cache-mode align --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0,"image":0}' --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 42
```

</details>

Not run: TP > 1 on GPU (a two-rank CPU run matched the reference exactly).

## Details

- **Root cause:** `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` returns an embedding method only for the b12x block codecs, and that method accepts only Q8_0 embeddings, so a `W4A16_NVFP4` embedding fails to load.
- The model must build its embedding with the checkpoint prefix, as Nemotron-H does.
- EAGLE drafts decide whether to share the target's embedding by comparing `weight.shape[-1]`, which is the packed width for a quantized embedding, so they keep their own. MTP drafts are not affected. Not changed here.
- **Relation to #42791:** it also adds NVFP4 weight-only embeddings. When I tried it on this model it failed at startup under torch.compile (`Constraints violated (L['input_ids'].size()[0])`): on CUDA, `dequantize_to_dtype(..., swizzle=False)` goes to `_triton_dequantize_nvfp4`, whose launch config branches on the row count, so Dynamo specializes `input_ids.size(0)`. This PR's kernel picks its block size from the hidden size only, so a `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` lookup with a dynamic token dimension runs without recompiles.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Quantization] Honor FP8 activations for Humming linear on SM100/SM110
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Honor requested FP8 activations in Humming dense linear layers on SM100–SM119: **1.4–1.9×** faster measured decode GEMMs on B300 and **−8% to −16% P50 TPOT** end to end across a concurrency 1–256 sweep on a 27B MXFP6A8 checkpoint, with GSM8K strict-match **0.681 → 0.683**. Developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code); Codex helped draft this description.

## Claims

- Quark MXFP4/MXFP6 dense layers honor FP8 dynamic activations, including MXFP6/MXFP8 requests converted to FP8 E4M3 and MXFP8 group-32/E8M0 schemas; compressed-tensors MXFP6A8 checkpoints take the same path.
- MoE grouped GEMMs retain BF16 fallback on SM100–SM119; SM90 and SM120+ behavior is unchanged.
- The FP4 request gate remains. Its dense fallbacks on SM100–SM119 now resolve to per-token FP8 E4M3 instead of INT8 (SM100) or BF16 (SM103).
- FP8 dense activations improve measured throughput with no measurable GSM8K accuracy cost; Wikitext perplexity increases by 0.060, within the existing CI tolerance.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py  # 17/17 passed (CPU, mocked SM versions)
```

- Re-confirmed after rebasing onto current main. SM100/SM103 MXFP8 rows resolve to BF16 on base and FP8 here; SM90, SM120, and FP4-gate rows pass on base. The same matrix checks that `allow_fp8_sm100=False` preserves the SM100 MoE BF16 fallback.
- CI: the broad `tests/quantization/` Buildkite lane is disabled pending a torchao pin; Humming lm-eval steps are marked TEMPORARY. No active step selects this file, as before this PR; these results are local validation.

**Kernel** (B300, SM103; `humming-kernels` 0.1.19; MXFP6 E2M3 weights, group-32/E8M0 scales; CUDA-graph replay device time, 200 iterations per shape): **1.4–1.9×** at measured decode sizes, **~1.7×** at M=8192.

| Shape (N, K) | M | BF16 act (µs) | FP8 act (µs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 17408, 5120 (27B gate/up) | 16 | 24.6 | 14.4 |
| 17408, 5120 | 128 | 28.7 | 18.1 |
| 17408, 5120 | 1024 | 129.2 | 86.1 |
| 17408, 5120 | 8192 | 1154.2 | 664.8 |
| 10240, 8192 (70B qkv) | 32 | 32.1 | 17.0 |
| 57344, 8192 (70B gate/up) | 32 | 127.6 | 73.3 |
| 8192, 28672 (70B down) | 32 | 70.3 | 41.8 |

**End to end** (`nm-testing/Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6A8`, compressed-tensors; 1×GB300, SM103, TP1; `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, seed 0, 4×concurrency prompts per point):

| Concurrency | Before P50 TTFT | After P50 TTFT | Before P50 TPOT | After P50 TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 275 ms | 211 ms (**−23%**) | 7.41 ms | 6.82 ms (**−8.0%**) |
| 16 | 1406 ms | 1058 ms (**−25%**) | 12.49 ms | 11.21 ms (**−10%**) |
| 64 | 1833 ms | 1591 ms (**−13%**) | 29.11 ms | 25.06 ms (**−14%**) |
| 256 | 2260 ms | 1733 ms (**−23%**) | 110.19 ms | 92.13 ms (**−16%**) |

Base silently resolves this checkpoint's MXFP8 request to BF16 on SM103. TTFT includes queueing under the burst; TPOT is steady-state decode. Both improve across the sweep: prefill is GEMM-bound at 8k-token prompts, and at high concurrency decode stays faster even though attention over the 8k KV takes a growing share of the step.

**Accuracy** (GSM8K: same 27B checkpoint, full test set, n=1319, greedy, lm-eval; Wikitext: `fxmarty/qwen1.5_moe_a2.7b_chat_w_fp6_e3m2_a_fp6_e3m2`, existing `test_ocp_mx_wikitext_correctness` setup):

| Metric | Base (BF16 act) | This PR (FP8 dense act) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K strict-match | 0.681 | **0.683** |
| GSM8K flexible-extract | 0.707 | **0.713** |
| Wikitext perplexity | 10.519 | **10.579** |

GSM8K differences are within ±0.013 stderr; Wikitext stays within the CI reference **10.6 ± 0.1**.

## Details

**Design.** Two schema gates predate dense FP8 UMMA support: blanket sub-16-bit deprecation on SM100–SM119 and an SM120-only MXFP8 group-32/E8M0 exception. Exempt FP8 from the first and start the second at SM100. The dense path supports block-scaled MX group-32/E8M0 and epilogue-scaled per-token/per-channel activations.

**Gate.** Pass `allow_fp8_sm100=False` at both MoE expert selection and weight processing: grouped FP8 GEMMs are unvalidated on SM100–SM119, and the dense tuner fix does not establish their correctness. Dense FP8 requires `humming-kernels` 0.1.19, already pinned by [#64802](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64802); [humming#178](https://github.com/vllm-project/humming/pull/178) fixes invalid two-CTA UMMA configurations emitted by the 0.1.18 SM100 dense tuner.

**Limitations.** Eager execution adds ~70 µs/call of Python dispatch in Humming's `process_input`; CUDA graphs remove it. FP8 E4M3 introduces quantization noise relative to BF16, as the Wikitext result shows.

**Compile cache.** The AOT key omits the resolved activation schema and Humming version. Switching paths in place with the same vLLM version string can reuse a stale artifact and fail a size/stride assertion; clear the compile cache between arms. Release upgrades are unaffected because the key includes the vLLM version string.

**Related PRs.** [#59460](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59460) makes activation fallbacks explicit/strict but does not enable SM100 FP8. [#61666](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61666) (merged) added compressed-tensors MXFP6 support; its MXFP6A8 checkpoints (`kMxfp8Dynamic` + float6e2m3/group-32/E8M0 weights) route through `HummingMxFp6LinearKernel` into this dense ungate, otherwise falling back to BF16 on SM100–SM119.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Tuned batch-invariant fused MoE configs on Blackwell
commits.pr_body:
# [Perf] Tuned batch-invariant fused MoE configs on Blackwell, +48% decode throughput

## Summary

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the Triton fused MoE kernel always runs one fixed config (`BLOCK 64x64x32, GROUP_SIZE_M 8, SPLIT_K 1`) because `get_moe_configs()` returns `None` and `get_default_config()` has no batch-invariant table. This PR adds a small per-architecture table of tuned configs, one config per expert shape used for every M, and looks it up from `get_default_config()` under the flag. Shapes without an entry keep the fixed config. Entries were tuned on GB300 (SM 10.3) for the TP=4 fp8 shapes of Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, DeepSeek-V3.1 and GLM-5.3 and the bf16 shape of Qwen3-30B-A3B.

Measured on 4×GB300 with this exact diff on top of `2d40c0609f`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, default backend selection (the FP8 MoE oracle resolves to `TRITON` under the flag):

**Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=4**

| workload | main r1 | PR r1 | main r2 | PR r2 | gain (means) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| serve decode, 128 concurrent (output tok/s) | 2434.69 | 3587.11 | 2420.71 | 3580.00 | +47.6% |

## Why one config per shape (and not M-bucketed tiles)

The first version of this table selected BLOCK_SIZE_M/N, num_warps and num_stages per M bucket with a fixed BLOCK_SIZE_K/SPLIT_K, like the dense `batch_invariant_configs.py` does for matmul. A kernel-level checker (8 probe rows inserted into random batches of M = 1 … 16384, 5 contexts per M, fp8 block-quant, GB300) showed bitwise-identical rows across every bucket boundary. The model-level needle test still failed:

| tree (Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=4, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) | `test_v1_generation_is_deterministic_across_batch_sizes_with_needle[default-FLASH_ATTN]` |
|---|---|
| main | PASS, PASS |
| M-bucketed tiles + fixed BLOCK_K=128 | FAIL 5/5 trials, FAIL 5/5 trials (batched outputs identical to each other, different from the batch-1 baseline) |
| fixed tiles (main's 64×64), BLOCK_K=128 only | PASS |
| M-bucketed tiles, BLOCK_K=32 (main's) | FAIL 1/5 trials |
| one config per shape for every M (this PR) | PASS |

So on Blackwell the per-row result of the Triton fused MoE kernel does depend on the tile configuration for real activations even when the K reduction is fixed, and the only safe table is one config per shape. The sweep data still favours this strongly over the fixed 64×64×32 config (Qwen3-235B shape, M=32: 381 µs fixed vs 211 µs single tuned config vs 132 µs bucketed), and the E2E numbers below are measured with exactly this diff.

## What changed

- `vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant_configs.py`: `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MOE_CONFIGS[(arch family, dtype, block_shape, E, N, K)] -> config` and `get_batch_invariant_moe_config()`; N and K are what the kernel sees (per-rank `w2.shape[2]`, `w1.shape[2]`). The family comes from the existing `_get_tuned_matmul_arch_family()` (major 10 → `blackwell`).
- `fused_moe.py::get_default_config()`: under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` return the table entry when there is one, else the existing fixed config.

## How the entries were chosen

Per shape: sweep `BLOCK_SIZE_M ∈ {16,32,64,128} × BLOCK_SIZE_N ∈ {64,128,256} × num_warps ∈ {4,8} × num_stages ∈ {2,3,4} × BLOCK_SIZE_K ∈ {32,64,128}` (`GROUP_SIZE_M=8`, `SPLIT_K=1`) through `fused_experts()` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` at M = 1…4096 (CUDA-graph timed, median of 20), reject anything not within 3% of the fixed config's output, and take the config with the lowest total time over all M. The sweep data (`timings.json`, raw per-candidate medians) is in the attached evidence archive.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MoE] Fuse SiLU-and-mul with per-token FP8 quant in TritonExperts and skip remote EP routes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fuse SiLU-and-mul with per-token FP8 quant into one Triton kernel for `TritonExperts` on ROCm, and skip the rows routed to remote experts under expert parallelism; applies to PTPC-FP8 MoE (e.g. Muse Spark) and matches `silu_and_mul` + `scaled_fp8_quant` on every row it writes: bit for bit in bf16, and within one FP8 step in fp16.

## Claims

- EP8, 8,192 tokens, one MI300X: the two kernels drop from 867 to 114 µs (7.6×); 1.6–1.8× at TP8.
- Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B PTPC-FP8, TP8 + EP, 8× MI300X: +0.8% to +5.7% total throughput over a 1k–16k × 1–64 sweep, median TTFT 7–9% lower at 8k and 16k.
- GSM8K 95.45 with this kernel in the Muse Spark EP stack against 94.84 for the base (±0.6).

## Validation

**Serve** (8× MI300X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-83c078d955`; base is the same image without this change):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-PTPC-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend triton --dtype bfloat16 --language-model-only \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --reasoning-parser muse
```

### Serving

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len $OSL \

```

3 × concurrency prompts per point (4 at c1), one run per point, after two warm-up runs.

| 64 | 512 × 1,024 | 6.1 → 2.4 µs (2.5×) | 75 / 512 | 12.6 → 5.0 µs (2.5×) |

### gfx950 (MI355X, TP4 + EP, `--load-format dummy`)

| 1k / 1k | 64 | 2,407 | 2,427 | +0.8% | 1.21 s → 1.14 s | 51.9 → 51.5 ms |
| 8k / 1k | 8 | 2,696 | 2,729 | +1.2% | 1.69 s → 1.61 s | 25.3 → 24.9 ms |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 7,591 | 7,759 | +2.2% | 1.72 s → 1.64 s | 73.2 → 71.7 ms |
| 16k / 1k | 16 | 6,369 | 6,485 | +1.8% | 2.60 s → 2.47 s | 40.0 → 39.3 ms |

### Tests

`pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_token_quant.py` compares the kernel with `silu_and_mul` + `scaled_fp8_quant` (bf16 and fp16, 1–1,000 tokens, H = 256–4,096, EP1/2/4/8, 8–256 experts), checks that out-of-range ids are skipped, and checks that `TritonExperts.apply` takes the fused branch with the right expert mask and matches the unfused path exactly. All three tests run on ROCm only, the only platform that takes the fused path. 15 passed on MI300X (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0` with this branch's Python tree and the image's compiled ops). Removing the lane mask from the kernel fails only the `hidden=768` case.

## Details

- Used on ROCm for SiLU without a clamp, FP8 W8A8 with per-token activation quant, no block shape, no static `a2_scale`, no LoRA and no quantization emulation. Everything else, and every other platform, keeps the existing path.
- Rows of the FP8 output and scale for remote experts are left uninitialized; the second GEMM and `moe_sum` never read them. Ids outside `[0, num_experts)` are dropped like `moe_align_block_size`.
- Not a duplicate of #49828 (CUDA C++, dense, no expert mask); #56827 (closed) addressed the same waste for Marlin ReLU2.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] DSpark draft on the specialized decode
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This is the DSpark half of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash specialized decode on GB300 (#61868). With `decode_backend` set to `latency_specialized`, the DSpark draft layers now run on the same decode executor as the target model, on its fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, attention and routed-expert GEMMs. The draft also samples through the model's `sample_sequential` hook: the fused Markov loop from #64442, plus a Markov chain sharded by vocabulary over the TP ranks at small batches.

Everything is under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`, with its tests. The speculators, the model runner and the other shared code are unchanged. With the switch off, nothing changes.

## Claims

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4) with DSpark (5 draft tokens), the switch on in both arms, this PR against `main` (with #63921):
- Decode step: −4.5% at batch 1, −3.4% at batch 8 and −1.6% at batch 40.
- GSM8K accuracy and the DSpark acceptance length are unchanged, within the spread of repeated runs.

## Validation

### Correctness

GSM8K, all 1,319 questions at concurrency 8, on `main` `54155688` and this PR's head `bc6b0f25`, which merges it:

| Task | `main` | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, strict match | 0.973 | 0.976 |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | 3.98 | 3.96 |

Both differences are inside the spread of repeated runs of this PR and #61868 across the earlier revisions: 0.970 to 0.976 for GSM8K, and 3.90 to 3.99 for the acceptance length. The batches, and with them the generated text, differ from run to run.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

```bash
# One SM100-family GPU: the sharded Markov chain (one rank) bitwise against the
# speculator's eager loop, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py -v
# One GPU: #64442's fused Markov loop, which the switch now turns on
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_fused_markov.py -v
# Four GPUs: the TP4 numerics
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v
# Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v
```

| Check | What it covers | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kernel tests (one GB300) | The sharded chain (one rank) bitwise against the speculator's eager loop: temperatures 0, 1 and 0.6, a padding row, BF16 and FP32 logits, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph. The draft's routed-expert finalize bitwise against FlashInfer's. | 197 passed |
| Fused Markov loop (one GB300) | #64442's test | 2 passed |
| Numerics (TP4) | #61868's collectives | Passed |
| Layers test (4× GB300) | With the switch on, the target's and the draft's executors both run, the draft's layers take the executor's routed-expert GEMMs, its logits come from the executor's LM head, and its `sample_sequential` is the sharded chain over the fused loop. With the switch off, neither executor runs and the draft has no `sample_sequential`. | Passed |
| pre-commit | All hooks | Passes on every changed file |

**CI.** The kernel tests run in the nightly 4×B200 step that #61868 added. No CI agent has four GB300, so the layers test skips there; the draft executor and the sharded chain's cross-rank exchange were validated on GB300 outside CI.

</details>

### Performance

**Decode step.** The speculative step with its draft, timed from the client over long-context decodes: one 524K-token request at batch 1, eight of 84K to 648K tokens at batch 8, and five times those eight at batch 40, with 3,000 output tokens each. The runs are ABBA blocks on one GB300 tray, with one server per block and two repeats per batch size. They compare `main` `54155688` with this PR's head `bc6b0f25`, which merges it, with the switch on in both. Both arms share one FlashInfer autotune cache, so they run the same GEMM tactics.

| Batch | `main` (µs) | This PR (µs) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3,966 | 3,788 | −4.5% |
| 8 | 7,505 | 7,248 | −3.4% |
| 40 | 15,515 | 15,266 | −1.6% |

At batches 1 and 8, every repeat of this PR beats every repeat of `main`. At batch 40, single repeats overlap, but both of this PR's blocks average below both of `main`'s (15,286 and 15,245 µs against 15,646 and 15,385 µs).

**Sharded chain.** The same ABBA on a second tray, at the previous revision (on `main` `866bccf0`), compares this PR with and without the sharded chain. Without it, the fused loop samples at every batch size.

| Batch | Without (µs) | With (µs) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4,109 | 4,061 | −1.2% |
| 8 | 8,873 | 8,880 | +0.1% |
| 40 | 16,703 | 16,565 | −0.8% |

The chain runs only up to 8 request rows, so the batch-40 difference is noise between blocks. The chain saves about 50 µs per step at batch 1 and nothing measurable at batch 8. It is 1,567 of this PR's 2,481 added lines, all in `specialized_decode/sampling/`. If reviewers prefer the smaller diff, it can be dropped without touching the rest.

## Details

### What changed

All paths are under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`.

| Area | Files | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft executor | `specialized_decode/runtime/draft.py` (new), `runtime/decode.py`, `runtime/model_state.py`, `runtime/warmup.py`, `specialized_decode/__init__.py` | `DraftDecode` runs the DSpark draft layers through the target executor's attention, MoE and boundary steps, on its fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, mailbox, publishing `wo_b` GEMM and mHC side stream. The target's model state builds it after the target's executor and warms both up. |
| Per-layer steps | `attention/step.py`, `moe/step.py`, `boundary/boundary.py`, `boundary/publishing_gemm.py` | Parameters for the draft's layers: the first layer's mHC pre over the expanded embedding, `wo_b` and the MoE kept TP-partial for the next boundary (the draft's stock layers reduce them themselves), and a residual-only last boundary. |
| Routed experts | `moe/routed_expert_finalize_cute.py` (new), `moe/routed_expert_gemm.py` | The draft's top-k finalize after the low-batch GEMMs, in CuTe DSL (adapted from FlashInfer's `finalizeKernel`). |
| Draft model | `dspark.py` | With the switch on, the draft registers for an executor, runs its decode steps on it, and samples through `sample_sequential`: #64442's fused loop, wrapped by the sharded chain once the executor exists. |
| Sharded Markov chain | `specialized_decode/sampling/sharded_markov.py`, `sharded_markov_cute.py` (new) | The draft's Markov chain sharded by vocabulary over the TP ranks, for batches of up to 8 request rows (4 at 8 ranks). |
| Tests | `tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/` | The sharded chain against the eager loop, the finalize kernel, and the draft executor in the layers test. |

### Design notes

**Structure.** The DSpark draft model registers itself when it is built with the switch on. The target's model state from #61868 then builds the draft's executor right after the target's, on the same fused kernel, mailbox and mHC side stream, and the draft model's forward asks it for a step the same way (`plan()`, then `run()`). Once the executor is built, the draft model replaces its `sample_sequential` (#64442's `FusedMarkovSampler`, which the switch implies) with one that sends batches of up to 8 request rows to the sharded chain and the others to the fused loop. `DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential` already asks that hook first, so the speculator is unchanged.

**Sharded chain: rank lockstep.**
- The chain exchanges each position's winner between ranks through a symmetric-memory mailbox, a cross-rank spin inside the draft step and its FULL graph, so every rank must launch it the same number of times.
- Whether it is installed depends only on configuration, and CPU all-reduces at load make the ranks agree on it.
- The per-call choice depends only on the padded batch shape. It applies up to 8 request rows (4 at 8 ranks).
- Steady state reads nothing back from the GPU.
- The draws reproduce the speculator's `gumbel_sample` loop, except for the bias reduction order before its BF16 rounding, so a bias element can differ from cuBLAS's in its last bit. The fused loop above 8 rows draws by inverse CDF (#64442); both sample the cached draft distribution exactly.

## Changelog

- 10-15: First version, stacked on #61868. The draft layers then moved into a draft executor, following #61867.
- 10-17: The draft finalize and the sharded Markov chain ported from run-time-compiled CUDA to CuTe DSL, with bitwise-identical outputs. Rebased onto `main` `03ee2e13` (FlashInfer 0.7.2).
- 10-19 and 10-20: Rebased onto `main` `aa3564ce` and `3b518982`.
- 10-21: #61868 merged; `main` merged into this branch.
- 11-03: Following review, dropped every change outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`: the post-forward CUDA graph, the context side stream, the multi-group DFlash prepare and the generic fused Markov sampler. The draft now samples through the existing `sample_sequential` hook, on #64442's fused loop, and the sharded chain moved to `specialized_decode/sampling/`. Merged `main` `866bccf0` (the sharded-chain measurement above), then `1fc9d008`.
- 11-04: Merged `main` `54155688`, which includes #63921's rework of the specialized-decode steps. The conflicts were in the attention and boundary steps, the two executors, `AGENTS.md` and the three tests. The draft now shares the mHC side stream that #63921 moved onto the target's layers. The decode-step, GSM8K and test results above are from this merge.
