commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Forward shutdown() in LMCacheConnectorV1 so EngineCore is not force-killed
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62808. `LMCacheConnectorV1` did not pass `shutdown()` on to the LMCache engine. Because of this, an LMCache thread kept EngineCore alive after SIGTERM, and EngineCore was force-killed after `--shutdown-timeout`. This PR adds `LMCacheConnectorV1.shutdown()`, which calls the engine's `shutdown()`.

## Claims

- With `LMCacheConnectorV1`, SIGTERM to `vllm serve` no longer ends in `force killing remaining process EngineCore`. LMCache's shutdown now runs on both the worker side and the scheduler side.
- The built-in connector now shuts down the same way as LMCache's own wrapper, `LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic`.
- A new test, `test_engine_shutdown_stops_lmcache_threads`, fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Related PRs

- #62821 made the same change for this issue. Its author closed it on Oct 27 without a review or a comment, so no open PR does this.
- #64924 (open) removes the in-tree LMCache package and `use_native`. It edits the same two files: both PRs add a test at the end of `test_lmcache_connector.py`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. If #64924 lands first, the `hasattr` guard in this PR is no longer needed.

## Validation

Setup: 1 x NVIDIA H200 NVL, vLLM at `5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9` with and without this commit, LMCache 0.5.6, torch 2.14.0+cu130. Settings from the issue: `--shutdown-timeout 28`, `kv_role: kv_both`, local-disk backend, TP=1. I picked the model (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`), the LMCache env values and the requests, because the issue does not name them.

The reproducer starts the server, sends 3 chat requests, sends SIGTERM to `vllm serve`, and counts two lines in the server log:

<details>
<summary>run.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: [KVC='...'] bash run.sh <server-log>
SL=$1
KVC=${KVC:-'{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_both"}'}
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 LMCACHE_CHUNK_SIZE=256 LMCACHE_LOCAL_CPU=False LMCACHE_LOCAL_DISK=file:///tmp/lmcache_disk/ LMCACHE_MAX_LOCAL_DISK_SIZE=5.0
rm -rf /tmp/lmcache_disk
T0=$(date +%s)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --port 8000 --shutdown-timeout 28 --kv-transfer-config "$KVC" > $SL 2>&1 &
PID=$!
timeout 900 bash -c 'until curl -sf localhost:8000/health >/dev/null; do kill -0 '$PID' 2>/dev/null || exit 3; sleep 2; done'; echo "ready rc=$? after $(( $(date +%s)-T0 ))s"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  BODY='{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper, request '$i'."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}'
  echo "RESPONSE: $(curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY")"
done
T1=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM $PID
timeout 120 bash -c 'while kill -0 '$PID' 2>/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'; echo "server gone rc=$? after $(( $(date +%s)-T1 ))s from SIGTERM"
echo "CHECK force_kill_lines=$(grep -c 'force killing remaining process EngineCore' $SL) lmcache_shutdown_lines=$(grep -c 'Starting LMCacheConnector shutdown' $SL)"
```

For the control, LMCache's own wrapper: `KVC='{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_connector_v1"}' bash run.sh server.log`

</details>

 | Tree | Connector | Runs | `force_kill_lines` | `lmcache_shutdown_lines` | SIGTERM to exit |
 |---|---|---|---|---|---|
 | `5d35ce3` | `LMCacheConnectorV1` | 4 (1 in a venv, 3 with the `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image of the same commit) | 1 in every run | 0 in every run | about 30 s (force kill at 28 s) |
 | this PR | `LMCacheConnectorV1` | 6 | 0 in every run | 2 in 5 runs, 1 in 1 run (see Details) | 10 s (2 s in the 1 run) |
 | this PR | `LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic` (control) | 3 | 0 in every run | 2 in every run | 10 s |

Before, on `5d35ce3`:

```
(EngineCore pid=1738057) INFO 10-28 05:45:25 [core.py:1573] [shutdown] EngineCore: exiting busy loop
(APIServer pid=1737781) WARNING 10-28 05:45:53 [utils.py:653] [shutdown] Process manager: force killing remaining process EngineCore pid 1738057
CHECK force_kill_lines=1 lmcache_shutdown_lines=0
```

After, with this PR:

```
server gone rc=0 at 07:30:32 after 10s from SIGTERM; total 119s
(EngineCore pid=1764423) INFO 10-28 07:30:22 [core.py:1573] [shutdown] EngineCore: exiting busy loop
[2026-10-28 07:30:22,003] LMCache INFO: Starting LMCacheConnector shutdown...
[2026-10-28 07:30:27,913] LMCache INFO: Storage manager closed.
[2026-10-28 07:30:27,913] LMCache INFO: LMCacheManager services stopped successfully in 5.91s
[2026-10-28 07:30:28,373] LMCache INFO: Starting LMCacheConnector shutdown...
CHECK force_kill_lines=0 lmcache_shutdown_lines=2
```

Unit test, `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_lmcache_connector.py`:

- With this PR: `25 passed` (24 existing tests and 1 new one).
- Without the fix: `AssertionError: assert ['storage-manager-event-loop'] == []`. After the failure, pytest itself could not exit, because the leftover thread kept it alive. `timeout` had to kill it (rc=124). This is the same hang as in EngineCore.

`pre-commit run --files` on both changed files passed.

The branch was later merged with main at `e5bec1ddd45d77a3e036cffcda17510e90a5e947`. On that commit's CI test image (`public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:e5bec1ddd45d77a3e036cffcda17510e90a5e947`, LMCache 0.5.6, torch 2.14.0+cu130), with this PR's two files mounted in, I ran the commands of the `V1 KV Connectors` CI step (`pytest -v -s -m 'not cpu_test' v1/kv_connector/unit`, then `v1/ec_connector/unit`) in one process on 1 x B200, next to the same image without this PR:

| | `v1/kv_connector/unit` | `v1/ec_connector/unit` |
|---|---|---|
| main `e5bec1d` | 5 failed, 2128 passed, 381 skipped | 373 passed |
| this PR | 5 failed, 2129 passed, 381 skipped | 373 passed |

The new test passed, and LMCache's shutdown ran on both the worker side and the scheduler side. The 5 failures are the same tests with and without this PR: 2 in `test_example_connector.py` (`Int8 not supported on SM100`) and 3 `test_cpu_offloading` cases in `test_offloading_connector.py`. The run used a 183 GB B200, not the 35 GB MIG slice of the CI step, so it does not reproduce memory pressure from the in-process engine on the tests that run after it. After the merge, `pre-commit run --files` passed again, and without `lmcache` installed the new test is skipped.

## Details

Root cause: `LMCacheConnectorV1` passes each connector call on to `self._lmcache_engine`, except `shutdown()`. So it inherited the no-op `KVConnectorBase_V1.shutdown()`. vLLM already calls `connector.shutdown()` on the scheduler side (`Scheduler.shutdown()`) and on the worker side (`ensure_kv_transfer_shutdown()`), but the call stopped at the wrapper. As a result, LMCache's `LMCacheConnectorV1Impl.shutdown()` -> `LMCacheManager.stop_services()` never ran. LMCache's `StorageManager` starts a thread named `storage-manager-event-loop`. It is not a daemon thread, it runs `loop.run_forever()`, and only `StorageManager.close()` stops it, which is reached only through that shutdown. So `EngineCore.shutdown()` returned, but at interpreter exit Python waited for that thread forever. To confirm this, I added temporary prints around `engine_core.shutdown()` in `run_engine_core`, on the unfixed code. They showed that `engine_core.shutdown()` returned at once, and that `storage-manager-event-loop` was the only non-daemon thread still alive besides `MainThread`.

The fix calls the engine's own `shutdown()`. It does not stop LMCache threads from vLLM, so the list of services to stop (health monitor, offload server, plugins, API server, lookup server and client, cache engine) stays in LMCache. LMCache's own `LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic.shutdown()` makes the same call. With LMCache 0.5.7 the adapter moved to the `lmcache_inprocess` package, which keeps the old import path as a shim and has the same `shutdown()`. The `hasattr` guard is for `kv_connector_extra_config.use_native: true`. In that mode the engine is the in-tree `lmcache_integration/vllm_v1_adapter.py:LMCacheConnectorV1Impl`, which has no `shutdown()`. That mode currently fails earlier, at import, with LMCache 0.5.6 (`ImportError: cannot import name 'CudaIPCWrapper'`, #64790), and #64924 removes it; the guard keeps shutdown from raising `AttributeError` while the mode exists. The file already uses `hasattr` for other optional engine methods (`register_kv_caches`, `bind_connector_metadata`). `lmcache_mp_connector.py` already has its own `shutdown()`.

Limitations:

- This fix makes LMCache's shutdown run, so LMCache's `ZMQOffloadServer.close()` now runs too. It closes a ZMQ socket from one thread while `offload-server-thread` is blocked in `recv()` on the same socket. In 1 of the 6 runs, EngineCore aborted there with `Assertion failed: pfd.revents & POLLIN (src/signaler.cpp:238)`. That run had no force kill: the server was gone 2 s after SIGTERM, but the scheduler-side shutdown did not run. In the other runs, and in the control runs, LMCache logs `Offload server thread did not terminate within timeout` and waits 5 s. A standalone pyzmq script (pyzmq 27.2.0, libzmq 4.3.5) with the same pattern aborted in 88 of 200 runs and left the thread stuck in the other 112. This is an LMCache bug, and LMCache's own wrapper reaches it the same way. I reported it as LMCache/LMCache_inprocess#NNN, where LMCache's in-process code now lives.
- On the worker side, LMCache's shutdown took about 6 s here, 5 s of which is that join timeout. With a very small `--shutdown-timeout`, EngineCore can still be force-killed before LMCache finishes.
- The new test builds a real `LLM` (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`) with the engine in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), so that it can see LMCache's threads. It needs a GPU and the `lmcache` package, and it skips itself (`pytest.importorskip("lmcache")`) when `lmcache` is not installed. In CI it runs in the `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) V1 KV Connectors` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`, which is enabled again on main; the CUDA CI image ships `lmcache` 0.5.6 (`.buildkite/scripts/check-kv-connectors.sh` requires it). The AMD mirror of that step (MI355) runs it too: the ROCm image builds LMCache 0.5.3 from source (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm`), which has the same `shutdown()` path. I have not run the test on ROCm.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] MXFP8 linear on AITER's tuned FlyDSL GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `AiterFlyDSLMxfp8LinearKernel`, an MXFP8 linear kernel for gfx950 that runs AITER's tuned FlyDSL GEMM. It sits ahead of the Triton `dot_scaled` kernel in the ROCm MXFP8 list, but only for (N, K) shapes that AITER has tuned. All other shapes stay on Triton.

The tuned configs come from ROCm/aiter#6060 and ROCm/aiter#7411, both in the AITER that main pins. This doesn't collide with the AITER Triton MXFP8 kernel in #64089.

## Claims

- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, TP4, DSpark 7, MI355X: at conc 32 / 64, ITL p50 is down 4.4% / 11.1% and throughput is up 2.0% / 7.7%.
- 1.1–1.9x faster per GEMM than Triton at M ≥ 32 on most M3.1 TP4 shapes.
- Keeps MiniMax-M3's fused MXFP8 quant epilogues, mono decode and the DSpark drafter kernels working.
- No accuracy change (GSM8K).

## Validation

**End to end.** InferenceX agentic recipe, NVFP4 KV, DBO (#63483 on both sides), synthetic acceptance 4.04. Each point is 900 s; c64 is the mean of two GPU-swapped runs.

| Conc | Metric | Nightly | Nightly + PR | Change |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | Throughput per GPU (tok/s) | 51,518 | 52,563 | +2.0% |
| 32 | ITL p50 (ms) | 5.66 | 5.41 | −4.4% |
| 64 | Throughput per GPU (tok/s) | 57,792 | 62,236 | +7.7% |
| 64 | ITL p50 (ms) | 12.52 | 11.13 | −11.1% |

With mono decode and the drafter kernels on (c4), performance is unchanged: 7,555 tok/s per GPU on both sides.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot strict-match with real rejection sampling, mean of two GPU-swapped runs per side:
- conc 64: 0.9648 on main, 0.9648 with the PR.
- mono + drafter at c8: 0.9648 on main, 0.9610 with the PR. Draft acceptance length is 4.68 vs 4.70.

**Per-GEMM latency (µs), Triton -> AITER.** MI355X, including the activation quant, CUDA-graph replay with rotating weights.

| N x K | M=1 | M=32 | M=128 | M=512 | M=8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2560 x 6144 (QKV) | 8.5 -> 8.1 | 9.6 -> 8.9 | 16.7 -> 13.5 | 34.7 -> 26.7 | 228.1 -> 174.4 |
| 6144 x 2048 (o_proj) | 5.8 -> 6.2 | 7.4 -> 6.8 | 11.4 -> 9.3 | 24.1 -> 15.5 | 189.7 -> 127.4 |
| 1536 x 6144 (shared gate/up) | 8.2 -> 7.2 | 8.5 -> 7.8 | 14.2 -> 11.4 | 34.8 -> 20.5 | 148.1 -> 116.8 |
| 6144 x 768 (shared down) | 3.9 -> 5.1 | 5.7 -> 5.6 | 6.8 -> 6.3 | 10.9 -> 9.8 | 103.6 -> 62.0 |
| 6144 x 6144 (dense gate/up) | 13.5 -> 10.8 | 14.3 -> 12.5 | 23.2 -> 19.6 | 64.5 -> 36.3 | 519.1 -> 355.4 |
| 1280 x 6144 (DSpark ctx K/V) | 9.8 -> 6.9 | 9.9 -> 7.5 | 19.0 -> 11.2 | 34.8 -> 18.2 | 142.3 -> 100.3 |

**Tests.**
- `test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py`: kernel selection gating (CPU).
- `test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py`: correctness against a dequantized reference, pre-quantized input, CUDA graphs, and the un-shuffle.
- `test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py`: fused epilogues and mono weight copies with this kernel.

## Details

- **Requirements.** Needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, gfx95x and a bf16 model. Off under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`.
- **Opt-out.** Set `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=AiterFlyDSLMxfp8LinearKernel`.
- **`--linear-backend=aiter`.** The kernel isn't registered under the `aiter` backend, so untuned shapes still get a kernel there.
- **Pre-quantized input.** It takes a `QuantizedActivation` (`kMxfp8Dynamic`, row-major E8M0 scales) like `dot_scaled`. That keeps MiniMax-M3's norm, swiglu and sparse-decode quant fusions on.
- **Weight layout.** Weights are (16, 16)-preshuffled at load. `row_major_weight()` undoes this for mono decode and the DSpark drafter, which read raw weights. Weight-cache exports work as is.
- **Known gaps.** Shared down (6144 x 768) is slower at M ≤ 8, and o_proj is about even at M=1. The kernel claims by (N, K), not by M.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Enables adaptive DSpark verification for MiniMax M3 on ROCm. Part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion (#51303):  each model needs varlen-capable sparse kernels before adaptive verification can redistribute draft tokens across requests.

Scope: only the ROCm Triton indexer and Triton sparse-decode paths gain ragged decode support (validated on MI325/gfx942 and MI355X/gfx950). The CUDA backends, the AITER MSA indexer / AITER sparse PA, the ROCm NVFP4 sparse path and the indexer CP path keep reporting device/CPU query-length mismatch as unsupported, so the selector keeps adaptive verification off there. With adaptive verification off, the uniform decode path is unchanged.

## Changes

- MiniMax M3 indexer and sparse attention (ROCm Triton): device-side ragged decode metadata. Both AMD index-score launch policies, the fused top-k selector and sparse decode map packed query tokens to requests from device `query_sta
rt_loc`, using upstream's `compute_token_to_req_indices` (a device-side binary search that doesn't depend on `max_query_len` and handles zero-length padding rows). Shared builder logic lives in `models/minimax_m3/common/varlen_decode.py`.
- Cudagraphs: the builders stay `UNIFORM_BATCH` and advertise the bounded varlen contract (`get_varlen_cudagraph_max
_query_len` = `1 + num_speculative_tokens`) only when adaptive verification is enabled. Mixed prefill+decode batches
 never replay FULL graphs.
- `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch()` on the MiniMax indexer/sparse backends is true only when the base rule
 holds and the builder has ragged decode kernels.
- `kernel_paged_attention_2d`: return for `query_len != 1` (previously `> 1`). FULL cudagraph replay pads the request dimension with zero-length rows, which fell into the decode path and read/wrote the row one past the last real token. `ROCM_ATTN` reports `ALWAYS`, so it replays the ragged decode graphs adaptive verification produces
- Indexer CP (`minimax_m3_indexer_cp`) rejects adaptive verification explicitly; its decode scores uniform rows.

The DSpark confidence-head config fallback that was here earlier removed

## Testing

- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` (incl. ragged index top-k and ragged sparse decode with zero-length padding rows, TP1–TP8 head shapes): pass on MI325 (gfx942) and MI355X (gfx950). The ragged index top-k test covers every gfx950 indexer decode launch path (balanced, high-batch and default score launches; single- and 16-chunk topk=16 selector).
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_varlen_cudagraph.py`, `test_minimax_m3_indexer_cp.py`: pass.
- `test_prefix_prefill.py::test_contexted_kv_attention` (now with a trailing zero-length row): pass on gfx942 and gfx950.
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`: pass.
- Stress test of the ragged index top-k and sparse decode kernels at serving-sized batches: 60 random batches of 380
–512 requests (1–8 query tokens each, up to 4K context, zero-length padding rows), reference-checked every 10th batch: all passed.

## End-to-end results 
MI325, `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-DSpark` drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, FULL cudagraphs, default memory settings, 
`--max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 512`. Fixed vs adaptive verification on the same build. This drafter declares a confidence head but ships no `confidence_head.*` weights, so adaptive verification uses the online acceptance estimator (#52228).

GSM8K, full test set (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 64):

| Checkpoint | TP | Fixed | Adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` | 2 | 0.8196 | 0.8226 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` | 4 | 0.8779 | 0.8711 |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` (BF16) | 8 | 0.8704 | 0.8688 |

Repeated MXFP8 runs vary by about ±0.01 for both modes (fixed 0.860–0.878 over 6 runs, adaptive 0.867–0.879 over 9 runs).

MI355X (gfx950), `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`, TP=2, same drafter and K=7, AITER MXFP4 MoE, FULL cudagraphs, `--max-model-len 32768`. main (fixed verification) vs this PR (adaptive verification):

| Eval | main (fixed K=7) | Adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPQA diamond, 0-shot CoT, flexible-extract | 0.7929 | 0.7929 |
| NIAH single 1/2/3 @ 4K/8K/16K, mean of 9 | 0.987 | 0.986 |

Sonnet 550 in / 150 out / 200 shared prefix, ignore EOS, output tok/s (adaptive gain vs fixed):

| Concurrency | MXFP4, TP=2 | MXFP8, TP=4 | BF16, TP=8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 649.96 → 674.59 (+3.8%) | 2241.79 → 2166.80 (−3.3%) | 3451.90 → 3327.16 (−3.6%) |
| 256 | 882.77 → 930.58 (+5.4%) | 2560.18 → 2605.40 (+1.8%) | 4005.66 → 4063.85 (+1.5%) |
| 320 | 965.59 → 1020.85 (+5.7%) | 2643.30 → 2733.47 (+3.4%) | 4099.15 → 4268.66 (+4.1%) |
| 380 | 1013.94 → 1071.63 (+5.7%) | 2686.83 → 2778.46 (+3.4%) | 4190.48 → see below |
| 420 | 1040.76 → 1102.05 (+5.9%) | 2713.55 → 2692.00 (−0.8%) | 4263.58 → see below |
| 500 | 1089.06 → 1146.61 (+5.3%) | fixed OOM → 1929.71 | 4228.05 → see below |

The gain shrinks as verification gets cheaper: TP=4 and TP=8 leave little verify cost for adaptive budgeting to saver MXFP8 fixed verification at concurrency 500 runs out of memory allocating the full verification logits (1.6 GB) at the default 
`--gpu-memory-utilization`; adaptive verification bounds that allocation and completes all requests.

BF16, TP=8, after #62769 (latest build), c512, 1k OSL: adaptive 3,322.8 tok/s (acceptance length 2.28) vs fixed k=7 3,082.1 tok/s (acceptance length 3.3); GSM8K 0.961 vs 0.959. The config that previously hung with `GPU Hang` at concurrency ≥ 380 now passes.

## Earlier results (before rebase)

MXFP4 target with the `olka-fi/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-DSpark` drafter, TP=2, same Sonnet workload, 3–5 minute steady-state runs; 9,040 requests, none failed.

| Concurrency | Fixed tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | Fixed median TPOT | Adaptive median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 299.82 | 330.13 | +10.1% | 381.78 ms | 342.55 ms |
| 256 | 413.86 | 479.84 | +15.9% | 500.45 ms | 406.09 ms |
| 320 | 471.08 | 573.31 | +21.7% | 570.16 ms | 446.81 ms |
| 380 | 488.89 | 603.86 | +23.5% | 615.22 ms | 478.64 ms |
| 420 | 528.18 | 658.30 | +24.6% | 645.89 ms | 489.64 ms |
| 500 | 568.84 | 731.51 | +28.6% | 667.91 ms | 521.15 ms |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Transformers] Infer mm encoder dynamic_arg_dims from forward signature
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`compile_mm_encoder` on the Transformers backend crashes at init with `No dynamic dimensions found` for encoders with no `torch.Tensor`/`torch.FloatTensor` argument; this infers their dynamic args from `forward` instead. Part of #63635 (blocker 1 of 3).

## Claims

- 15 encoders no longer crash at init: aria, cohere2_vision, deepseek_vl, deepseek_vl_hybrid, gemma3, glmasr, idefics2, idefics3, llava_onevision, minicpmv4_6, minicpmv4_7, moss_transcribe_diarize, paligemma, smolvlm, voxtral.
- 11 encoders that already had a recognised annotation get extra dynamic args; InternVL3, the only one of them that runs on the backend today, gives identical outputs.
- Marking a non-tensor argument dynamic now raises an error naming the type hint to fix.
- Gemma 4 checkpoints without an audio tower (e.g. 31B) no longer try to decorate `NoneType`.
- Blockers 2 and 3 in #63635 are unchanged, so e.g. LLaVA-OneVision still fails later in Dynamo.

## Validation

B200, transformers 5.22.2, `compile_mm_encoder=True`, greedy, 3 image sizes sent one at a time then batched (6 outputs). "Same" compares against the encoder run eagerly.

| Model | `main` | This PR | Same as eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| SmolVLM-256M-Instruct | `ValueError: No dynamic dimensions found` | OK | 3/6 |
| InternVL3-1B-hf | OK | OK | 5/6 |

Mismatches are a near-tie at token 3 ("we can see" vs "there is"); eager output itself changes between single and batched requests.

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k "compile_mm_encoder or infer_dynamic_arg_dims or missing_encoders"
```

All pass; `test_compile_mm_encoder` fails on `main` with the `ValueError` above, and `test_missing_encoders_are_skipped` fails on `main` with `NoneType`.

## Details

- Root cause: `support_torch_compile(dynamic_arg_dims=None)` only recognises `torch.Tensor`/`torch.FloatTensor` (optionally `| None`) annotations, but many HF encoders leave `pixel_values` unannotated or use legacy types like `torch.BoolTensor`.
- `infer_dynamic_arg_dims` marks dim 0 of unannotated and `torch.*Tensor` arguments (including inside unions) and leaves containers like `list[torch.Tensor]` static. It is used for every encoder so there is one rule; an unannotated non-tensor argument fails at the first call with a pointer to its type hint.
- Of the other 10 encoders whose dims widen, Muse-Glimmer fails identically before and after (blocker 2), Muse-Spark (816B) is untested, and 8 cannot run on the backend yet for unrelated reasons (missing processor or model hooks, weight layout).

---

commits.pr_title: [MRV2][PP] Support different CUDA graph padding across pipeline stages
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

PP stages resolve CUDA graph modes from their local attention backends, so the same batch can have different padded sizes on adjacent stages. The receiver currently copies using its own padded size, which fails when the sender provides fewer rows. Since #65896, the copy-engine transport, the default for TP=1 PP within one node, skips this copy, so the failure now occurs only when PP uses NCCL (for example, TP>1 or PP across nodes).

The two stages share the same real token rows, but their padding is local to each stage. This PR therefore sends only the real token rows between stages, copies them into the receiver's persistent intermediate buffers, and uses the receiver's padded size for execution.

## Claims

- Fix the intermediate-tensor size mismatch when the receiving PP stage pads a batch to more rows than the sending stage.
- Cover the failure with an end-to-end PP + EAGLE3 regression test that compares generation against eager execution.

## Validation

All runs used NVIDIA B300 GPUs, Model Runner V2, PP=2, and greedy decoding. Runs on main use the NCCL transport.

**Different graph modes:** only stage 1 downgrades from `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` to `PIECEWISE`.

| Configuration | main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 (`RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3`), 2 speculative tokens, target `TRITON_ATTN`, draft `FLASHINFER`, `use_trtllm_attention=false` | First decode step fails: `(4) must match (3)` | Completes. Across 9 greedy outputs of 24 tokens, the first divergence from eager occurs at the same positions as with matching stage modes (draft on `TRITON_ATTN`) |
| OPT-350m + OPT-125m draft, 3 speculative tokens, default settings, with #66063 | First decode step fails: `(24) must match (20)` | 366/450 tokens accepted, matching eager and PP=1; 8/8 outputs equal |

**Matching padding:** main vs. this PR.

| Configuration | Accepted tokens, main → this PR | Equal outputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 11 sequences across prefill and mixed decode steps | — | 11/11 |
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 | 259/753 → 259/753 | 8/8 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B MTP | 319/582 → 319/582 | 8/8 |

At TP=2 × PP=2, Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 show some output differences between main and this PR. Three repeated runs of each configuration show the same variation within each revision; some main and PR runs match exactly.

**Regression test:** `test_pp_cudagraph_mode_differs_across_stages` uses the Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 configuration above, generates 32 tokens for 4 prompts with and without `enforce_eager`, and compares outputs with `check_logprobs_close`.

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py::test_pp_cudagraph_mode_differs_across_stages
```

On main:

```
(Worker_PP1) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1223]   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 2085, in execute_model
(Worker_PP1) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1223] RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (16) must match the size of tensor b (12) at non-singleton dimension 0
FAILED distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py::test_pp_cudagraph_mode_differs_across_stages
```

With this PR: **1 passed in each of 4 runs**.

The test sets `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT=nccl` because the copy-engine transport receives directly into the persistent intermediate buffers, so the receiving stage performs no copy. With `VLLM_PP_TRANSPORT=copy_engine`, the test also passes.

The test also passes at TP=2 × PP=2, where both TP ranks of stage 1 use `PIECEWISE`. This run uses NCCL because the copy-engine transport requires TP=1.

Runs with temporary row-count logging (the copy-engine and TP=2 runs of this test, and `test_pp_dp_v2.py`) show that every receive got exactly `num_tokens` rows and that the sending stage no longer sends its padding rows, for example 57 rows instead of 64 in a prefill step.

Existing tests with this PR:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_pp_cudagraph.py::test_pp_cudagraph   # 1 passed
pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_pp_dp_v2.py                       # 6 passed
```

The regression test requires SM90 or newer. Below SM90, FlashInfer supports full CUDA graphs for speculative decode batches, so both stages select the same mode. The L4 `Pipeline + Context Parallelism` step skips the test; this PR adds it to `:nvidia: (B200) [Nightly] Distributed`.

## Details

The failure occurs with Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 at PP=2 when the target uses `TRITON_ATTN` and the draft uses `FLASHINFER` with TRT-LLM disabled. Each rank calls `resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes` using the weakest CUDA graph support among its attention layers. Draft attention runs only on the last stage and causes that stage to use `PIECEWISE` graphs for speculative decode, while the first stage uses `FULL` decode graphs.

For one request with two draft tokens:

| | Stage 0 | Stage 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real tokens | 3 | 3 |
| Execution rows after padding | 3 | 4 |

Stage 0 sends three rows. Stage 1 receives those three rows but attempts `dst[:4].copy_(recv[:4])`, causing a shape mismatch. PP stages agree on the real tokens; the padding belongs to each stage's local execution.

The fix sends only the first `num_tokens` rows from the sending stage; both PP transports size the received tensors from the sender's row count. The receiving stage copies those rows and passes a `num_tokens_after_padding` view of the destination buffer to the model. This separates the valid data sent over PP from the padding used by each stage's local graph, so padding rows are not transferred between stages. Padding rows on the receiving stage retain their existing contents and are handled by the existing attention metadata and padding-slot logic.

With #66063, OPT-350m + OPT-125m also reaches this failure under default settings: the draft's head counts rule out TRT-LLM, and only the last stage lowers its graph mode.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR changes this copy. Searches: "pipeline parallel cuda graph padding", "PP cudagraph mode stage", and "intermediate tensors padding pipeline".

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Offload] Apply --cpu-offload-gb to models served by the Transformers modeling backend
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--cpu-offload-gb` was silently ignored for models on the Transformers modeling backend. Their decoder layers are now built one at a time and passed to the offloader, the same way `make_layers` does it.

Closes #66810

## Claims

- Decoder layers (and their MoE experts) are offloaded for every offloader, and peak device memory during construction is about one layer above what stays resident.
- No change when offloading is off. MTP drafts are not offloaded, the same as native drafts.
- Not covered: multimodal models still fail with `--cpu-offload-gb`, as on main, because `_mark_tower_model` wraps the towers while their parameters are still on `meta`. Left as a follow-up.

## Validation

Peak device memory above resident while the decoder is built (8 layers, dummy weights, `cpu_offload_gb=4`), from `test_transformers_backend_weight_offloading`:

| Model | Without per-layer build | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm-project/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` | 8.15 layers (offloaded after `__init__`) | 1 layer |
| `TitanML/tiny-mixtral` | 7.8 layers (experts fused before the decoder pass) | ≤ 1.5 layers (passes) |

```
cd tests && pytest -v --forked basic_correctness/cpu_offload/test_cpu_offload.py -k transformers_backend
```

B200: all 5 tests pass (peak memory for both models, and output comparisons with the UVA, non-UVA and prefetch offloaders). The B200 runs forced `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` because of a local FlashInfer JIT build problem. ruff and mypy pass.

Includes the MoE idea from #66804, by @francesco-bertolotti (co-author on 0b05cc9). AI assistance (Claude) was used.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSA] Honor skip_kv_gather in the ROCm sparse-indexer prefill loop
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, the DSA sparse-indexer prefill loop (`rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer`) re-gathers the full indexer K cache for every query sub-chunk of a long request. The metadata builder already marks those continuation sub-chunks `skip_kv_gather=True` and the CUDA path (`sparse_attn_indexer.py`) honors it; this PR adds the same guard to the ROCm loop.

Prior attempts: #46478 and #40049 (both closed unmerged as stale; motivated by #40018). This PR adds the MI300X measurements those lacked.

## Claims

- Removes the redundant per-sub-chunk K gather on ROCm. The logits are unchanged: the skipped gather would write the same rows into the same workspace slice, and nothing writes that slice in between.
- GLM-5.3-FP8 on MI300X (gfx942), warm 512K-context prefill at the default `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=512`: TTFT **39.2 / 39.8 s → 36.3 / 37.2 s** on a `main` nightly (−7%). In-server K-gather time per request **2.8 s → 0.12 s**. With a 64 MB budget (more sub-chunks), TTFT **70.1 s → 52.2 s**.

## Validation

**Setup.** GLM-5.3-FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, DSA indexer on 21 of 78 layers). 1P1D PD disaggregation on 2× 8×MI300X, DP8/EP8 prefill + DP8/EP8 decode, MoRIIO WRITE, prefix caching on, AITER + FlyDSL `fp8_mqa_logits`.

**Workload.** A single request (c1) through the PD proxy, streaming. "Warm 512K" means a 457.5K-token cached prefix plus 65.6K new tokens, so 523K total. The same prompts are used in every arm. Two reps per arm.

**On `main`.** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly built from `00b6c4c565` (HIP 7.15, AITER 0.1.26); `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` there is byte-identical to this PR's base. "With guard" is the same image with this PR's file copied in. That image also carried the files of #63879 and #63880, which only touch the MoRIIO connector.

| | Gate (chat + completion, c1 + 2× c8) | Warm 512K TTFT (2 reps) | Cold 457K-prefix TTFT (2 reps) | Prefix hit | Needle in the 523K prompt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nightly | pass | 39.20 / 39.78 s | 193.2 / 188.5 s | 0.874 | pass / pass |
| Nightly + this PR | pass | **36.30 / 37.16 s** | 187.8 / 185.2 s | 0.875 | pass / pass |

**On v0.32.0** (the guard applied as a runtime patch to the same function), including the smaller logits budget:

| `MAX_LOGITS_MB` | Without guard (TTFT, 2 reps) | With guard (TTFT, 2 reps) |
|---|---|---|
| 512 (default) | 39.52 / 39.57 s | **37.13 / 37.92 s** |
| 64 | 70.13 / 70.17 s | **52.17 / 52.71 s** |

In-server indexer time per warm-512K request at 512 MB on v0.32.0, from CUDA-event timers around each stage summed over indexer layers:

| | Logits | Top-k | K gather | Indexer total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Without guard | 10.4–10.5 s | 2.9 s | **2.8 s** | 16.2 s |
| With guard | 10.4 s | 3.1 s | **0.12 s** | 13.6 s |

**Correctness with the guard (v0.32.0).**
- NIAH at 256K (261,586 tokens) and 512K (523,205 tokens), depths 0.1/0.5/0.9: 3/3 at each length.
- 8 concurrent distinct 64K needles × 2 rounds: 16/16.
- Coherence gate (chat + completion at c1 and c8): pass.

**Unit tests.** There is no new unit test. This is a performance-only change, and the output is identical with or without the guard, so no output assertion can fail without the fix. The existing ROCm sparse-MLA kernel tests cover the loop's numerics.

<details>
<summary>Why the gather repeats</summary>

`_split_indexer_prefill_chunks` bounds the logits buffer: at depth N, one sub-chunk holds about `MAX_LOGITS_MB / (4·N)` query rows. For one 8192-token prefill step at 491K depth, that is 31 sub-chunks at 512 MB and 241 at 64 MB. All sub-chunks of a request use the same `block_table` / `cu_seq_lens`. `build_prefill_chunk_metadata` sets `skip_kv_gather = query_slice.start > 0` for every sub-chunk after the first. The ROCm loop ignored the flag, so each of those sub-chunks ran `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` over the full K range again.
</details>

## Details

- The change is the same `skip_kv_gather` guard used by `sparse_attn_indexer.py` (CUDA) and `models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`. ROCm has no PCP/DCP-local extents, so there is no `local_total_seq_lens` check. Chunks with `total_seq_lens == 0` are already dropped by the builder.
- There is no new host/device synchronization; the change only skips a kernel launch, based on host-side metadata.
- **CI coverage gap:** CI does not run a long-context DSA prefill on ROCm. The numbers above were measured outside CI on MI300X.
- Not part of this PR: #63038 changes chunk budgeting for CUDA only and does not touch this loop.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Apply the layer q_scale only to FP8 queries in FlashInfer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63043.

When the query that reaches FlashInfer is BF16/FP16, `FlashInferImpl.forward` still passed the layer's FP8 query scale (`layer._q_scale_float`) to the kernel. FlashInfer multiplies the softmax scale by it, so with a checkpoint that has a non-unit `q_scale` the attention output is wrong. This PR adds `FlashInferImpl.get_q_scale(layer, q_data_type)`. It returns the layer's q scale only for an FP8 query and 1.0 for any other dtype. Every place where the backend hands a q scale to FlashInfer now uses it.

Compared with #53754, this fix:

- No activity in #53754 for 2 months
- Also applies the rule to the cached `self.bmm1_scale`, which trtllm-gen decode and TRTLLM prefill read on SM100. With #53754's change on B200 and `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization`, the end-to-end checkpoint test below still gives garbage text, and the two TRTLLM rows of `test_flashinfer_bf16_query_ignores_q_scale` still fail.
- Has tests that go through the real `FlashInferImpl.forward`. The test in #53754 only calls the new helper. It still passes 4/4 when the helper is added but `forward` keeps the bug.

## Claims

- With a non-unit checkpoint `q_scale` and a query that is not FP8, FlashInfer no longer descales the query. This fixes native prefill, sink prefill, native decode, DCP native decode and trtllm-gen decode.
- An FP8 query still gets the layer's q scale on every path. `get_xqa_bmm1_scale` returns the same values as before.
- Two related defects are not fixed here (see Details).

## Validation

Reproducer (from the issue): a CPU check, with no server and no model. It builds random BF16 Q and FP8 K/V and calls the real `FlashInferImpl.forward`. Only the FlashInfer GPU wrapper is replaced by a CPU stand-in. The stand-in records the `q_scale` it receives and computes attention with it. `error` is the max abs difference from an FP32 reference. The `stored_q_scale=1.0` case is the control.

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' python3 repro.py
```

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""CPU-only argument-boundary repro; the GPU wrapper is a numerical stand-in."""

import os

os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = ""

from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import vllm.v1.attention.backends.flashinfer as backend


def main():
    torch.set_num_threads(1)
    generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(7)
    n, heads, dim = 16, 2, 64
    sm_scale, kv_scale = dim**-0.5, 0.125
    q, k, v = [
        torch.randn(n, heads, dim, generator=generator).to(torch.bfloat16)
        for _ in range(3)
    ]
    k8, v8 = [(x.float() / kv_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) for x in (k, v)]
    cache = torch.cat((k8, v8), dim=-1).transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0)
    kh, vh = [x.float().transpose(0, 1) * kv_scale for x in (k8, v8)]
    scores = (q.float().transpose(0, 1) @ kh.transpose(-1, -2)) * sm_scale
    scores.masked_fill_(torch.ones(n, n, dtype=torch.bool).triu(1), -torch.inf)
    expected = (scores.softmax(-1) @ vh).transpose(0, 1)
    selected = []

    class CPUPrefill:
        _window_left, _logits_soft_cap = -1, 0.0
        _sm_scale, _causal = sm_scale, True

        def run(self, query, kv, *, q_scale, k_scale, v_scale, out, **kwargs):
            selected.append(q_scale)
            result = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
                query.float().transpose(0, 1),
                kv[0][0].float() * k_scale,
                kv[1][0].float() * v_scale,
                is_causal=True,
                scale=sm_scale * q_scale,
            )
            return out.copy_(result.transpose(0, 1))

    for stored_q_scale in (1.0, 0.25):
        impl = object.__new__(backend.FlashInferImpl)
        impl.__dict__.update(
            bmm1_scale=None,
            bmm2_scale=None,
            scale=sm_scale,
            kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
            is_kvcache_nvfp4=False,
            nvfp4_fa2=False,
            nvfp4_trtllm=False,
            dcp_world_size=1,
            head_size=dim,
            num_kv_heads=heads,
            window_left=-1,
            logits_soft_cap=0.0,
        )
        layer = SimpleNamespace(
            _q_scale=torch.tensor(stored_q_scale),
            _q_scale_float=stored_q_scale,
            _k_scale_float=kv_scale,
            _v_scale_float=kv_scale,
        )
        metadata = SimpleNamespace(
            prefill=backend.FIPrefill(CPUPrefill()),
            decode=None,
            kv_cache_layout=backend.KVCacheLayout.LBHNC,
            num_actual_tokens=n,
            num_decode_tokens=0,
            num_prefill_tokens=n,
            q_data_type_prefill=q.dtype,
            causal=True,
        )
        out = torch.empty_like(q)
        with patch.object(backend, "BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper", CPUPrefill):
            impl.forward(layer, q, k, v, cache, metadata, out)
        error = (out.float() - expected).abs().max().item()
        print(
            f"stored_q_scale={stored_q_scale}: passed={selected[-1]}, error={error:.6f}"
        )
        assert not torch.cuda.is_initialized()
        assert selected[-1] == 1.0, "BF16 Q must not receive FP8 query descaling"
        assert error < 0.01


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

It ran on a machine with 1 x B200, but the script hides the GPU, so the check runs on CPU.

Before, on base commit `5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`: 3 of 3 runs gave identical output. The `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit (`0.32.1rc1.dev602+g5d35ce393`) also gave it in 3 of 3 runs:

```
stored_q_scale=1.0: passed=1.0, error=0.006877
stored_q_scale=0.25: passed=0.25, error=1.234021
```

The script then stops with `AssertionError: BF16 Q must not receive FP8 query descaling` (exit code 1).

After, with this PR: 6 of 6 runs passed with exit code 0. I ran 3 on the final tree, and an independent re-check ran 3 more:

```
stored_q_scale=1.0: passed=1.0, error=0.006877
stored_q_scale=0.25: passed=1.0, error=0.006877
```

Tests on 1 x B200:

 | Command | Base `5d35ce39` | This PR |
 |---|---|---|
 | `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k 'q_scale or xqa_bmm1'` | 8 failed, 3 passed | 11 passed |
 | `pytest tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_flashinfer_bf16_query_with_checkpoint_q_scale` | 1 failed (Triton `'\n2. Open'`, FlashInfer `', , '`) | 1 passed |
 | `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_trtllm_attention_integration.py` | not run | 173 passed, 9 skipped |

- The changed call sites were reverted to the old code one at a time: sink prefill + DCP decode, cached `bmm1_scale`, native prefill, native decode. Each revert alone makes at least one of the `q_scale` rows fail.
- A wider run of five attention test files (`test_attention_backends.py`, `test_trtllm_attention_integration.py`, `test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py`, `test_mm_prefix.py`, `test_kv_head_stride_canonicalization.py`) gave 212 passed, 16 skipped. `tests/kernels/test_fused_muse_spark_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, which feeds an already-quantized FP8 query into `FlashInferImpl`, gave 29 passed, 2 skipped (ROCm).
- The skips need other hardware: SM90/SM12x (sinks, XQA), SM8x/SM12x (NVFP4 fa2), GPUs before SM90 (fa2 spec decode), ROCm.
- pre-commit passes on the three changed files.

Not run:

- Nothing ran on SM90 (H100/H200). There, `test_flashinfer_bf16_query_ignores_q_scale` goes down native prefill and XQA decode.
- The real sink prefill and DCP decode kernels did not run, because they need SM90/SM12x or more than one GPU. The mock test only checks the scale that vLLM hands to the wrapper.
- The serving check with the model from the issue did not run.

## Details

Root cause: FlashInfer's `q_scale` is the dequantization scale of an FP8 query ("The calibration scale of query for fp8 input"). FlashInfer multiplies the softmax scale by it and does not check the query dtype. The sink prefill wrapper and the TRTLLM kernels take the same factor folded into `sm_scale` / `bmm1_scale`. vLLM quantizes the query with `layer._q_scale` only when the query that reaches the kernel is FP8 (in `maybe_quant_query`, or earlier in the layer's `query_quant`). But `forward` applied `layer._q_scale_float` at every native call (except NVFP4 fa2) and in the cached `self.bmm1_scale`. `layer._q_scale_float` comes from the checkpoint and is set even when the KV cache is not quantized. The query stays BF16/FP16 in these cases:

- an FP8 KV cache on fa2-only GPUs (SM8x, SM12x);
- an FP8 KV cache with `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization`, on any GPU;
- SM90 native decode;
- an unquantized KV cache.

With a real checkpoint (q scale about 0.03), the output is garbage. With `q_scale == 1.0`, the bug is hidden.

Fix:

- The XQA decode path already had the right rule, in `get_xqa_bmm1_scale`. The rule moves into `get_q_scale`, and `get_xqa_bmm1_scale` now calls it.
- Each of the four native calls passes the dtype of the query tensor it hands to the kernel.
- The cached `self.bmm1_scale` uses `attn_metadata.q_data_type_prefill`. Only SM100 reads it (TRTLLM prefill, trtllm-gen decode), and there prefill and decode use the same query dtype.
- The `1.0 if self.nvfp4_fa2` special case is dropped. The fa2 NVFP4 query stays in the model dtype, so the dtype rule already gives 1.0.
- Not chosen: setting `layer._q_scale_float` to 1.0 when the query is not quantized. On SM90/SM12x one layer runs an FP8 prefill query and a BF16 decode query, so one value per layer cannot be right for both.

Tests:

- `test_flashinfer_bf16_query_ignores_q_scale`: real kernels, q scale 0.25, `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization=True`. Its 6 rows cover FP8 or unquantized KV, native or TRTLLM, and prefill or decode.
- `test_flashinfer_sink_prefill_and_dcp_decode_q_scale`: runs the real `forward` with a `Mock(spec=...)` wrapper that records the scale, because the real kernels need SM90/SM12x (sinks) or several GPUs (DCP). BF16 rows expect 1.0, and FP8 rows expect 0.25.
- `test_flashinfer_bf16_query_with_checkpoint_q_scale`: uses `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-kvcache-fp8-tensor` (per-layer q scale about 0.03) with FP8 KV. It compares FlashInfer greedy logprobs (with `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization`) against Triton.
- The test helpers get `q_scale` / `layer_q_scale` / `attention_config` arguments. The defaults keep the old behaviour. When the backend takes an FP8 query, the helper now quantizes `query / layer_q_scale`. With the default 1.0, this gives the same values as before.
- The backend tests are in `tests/v1/attention`, which the `V1 Attention` Buildkite step already runs.

Not fixed here (each needs a separate change):

- TRTLLM prefill with a BF16 query over an FP8 KV cache (SM100, `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization=True`) still applies the k/v scales twice. This PR removes the wrong q-scale factor there, but that path is still wrong when `k_scale != 1`.
- DCP prefill (`BatchDCPPrefillWrapper.run`) passes no q scale at all, so an FP8 query there is never descaled.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Pin the AMD monokernel steps to explicit test files
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Two **blocking** AMD monokernel steps select a whole directory rather than naming their test files:

| Step | Agent | Timeout | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minimax-m3-monokernel-mi355` | mi355_4 | 45 min | `pytest -v -s models/minimax_m3/amd_specialized_decode` |
| `kimi-k3-specialized-decode-amd` | mi355_8 | 60 min | `pytest -v -s tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode` |

`tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py` treats a directory selection as covering everything beneath it (`_path_is_within`: `path == parent or path.startswith(parent + "/")`). So a new file dropped into either directory joins a blocking multi-GPU step the moment it merges, and the hook stays silent because the directory already "covers" it. Nobody reviewing the test has to notice they just added 20 minutes to every PR's critical path on an 8-GPU agent.

Naming the files inverts that: adding a test to a blocking step becomes a visible line in the diff, and the hook *refuses* a commit that adds a test file without placing it.

The hook reads **every** pipeline yaml, legacy `test-amd.yaml` included (`_pipeline_yaml_paths()` appends it), and one directory selection anywhere is enough to keep it quiet. So the legacy AMD steps are pinned too. Dropping a probe file into both directories:

| | result |
|---|---|
| only `test_areas/` pinned | exit 0, silent |
| legacy pinned as well | exit 1, both flagged |

This is groundwork for the AMD monokernel test work in #63486, which adds several large files to exactly these directories. Landing it separately keeps that review about the tests.

## Changes

**`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`**

1. The two blocking steps above name their test files.
2. `:nvidia: (4xB200) Kimi K3` and its `:amd: (MI355) Kimi K3` mirror gain `--ignore=models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode`, so the directory is collected by the one step that can actually run it.

**`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`** (second commit) - the same treatment, so the hook is not defeated from there:

3. `:amd: (MI355) MiniMax M3 Specialized Decode` names its three files, and its `--optional -m optional` stress pins to `test_ops.py`, the one `pytest.mark.optional` in the directory (line 697).
4. `:amd: (MI355) Kimi K3` and `:amd: (MI355) Kimi K3 Multi-GPU` gain the same `--ignore`.

All three legacy steps are `optional: true`, so no blocking cost moves. Only `commands` strings change; no step, schema key or dependency is touched.

(2) and (4) follow the precedent already in `kernels.yaml`:

```yaml
- pytest -v -s models/minimax_m3 --ignore=models/minimax_m3/amd_specialized_decode
```

**No test file is touched.** `source_file_dependencies` is deliberately left directory-shaped: the tethering checker reads a step's `commands`, not its deps, and the directory dep is what makes an added file still *trigger* the step.

## No coverage is lost

Everything below was measured on an 8x gfx950 (MI355X) box in `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1ca0c`. The image's `/vllm-workspace/tests` is byte-identical to this PR's base for both directories, and this PR changes no test, so the two arms differ only in the command line.

**The de-globbed steps collect the same set.**

| Step | Globbed | Explicit | `diff` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kimi-k3-specialized-decode-amd` | 272 items | 272 items | identical |
| `minimax-m3-monokernel-mi355` | 65 items | 65 items | identical |
| legacy MiniMax, 3 files | 65 items | 65 items | identical |
| legacy MiniMax, `--optional -m optional` | 1 item | 1 item | `test_ops.py:697` |

**The `--ignore` removes exactly the intended directory.**

Identical in both files, since both generic Kimi jobs select the same directory:

```
before: 952 items    after: 680 items     (difference = 272, the whole directory)

removed, by file:
      2  tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_engine_fault.py
    133  tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_numerics.py
    137  tests/models/kimi_k3/amd_specialized_decode/test_runtime.py

removed outside amd_specialized_decode:  none
added:                                   none
```

**The dedicated step is a strict superset of what the generic one runs.** This is the part worth checking, because `test_runtime.py` has no ROCm guard and so really does execute on the generic agents today. Same 272 items, two geometries:

| GPUs | Passed | Skipped | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (the generic step's geometry) | 250 | 22 | 4:25 |
| 8 (the dedicated step's geometry) | 256 | 16 | 18:30 |

```
1 GPU : 16 x the nacc = 1 case
         6 x Need at least 8 GPUs to run the test.
8 GPU : 16 x the nacc = 1 case
```

`nacc = 1` is a degenerate-parametrization guard, not a hardware gate, so it is the same on both. The 8-GPU skip set is therefore a strict subset of the 1-GPU one, and since both arms collect the identical 272 items, the 8-GPU run's passes strictly contain the 1-GPU run's — by exactly the 6 multi-GPU items.

On B200 the margin is wider still: all 10 `test_numerics.py` tests and the `test_engine_fault.py` test carry `needs_gfx950`, whose helper returns `False` unless `current_platform.is_rocm()`, leaving only `test_runtime.py` — a subset of the 250 above.

The legacy `Kimi K3 Multi-GPU` job (mi355_4) drops 6 collected items, `15/952 → 9/680` under `-m distributed`. Every `@multi_gpu_test` in that directory asks for 8 GPUs, so four could never run them; they are the same 6 the mi355_8 step runs. No selection goes empty, so no step can exit 5.

## Test plan

Both blocking steps were run on MI355X with their new commands, from the `working_dir` each declares:

```
kimi-k3-specialized-decode-amd  (8 GPU)   256 passed, 16 skipped   18:30
minimax-m3-monokernel-mi355     (4 GPU)    64 passed,  1 skipped    6:46
```

The MiniMax skip is `test_ops.py:697 need --optional option to run`, which is pre-existing.

The generic Kimi steps were not run in full: the change there is a pure removal, and the collection diff above already shows precisely what it removes.

Also clean: `yaml.safe_load` over every `.buildkite/test_areas/*.yaml`, and `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`.

The probe in the table above is the direct check that the guard now works: `echo "def test_x(): pass" > tests/models/<model>/amd_specialized_decode/test_zzz_probe.py`, then run the hook on it.

`check_test_tethering.py --all` is unchanged by this PR. Note it does not exit 0 on main either way — it reports two stale allowlist entries (`tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py`, `tests/distributed/test_pipeline_partition.py`) that predate this change and are left alone to keep the diff to one concern.

---

commits.pr_title: [Docs][ROCm] Add AMD verified ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview recipe
commits.pr_body:
Marks `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview` as verified on 1x MI355X with the BF16 checkpoint. 

- `meta.default_variant: {amd: bf16}`. The default NVFP4 checkpoint runs on ROCm only through `EmulationNvFp4LinearKernel`, which is slower than BF16 (see below).
- `spec_decoding` AMD override: the same DFlash2 config plus `--max-model-len 1048576`. With BF16 weights on one GPU, the drafter's KV cache does not fit at 2M (168.8 GiB needed, 151.5 GiB available, estimated maximum 1,869,840).
- New "AMD (1x MI355X, BF16)" guide section with the `docker run` line.

## Validation

1x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (0.33.0rc1.dev1065+g083fbac02), `ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview` (BF16), TP1, default `ROCM_ATTN` attention.

- Chat, `--reasoning-parser ripple` (reasoning in `reasoning_content`, no `<think>` leak) and `--tool-call-parser ripple` (tool call, tool-result round trip, streamed tool call) all pass, with and without DFlash2.
- Full 2,097,152-token context loads. The needle passed at 131K, 524K and 1M prompt tokens.
- AIME25, 30 problems × 4 samples, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, 64K max tokens, BF16 + DFlash2: **97.5%** (117/120; per sample 29/29/29/30) against 98.3 on the card. One response hit the 64K limit. Mean output is 10.4K tokens; the runs finished in about 50 minutes with one sample per GPU.

### DFlash2

Same 8 AIME25 problems, 1 sample each, 8 concurrent:

| | Correct | Output tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | 8/8 | 59 |
| BF16 + DFlash2 (7 tokens) | 8/8 | 221 |

Mean acceptance length is 4.6–4.8 out of 7; per-position acceptance is about 0.85 / 0.69 / 0.56 / 0.49 / 0.42 / 0.35 / 0.31.

### Throughput (1x MI355X, BF16, random data, concurrency 32)

| Config | 1K in / 1K out | 16K in / 1K out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ROCM_ATTN` (default) | 844 tok/s, median TPOT 35 ms | 98 tok/s, median TPOT 285 ms |
| `ROCM_AITER_FA` + `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` | 1,073 tok/s, median TPOT 30 ms | 363 tok/s, median TPOT 82 ms |

`ROCM_AITER_FA` is 3–4× faster at long context, but its workspace grows with `--max-model-len`. At 2M it fails to allocate 79.9 GiB, so it is not in the recipe. It fits at 262,144.

Long-context prefill with `ROCM_ATTN` is slow: the 1M needle prompt took 6,326 s (166 tok/s).

## NVFP4 on ROCm

| Checkpoint path | 1K in / 1K out, concurrency 32 | 8-problem AIME25 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | 844 tok/s | 8/8, 59 tok/s |
| NVFP4, `EmulationNvFp4LinearKernel` | 337 tok/s | 8/8, 42 tok/s |
| NVFP4 MLPs converted to MXFP4 at load time ([#61620](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61620)) | 1,125 tok/s | 8/8 |

This PR does not change the NVFP4 variant. It stays selectable on AMD and runs correctly through emulation, but BF16 is the AMD default because it is 2.5× faster. Faster NVFP4 on ROCm depends on online NVFP4-to-MXFP4 conversion for linear layers ([#61620](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61620), open). Once that lands, a follow-up can add an AMD override with the flag below to the NVFP4 variant, after a confirming accuracy run. With it, `--quantization-config.targets '{"*mlp*": "mxfp4"}'` converts the 160 MLP layers and runs them on `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` (52 GiB of weights). Full AIME25 with this conversion (run with `ROCM_AITER_FA` at a 262K context, no DFlash2) is 94.2% (113/120), 3.3 points below BF16. That is about two standard errors, so a small accuracy cost is possible, but not yet conclusive.

commits.pr_title: [Docs][ROCm] Add AMD verified inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny recipe
commits.pr_body:
Marks `inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-asr-tiny` as verified on 1x MI355X and adds an AMD serve path. 

- AMD override on the default variant: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`. The nightly image already ships torchaudio and torchcodec, so the torchaudio dependency step is not needed.
- `:nightly`, not `:latest`: vLLM 0.33.0 (`:latest`) does not include the Ming model.
- New "AMD (1x MI355X, BF16)" guide section with the `docker run` line, including the n-gram logits processor.

## Validation

1x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (0.33.0rc1.dev1065+g083fbac02), recipe flags, default ROCm backends (`TRITON_MLA`, Triton MoE).

- Every guide example works:
  - The English, Mandarin and Context clips give the transcriptions in the guide. The Context clip with topic and hotwords returns `同囚`, both over the API and with the offline snippet.
  - Streaming, `response_format=text`, `context_chunks` and `audio_chunk_frames` work.
  - Translation, timestamps, and combined chunk options are rejected.
- LibriSpeech, Whisper English normalizer, 10-gram blocking:

  | Set | WER (MI355X) | Card |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | test-clean (2,620) | 1.18% | 1.29% |
  | test-other (2,939) | 2.38% | 2.56% |

- Mandarin: on a 200-utterance AISHELL-1 sample, vLLM transcripts were identical to the official Transformers runtime (`hf_runtime.py`, BF16, SDPA, greedy, `no_repeat_ngram_size=10`). Full-set CER (2.3% AISHELL-1, 7.6% FLEURS zh) is above the card. That comes from our dataset copies and scoring, not from vLLM: the reference runtime fails on the same clips.

## AITER

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is not set. It selects `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, AITER FA (audio encoder and MLA prefill) and AITER MoE; all of them run correctly, but there is no gain. Error rates are the same. Throughput is the same for a single stream and lower under load (AISHELL-1 clips/s, sequential runs on one GPU):

| Concurrency | Default | AITER |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 15.3 | 15.3 |
| 32 | 52.3 | 42.5 |
| 128 | 74.9 | 54.9 |

Disabling AITER MoE, MLA, MHA or linear one at a time did not recover the default throughput (40–50 clips/s at concurrency 128), so the slowdown is spread across components.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix reshape & cache dropping KV heads past 512 chunks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`reshape_and_cache` leaves KV heads unwritten when a token has more than 512 16-byte chunks, so `ROCM_ATTN` silently reads stale KV cache data for shapes such as 32 KV heads × head size 192/256 in bf16. This restores a thread-stride loop in the kernel and adds a regression test. It fixes Pattern B of #62697. Pattern A (decode reads at block size 528 on gfx1201) is a separate problem and isn't addressed here.

## Claims

- `reshape_and_cache` now writes every KV head for any `num_kv_heads * head_size`. Before, chunks past the 512th per token were skipped whenever `num_kv_heads * head_size * cache_element_size > 8192` bytes.
- With the reporter's script, the three failing Pattern B cases of #62697 now match `TRITON_ATTN` (max error ≤ 0.0006, previously 0.097–0.196).
- No other test outcome changes, and no performance change for shapes that fit within 512 chunks per token (see Validation).

## Testing & Validation

All runs used 1× MI355X (gfx950)
```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k test_reshape_and_cache_many_heads \
    tests/compile/passes/test_rope_kvcache_fusion.py -k ROCM_ATTN \
    tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py 
```
**Reporter's reproducer** (the gist script from #62697, unmodified), `ROCM_ATTN` max error against an fp32 reference:

| Case | Baseline | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `p2-d256-bs16-gqa1` (32/32 heads, head 256, decode) | 0.1935, mismatch | 0.0006 |
| `p2-d192-bs16-gqa1` (32/32 heads, head 192, decode) | 0.1955, mismatch | 0.0006 |
| `p2-d256-bs16-gqa1-prefill` (cached context) | 0.0967, mismatch | 0.0003 |
| `ok-d256-bs16-gqa1-fresh-prefill` | 0.0085, but cache read-back off by up to 5.31 | 0.0085, cache exact |

The other six cases (GQA-4, and the block-528 cases, which use the Triton writer) pass on both builds. A direct check of `ops.reshape_and_cache` on the baseline found exactly the unwritten heads predicted by the root cause below (heads 16–31 for 32 × 256; heads 21–31 for 32 × 192, with head 21 partly written), and none with the fix.

**Performance.** `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_reshape_and_cache.py --dtype bfloat16 --block-size 16 --mode cudagraph --iters 200`, sweeping 2 to 65,536 tokens. Each config ran 3 rounds with baseline and fix alternating; numbers are medians.

| KV heads × head size, cache | Chunks/token | Work completed by baseline | Fix/base, all sizes | Fix/base, ≥1024 tokens | Baseline spread |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 × 128, auto | 128 | 100% | 1.004× | 0.997× | 0.4–20.1% |
| 8 × 256, auto | 256 | 100% | 1.005× | 1.001× | 0.3–17.8% |
| 32 × 128, auto | 512 | 100% | 1.001× | 0.996× | 0.3–17.8% |
| 32 × 256, fp8 | 512 | 100% | 0.984× | 0.969× | 0.4–18.9% |
| 32 × 256, auto | 1024 | 50% | 1.604× | 2.260× | 0.2–17.8% |
| 64 × 256, fp8 | 1024 | 50% | 1.650× | 2.169× | 0.3–16.9% |
| 128 × 128, auto | 2048 | 25% | 2.693× | 4.487× | 0.3–15.4% |

For shapes within 512 chunks, the loop executes once and performance is unchanged (0.969–1.001× for ≥1024 tokens). For shapes over 512 chunks, raw latency is not an equivalent-work comparison: the baseline skipped half or three quarters of the writes. Normalized by bytes actually written, the fixed kernel retains 88.5%, 92.2%, and 89.1% of the broken baseline's partial-write throughput for the three over-limit configurations at ≥1024 tokens.

### GSM8K Test 

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, on one MI355X, `main` at dd4e40142a:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen1.5-14B-Chat --attention-backend <backend> --block-size 16 --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0
```

| Backend | Code | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| ROCM_ATTN | main | 0.411 |
| TRITON_ATTN | main (reference) | 0.688 |
| ROCM_ATTN | this PR | 0.691 |

Most current models use GQA with 8 KV heads, so they stay far under the limit (8 × 128 bf16 is 128 chunks). This affects models whose KV heads × head size per GPU exceeds 4096 elements in bf16, such as 13B+ multi-head models (Qwen1.5-14B, Llama-2-13B, OLMo-2-13B) at TP=1, or MHA models with head size 192/256. On MI300/MI355 it only shows up when `ROCM_ATTN` is selected explicitly. On RDNA it's the default backend.

## Details

**Root cause.** #25955 replaced the kernel's thread-stride loop over all elements with one thread per (KV head, 16-byte chunk) pair, but kept the launch cap of `dim3 block(std::min(num_heads * head_div_x, 512))`. When `num_heads * head_size / x > 512` (`x = 16 / cache element size`, so 8 for fp16/bf16 and 16 for fp8), the extra chunks get no thread. For example, with bf16 and 32 KV heads, head size 256 means 1024 chunks, so heads 16–31 are never written. Head size 192 means 768 chunks, so head 21 is partly written and heads 22–31 not at all. The unwritten slots keep whatever the cache block held before, so the outputs are silently wrong rather than crashing. `test_reshape_and_cache` only uses `NUM_HEADS = [8]` (at most 256 chunks), so CI never hit the limit.

**Fix.** The per-chunk body is wrapped in `for (h_block_idx = threadIdx.x; h_block_idx < num_heads * h_block_count; h_block_idx += blockDim.x)`, and the scale setup moves above the loop. `reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` already strides by `blockDim.x` in the same way. The launch configuration is unchanged. Most of the diff is re-indentation, so view it with whitespace hidden (10 lines changed).

This keeps one block per token, preserving the current launch behavior and avoiding repeated token metadata and scale loads. A 2D launch with multiple blocks per token could expose more parallelism for over-limit shapes, but would add scheduling overhead and needs tuning across token counts and GPU architectures. The strided loop is the minimal correctness fix; a multi-block layout can be evaluated separately as a performance optimization.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used for the root-cause analysis, the patch, the test and the validation scripts. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Keep unquantized routed experts unquantized under AutoGPTQ
commits.pr_body:
# Issue #49141 — Fused_moe dimension mismatch for Qwen MXFP4 model on ROCm

## 1. Root cause

The issue has two reports. Both are the same underlying defect: **a MoE layer whose
expert weights are stored *unquantized* in the checkpoint is still given a
*quantized* MoE method**, so the allocated parameters do not match the checkpoint
tensors.

The trigger in both cases is the MTP (speculative-decoding drafter) layer. AMD's
Quark and community GPTQ quantizations of `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` quantize the 40
transformer layers but leave the MTP layer's experts in bf16. The main model
loads fine; only the drafter fails.

* **Original MXFP4/Quark report** (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must
  match the size of tensor b (512) at non-singleton dimension 1`, in
  `routed_experts.py::_load_w2`).
  `hidden_size=2048`, `moe_intermediate_size=512`. Quark MXFP4 allocates
  `w2_weight` as `(E, hidden, intermediate // 2)` = `(E, 2048, 256)` (fp4 packs
  two values per byte), while the checkpoint's MTP `down_proj.weight` is the
  unquantized `(2048, 512)`. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`'s
  `quantization_config.exclude` lists `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.<i>.{gate,up,down}_proj`
  for all 256 experts, but `should_ignore_layer()` only compared the *parent*
  layer name `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts` against those *child* entries.
  **This half is already fixed on main** by the `check_children` argument added
  to `quark/utils.py::should_ignore_layer` (the amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 fix), which is
  why a commenter on the issue could not reproduce it on main. No change needed.

* **Still-broken GPTQ report** (issue comments:
  `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_weight'. Did you
  mean: 'w2_qweight'?`, same drafter-loading path).
  `AutoGPTQConfig` tracks which modules the checkpoint actually quantized in
  `modules_in_block_to_quantize` — auto-derived in `maybe_update_config()` from
  the safetensors dtypes, so it contains only the quantized layers' per-expert
  module names. `get_linear_quant_method()` consults it via
  `is_layer_gptq_quantized()`, but the `RoutedExperts` branch of
  `AutoGPTQConfig.get_quant_method()` **never consulted it at all** — neither on
  the Marlin path nor on the `MoeWNA16Config` fallback path taken here. The MTP
  layer therefore got a WNA16 MoE method allocating `w13_qweight`/`w2_qweight`,
  while the checkpoint supplies `...down_proj.weight`, and
  `RoutedExperts.load_weights()`'s `getattr(self, "w2_weight")` raised.

## 2. The fix and why

Consult `modules_in_block_to_quantize` for routed-expert layers, the same way it
is already consulted for linear layers.

* New `is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized(prefix, quantized_layers)` in
  `gptq_utils.py`. `prefix` is the fused layer (`...mlp.experts`) while the
  config lists individual expert projections (`...mlp.experts.0.down_proj`), so
  a plain substring test in either direction is wrong. The helper normalizes
  each entry to its `...experts` parent and matches that as a suffix of
  `prefix`, which works for both absolute names (the auto-derived case) and the
  block-relative names optimum writes.
* Called from `AutoGPTQConfig.get_quant_method()` *before* the Marlin-support
  check, so both the Marlin path and the `MoeWNA16Config` fallback are covered
  by the single early `return UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod(layer.moe_config)`.

Deliberately conservative: when the config enumerates no expert module at all it
carries no information about experts, so the helper returns `True` and behaviour
is byte-for-byte unchanged for every config shape that does not list experts.

## 3. Files changed

* `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/gptq_utils.py` — add
  `is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized()`.
* `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/auto_gptq.py` — import it and use it
  in the `RoutedExperts` branch of `get_quant_method()`.
* `tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py` — add
  `test_moe_layer_quantized_only_when_its_experts_are_in_the_checkpoint`.

## 4. Risk / uncertainty

* The behaviour change is gated on `modules_in_block_to_quantize` containing at
  least one `...experts...` entry. Fully-quantized MoE GPTQ checkpoints list
  every layer's experts, so they keep the quantized method. The residual risk is
  a checkpoint that lists experts for *some* layers under a naming scheme where
  the `...experts` suffix does not line up with the vLLM module prefix; that
  layer would silently fall back to unquantized (loud failure on the following
  weight load rather than silent wrong numerics, since the parameter names would
  then mismatch).
* Block-relative configs (`mlp.experts.0.down_proj`) still cannot distinguish
  the MTP layer from the main layers, so the fix does not help there. That is
  the pre-existing behaviour, asserted in the test so the limitation is explicit.
* I could not obtain the exact GPTQ checkpoint the reporter used, so the shape of
  its `modules_in_block_to_quantize` is inferred from `maybe_update_config()`'s
  derivation logic plus the `w2_weight`-vs-`w2_qweight` error, not observed.
* Not touched: the Quark/MXFP4 path (already fixed on main) and the AWQ path,
  which uses a different exclusion mechanism (`modules_to_not_convert`).

## 5. How I verified it

* **Root cause**, traced from the traceback through `routed_experts.py`
  (`_load_w2`, `weight_loader`, `build_expert_params_mapping`),
  `quark/quark_moe.py::create_weights` (`get_packed_dim`), `quark/utils.py`,
  `auto_gptq.py`, `moe_wna16.py` and `gptq_utils.py`, cross-checked against
  `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/config.json` (`hidden_size=2048`,
  `moe_intermediate_size=512` — exactly the 2048×256 vs 2048×512 mismatch) and
  `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4/config.json` (the `mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.*`
  exclude entries).
* **Confirmed the MXFP4 half is already fixed** by diffing
  `quark/utils.py::should_ignore_layer` at the reporter's commit `97c162676`
  (no `check_children`) against `main` (has it), matching the issue comment
  reporting it no longer reproduces.
* **Helper logic**: executed `is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized` in isolation over 8
  cases (main-model layer, MTP layer, block-relative names, no-experts config,
  fused-expert entry, nested `list[list[str]]` form, empty config) — all pass.
* **Lint**: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all three files;
  `py_compile` clean.
* **Not run**: the pytest suite. This environment has no `.venv` and no torch
  installed, so `tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py` could not be executed, and
  no end-to-end load of the affected checkpoints was performed.

## Duplicate check

GitHub search for open PRs referencing `49141` in the body returned
`total_count: 0`. No open PR touches `is_layer_gptq_quantized` /
`get_moe_quant_method`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Enable FlashInfer mm-prefix attention
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This keeps multimodal PrefixLM batches on the native FlashInfer backend. It is the vLLM adapter for FlashInfer's mm-prefix batch-prefill wrapper: it builds per-query `[start, end]` rows from request metadata, decides when the path is eligible, and calls the wrapper, whose attention variant evaluates `(causal AND sliding_window) OR mm_prefix` on every KV tile. No `O(qo_len * kv_len)` mask is materialized; the ranges are one `int32 (N, 2)` buffer sized by scheduled tokens, 128 KiB at 16384 tokens. The prefill still traverses the full rectangle, so the gain is memory, not FLOPs.

The wrapper comes from [FlashInfer #5189](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5189) and has shipped since 0.7.1, so main's pin already has it. FlashInfer builds the variant's JIT module when the wrapper is constructed.

The mm-prefix wrapper is planned beside the regular prefill path rather than replacing it, so text-only batches, decodes and layers whose ranges are cleared at forward time (Gemma 4 full-attention groups) keep trtllm-gen or FA3 with main's query dtype and scales. On the SM100 family `TRITON_FLASHINFER` stays the automatic choice; an explicitly selected `FLASHINFER` serves the ranges natively and does not advertise large pages. An SM100 NVFP4 cache keeps its V scale factors in the trtllm-gen swizzle, so native mm-prefix accepts it only when FlashInfer's wrapper takes `v_sf_swizzled` and rejects it otherwise. That option comes from [FlashInfer #7012](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/7012), which shipped in FlashInfer 0.7.3, the version main has pinned since #65930. One predicate, `_native_mm_prefix`, decides eligibility for selection and the builder's range state, so the composite's FlashInfer child keeps main's routing and allocates no range buffers. On SM90 the automatic priority still prefers the `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` composite; this PR leaves that priority unchanged, while native FlashInfer can be selected explicitly. For native mm-prefix, FlashInfer rejects `fp8_e5m2`, `nvfp4_4over6`, sinks and DCP at selection, and `logits_soft_cap` at engine start.

An `fp8` or `fp8_e4m3` cache takes the native path too. fa2 has no FP8 query or output, so only the mm-prefix call adapts: a query the layer already quantized to FP8 goes back to the model dtype losslessly with its q_scale, and a fused FP8 output is quantized after the call. Native mm-prefix models are offered FP8 output fusion only, as the composite is.

#47118 also enables FlashInfer for Gemma 4 multimodal models, but only for text-only requests; this PR serves the mm-prefix batches.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_splitting.py -rs
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k "mm_prefix or composite or hopper" -rs
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py -rs
```

## Test Result

On sm_80 with FlashInfer 0.7.2, the first command gives 24 passed and 22 skipped (FA4 mask_mod), the selector tests give 25 passed with the Hopper and Blackwell cases skipped, and the Gemma 3 E2E test passes with both the automatic backend and `FLASHINFER`. The selector tests cover the SM100 automatic composite against an explicit `FLASHINFER` for no-quant and FP8 KV, and an NVFP4 cache with and without `v_sf_swizzled`. Before the review cleanup, code equivalent to `37c1fa3980` also passed GPU tests against a dense float32 reference on sm_80 and sm_103, including an FP8 KV cache; those were replaced by the E2E test in review. pre-commit passes.

On sm_103 with `RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-NVFP4` and an FP8 KV cache, explicit `FLASHINFER` was measured against `TRITON_FLASHINFER` with one run per configuration, with code equivalent to `37c1fa3980`, before the cleanup. Text throughput was 0.2% lower at concurrency 32; image throughput was 0.8% lower at concurrency 1 and 0.5% and 1.6% higher at 32 and 128; ChartQA (500 examples, relaxed accuracy) was 68.2 against 66.8. These numbers describe this run only. The compiler-fused FP8 output path has not been verified on a full model. Gemma 3 4B with an NVFP4 KV cache, which `TRITON_FLASHINFER` rejects on SM100, scored 43.8 on the same ChartQA set against 43.6 with FP8 KV.

<details>
<summary>Historical serving measurements from the earlier in-tree variant</summary>

These results are historical context, not validation of the current wrapper-based adapter. They were measured with the former in-tree variant on a tree that also carried persistent attention-workspace profiling. That profiling code is not part of this PR, and the measurements have not been repeated against this revision.

Run on 2 SM80 devices, `-tp 2`, BF16 weights and KV, a 31B multimodal model, `--max-model-len 8192`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`. FlashInfer carried the mm-prefix batches end to end; a single 896x896 image request completed successfully, and no workspace or KV-cache assertion fired. The same-host comparison against the `TRITON_ATTN` baseline used the image workload definition and seeds from the composite PR's repro block: an 896x896 image plus a configured 1024-token text input and 1024-token output, with multimodal expansion producing 1295-1297 measured input tokens, `--temperature 0 --ignore-eos`, and prefix and mm caches reset between runs. The server configurations differ in attention backend, block size, and available KV capacity, so this compares complete serving configurations rather than isolating the mm-prefix kernel. **This is not a reproduction of that PR's numbers** — different architecture and parallelism, so only the within-host results are meaningful.

Values are `TRITON_ATTN / FLASHINFER`, **bold is better** (higher tok/s, lower latency):

| Conc | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | E2EL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14.2 / **58.5** | 6.3 / **25.8** | 3884 / **2167** | 155.4 / **36.6** | 162860 / **39652** |
| 32 | **437.8** / 426.7 | **193.3** / 188.4 | 31441 / **30559** | **134.9** / 140.1 | **169446** / 173846 |
| 128 | 416.2 / **438.0** | 183.7 / **193.4** | 280114 / **275765** | **186.1** / 190.2 | 470526 / **470314** |

Caveats, so the table is not read for more than it says:

- The concurrency-32 FlashInfer figure is the mean of three seeds (10032/10033/10034: 426.6 / 427.0 / 426.7, spread 0.09%). The `TRITON_ATTN` figure on that row is a **single seed**, so its 2.6% lead carries an unmeasured seed-variance error bar and should not be read as a real difference. Concurrency 1 and 128 are single-seed on both sides.
- At concurrency 32, the measured inputs are 1295-1297 tokens with 1024 output tokens, putting the maximum full-request footprint at approximately 74K tokens, above either KV budget; concurrency 128 is more constrained. Scheduling and cache pressure can therefore affect these rows, and they do not isolate attention-kernel cost.
- The two arms do not get identical KV budgets: FlashInfer reserves its attention workspace during profiling and lands at 49,593 tokens against the baseline's 51,515. The FlashInfer configuration is therefore measured with approximately 3.7% less KV capacity.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Use the SigLIP chat template over the Gemma one for SigLIP2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #66417. SigLIP2 text sent to `/v1/embeddings` as `messages` still gets a different embedding than the same text sent as `input`. The SigLIP2 checkpoints report `model_type: "siglip"` but reuse the Gemma tokenizer, which ships Gemma's chat template. A tokenizer template outranks vLLM's predefined fallbacks, so the text is wrapped in `<start_of_turn>user ... <end_of_turn>` and loses EOS (11 tokens instead of 6 for "a photo of a cat").

This lets selected model types use their predefined template ahead of templates shipped on the Hub, and enables it only for `siglip`, whose `template_siglip.jinja` from #66417 gives the same tokens as the tokenizer. An explicit `--chat-template` still wins.

The NaFlex checkpoints (`model_type: "siglip2"`) ship no chat template, but their fallback was still `template_basic.jinja`, which drops the EOS their tokenizer adds (5 tokens instead of 6). They now use `template_siglip.jinja` too.

Hub-side fix for the template itself: https://huggingface.co/google/siglip2-base-patch16-224/discussions/23

## Validation

- Chat vs. `input` tokens for CLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2 and both NaFlex checkpoints: all identical with the fix; SigLIP2 and NaFlex differ without it
- `test_dual_encoder_chat_text_matches_input` now includes `google/siglip2-base-patch16-224`
- `tests/renderers/test_hf.py`: 73 passed; the 4 failures are the same without the change (gated models, CPU build without Triton)
- `pre-commit` passes

These ran on Mac CPU; the end-to-end test was not run on a GPU and is covered by CI.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the code, tests and this description; the validation runs above were executed locally.
